frameworks.name: GHG Protocol
frameworks.tagline: The world's default corporate carbon accounting rulebook, now being rebuilt jointly with ISO.
frameworks.description: The GHG Protocol sets the accounting rules almost every company uses to add up its emissions, and almost every regulator points to. Since 2024 it has been running a full revision of its corporate suite, and since September 2025 it has been doing that jointly with ISO. As of July 2026 the separate Corporate, Scope 2, Scope 3 and market-instruments revisions have been merged into one consolidated standard co-developed with ISO, aimed at consultation in 2027 and publication in 2028.
frameworks.status_headline: Four separate revisions collapsed into one GHGP-ISO consolidated corporate standard on 29 July 2026: consultation now targeted for Q2 2027 and publication for Q4 2028, so nothing in the corporate suite changes for reporters before then except the Land Sector and Removals Standard, which becomes effective 1 January 2027.

workstreams.name: Consolidated GHGP-ISO Corporate Standard
workstreams.status_label: Drafting; single integrated consultation targeted Q2 2027
workstreams.summary: On 29 July 2026 GHG Protocol published version 2.0 of its Standard Development Plan, merging the previously separate Corporate Standard, Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard and Actions and Market Instruments workstreams, together with ISO 14064-1, into a single co-branded corporate standard. The deliverable is planned as a two-part document: Part 1 covering general requirements and the physical GHG inventory, and Part 2 covering actions and market instruments. One integrated public consultation is estimated for Q2 2027 with publication estimated for Q4 2028.
key_points: Replaces four parallel revision tracks with one document; the four original Standard Development Plans dated 20 December 2024 are superseded.
Two-part structure: Part 1 General Requirements and Physical GHG Inventory; Part 2 Actions and Market Instruments, with separate guidance documents to follow.
Timeline in the plan is explicitly estimated: Q2 2027 consultation, Q4 2028 publication.

Final approval needs both GHG Protocol Independent Standards Board ratification and a two-thirds majority of permanent members of ISO/TC 207/SC 7, and the consultation will incorporate an ISO committee draft review stage.
Until publication, the 2004 Corporate Standard, 2011 Scope 3 Standard and 2015 Scope 2 Guidance remain the standards in force.

confidence.reasoning: The consolidation decision and the two-part structure are set out in an official published Standard Development Plan and press release, but the Q2 2027 and Q4 2028 dates are labelled as estimates in that plan, and a plan that has already been rewritten once in eighteen months could slip again.

workstreams.name: Scope 2 Guidance revision
workstreams.status_label: Consultation closed 31 Jan 2026; proposals being reworked inside the consolidated standard
workstreams.summary: A public consultation on revised Scope 2 accounting ran from 20 October 2025 to 31 January 2026 and drew close to 1,100 responses from 56 countries. The headline proposals were an hourly and geographic matching requirement for market-based claims and a new emission factor hierarchy for the location-based method. GHG Protocol reported on 29 July 2026 that responses diverged sharply on renewable energy accounting and that the technical team is now exploring multiple reporting approaches rather than finalising the consulted text.
key_points: The Independent Standards Board approved the location-based and market-based revisions for consultation on 14 July 2025 by 10 votes to 1 on each.

Consulted market-based proposals included hourly matching (required only for voluntary claims), deliverability/geographic matching, permission to approximate hourly data from load profiles, exemptions for smaller organisations, legacy clauses for long-term contracts, and a multi-year phase-in.
Consultation attracted close to 1,100 responses from 56 countries, with broad support for improving accuracy, comparability and integrity but no consensus on renewable energy accounting.
The separate Scope 2 publication track announced in October 2025 no longer stands: Scope 2 is now a component of the consolidated standard with a Q2 2027 consultation and Q4 2028 publication.
A parallel consultation on electricity-sector consequential accounting ran on the same dates; that work has been moved to the Actions and Market Instruments workstream.

confidence.reasoning: The consultation, its content, its response volume and its absorption into the consolidated standard are all documented on official GHG Protocol pages, but the substantive outcome is genuinely unresolved because GHG Protocol itself says multiple reporting approaches are still being explored.

workstreams.name: Scope 3 Standard revision
workstreams.status_label: Phase 1 proposals published March 2026; no draft text yet, no consultation open
workstreams.summary: GHG Protocol published a Scope 3 Phase 1 Progress Update on 31 March 2026 covering work through end-2025 across 42 Technical Working Group meetings. It sets out proposals in three series: data quality disaggregation and verification disclosure, a prescriptive 95 percent boundary threshold with justification of exclusions, and a narrowing of Category 15 with a new Category 16 for facilitated activities. The document states explicitly that all revisions remain under development and subject to change.
key_points: Series B proposes replacing the current relevance-based screening with a quantitative 95 percent inclusion threshold, requiring companies to quantify total required scope 3 emissions in order to justify any exclusion.
A new Category 16 is proposed for facilitated activities, with Category 15 narrowed to investment-related activities only - a material change for banks, insurers and asset managers.
Series A would require emissions to be disaggregated by data type, require disclosure of verification status, and restrict allocating corporate-level supplier data to non-homogeneous suppliers.
No draft standard text has been released and no Scope 3 consultation is open; the draft will now come through the consolidated standard consultation.
The progress update carries an explicit 'subject to change' caveat and Phase 2 revisions have not yet been published.

confidence.reasoning: The proposals are set out in an official GHG Protocol progress update, but the document itself states that all revisions remain under development and subject to change, so the 95 percent threshold and Category 16 could both be dropped before consultation.

workstreams.name: Actions and Market Instruments (AMI) Standard
workstreams.status_label: RFI closed 31 May 2026; moving to drafting, consultation planned Q3 2027
workstreams.summary: The AMI workstream is building the rules for how companies account for climate actions and purchased market instruments - PPAs, energy attribute certificates, green steel and cement certificates, biomethane, sustainable aviation fuel and carbon credits. Its Phase 1 White Paper, released for a Request for Information on 31 March 2026, proposes a multi-statement reporting structure that separates the physical inventory from market-based accounting and from consequential impact claims. The RFI closed on 31 May 2026 with close to 500 responses and preliminary findings supporting the multi-statement approach.
key_points: The multi-statement structure would separate physical inventory emissions, market-instrument-linked emissions, and GHG impacts of climate actions assessed using consequential methods, plus non-GHG indicators.
This is the single biggest architectural change proposed anywhere in the programme: market-based figures would stop being a variant of the inventory and become a separate statement.

AMI absorbed the electricity-sector consequential accounting work after the Independent Standards Board declined to advance the proposed Marginal Impact Method within Scope 2 in July 2025 (7 against, 4 for).

The AMI Technical Working Group held its second in-person meeting in Amsterdam on 30 June to 2 July 2026 on market-based inventory design, GHG impact assessment, additionality and traceability, and is moving to drafting.

GHG Protocol advises that organisations wishing to adopt a multi-statement approach ahead of finalisation should report physical inventory emissions, market-based emissions and climate action impacts separately and transparently.
AMI becomes Part 2 of the consolidated corporate standard; a formal draft consultation is indicated for Q3 2027.

confidence.reasoning: The white paper, the RFI dates and the multi-statement proposal are all officially published, but the standard is pre-draft and the Q3 2027 consultation date sits later than the Q2 2027 date given for the consolidated standard, which GHG Protocol has not reconciled on any page I could find.

workstreams.name: Land Sector and Removals Standard and Guidance
workstreams.status_label: Published and final; effective 1 January 2027
workstreams.summary: The Land Sector and Removals Standard was published on 30 January 2026 as GHG Protocol's first global standard for corporate accounting of land-sector emissions and CO2 removals. A companion LSR Guidance version 1.0 followed on 30 June 2026, alongside a minor v1.1 update to the Standard, a reporting requirements checklist and sample inventory templates. Both the Standard and the Guidance take effect on 1 January 2027.
key_points: Effective date is 1 January 2027 - this is the only piece of the GHG Protocol revision programme that bites within the next reporting cycle.
Covers land management and land use change, CO2 removals stored in land and geologic carbon pools, and emissions from biogenic products and technological CO2 removal products across supply chains.
Current version of the Standard is v1.1 (June 2026), incorporating minor non-substantive edits made alongside the Guidance; a change summary from v1.0 is published.
The Guidance adds worked examples, equations and calculation guidance plus 10 corporate case studies; it is implementation support, not new requirements.
Companies with agricultural, forestry, food or timber value chains, and any company claiming CO2 removals, are in scope.

confidence.reasoning: Both the Standard and the Guidance are published final documents on ghgprotocol.org with a stated effective date of 1 January 2027.

workstreams.name: Product Standard / joint ISO-GHGP product-level standard
workstreams.status_label: Joint working group formed April 2026; no published timeline

On 27 October 2025 ISO and GHG Protocol announced they would jointly develop a new product-level GHG accounting standard, and on 9 April 2026 they confirmed the Joint Working Group was finalised after more than 450 applications from over 50 countries. The work builds on both ISO 14067 and the existing GHG Protocol Product Standard.

frameworks.name: ISO
frameworks.tagline: The 14060 family of GHG standards, now co-developed with GHG Protocol.
frameworks.description: ISO's 14060 family sets out how organisations, projects and products quantify and verify greenhouse gas emissions, and how those claims get verified. Since September 2025 ISO has been co-developing its corporate GHG standard with GHG Protocol rather than maintaining a parallel one. Separately ISO is finalising a revised carbon neutrality standard and consulting on the first international standard for net zero alignment.
frameworks.status_headline: ISO 14064-1 is being folded into the joint GHGP-ISO corporate standard, ISO 14068 carbon neutrality is at the printer with a September 2026 target, and ISO/DIS 14060 on net zero aligned organizations is out for a 12-week DIS ballot that closes in early September 2026.

workstreams.name: Scope 3 treatment under V2.0
workstreams.status_label: Rewritten: significance-based boundary, alignment pathways, intensity methods removed
workstreams.summary: Scope 3 was the stated reason for the whole revision and is where V2.0 differs most from V1. The fixed percentage coverage threshold is gone, replaced by a significance test on each category; supplier engagement targets become broader supplier and customer alignment pathways; and the economic and physical intensity methods have been withdrawn entirely.
key_points: The V1 fixed-percentage coverage threshold is replaced by a significance-based boundary: cover every scope 3 category that is at least 5% of categories 1-14 emissions.
Named categories (3, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 14) carry specific optional exclusions where a company lacks practical ability to influence the outcome, but every exclusion must be reported and justified.
The economic and physical intensity methods built on ~7% year-on-year intensity reduction were removed for lack of science-based reference pathways.

Supplier engagement targets are expanded into supplier and customer alignment pathways measuring the share of 'in-transition' or 'net-zero aligned' suppliers and customers; new volume, product use and product end-of-life alignment methods are added.
For category 11 (use of sold products) a tightly constrained exception may be sought subject to SBTi approval, conditional on a mandatory long-term target and annual reporting.
Long-term scope 3 targets are now optional for all companies, and scope 3 target-setting as a whole is optional for Category B companies.
Category A companies must identify and quantify emissions-intensive activities (EIAs) and report any that are at least 5% of scope 3 emissions.

confidence.reasoning: Every point is set out in the published V2.0 Main Changes Document and the V2.0 Criteria document.

workstreams.name: Scope 2 and electricity under V2.0
workstreams.status_label: Targets anchored to location-based inventory; market instruments moved to implementation
workstreams.summary: V2.0 separates the ambition of a scope 2 target from the actions used to meet it. Target trajectories are set against the physical, location-based inventory, while energy attribute certificates and PPAs are governed by integrity criteria in the implementation hierarchy. The framing shifts from 'renewable' to 'low-carbon' electricity.
key_points: Scope 2 targets must cover 100% of purchased electricity, heat, steam and cooling and are based only on the location-based (physical) inventory.
Two options: a scope 2 emissions reduction target, or a low-carbon electricity alignment target increasing the share of low-carbon electricity used, contracted or matched.
The scope 2 emissions intensity target option is removed; Category A companies with electricity demand growth above 20% per annum must set emissions reduction targets rather than alignment targets.
Market instrument criteria follow a 'near, new, now' test: same synchronous grid, generator generally no more than 15 years old, and annual (12-month) temporal matching.

Hourly matching is not required for target progress, but Category A companies with significant electricity consumption must publicly report hourly matching performance, with voluntary recognition for leaders.

The V1 draft ambition of moving to low-carbon electricity no later than 2040 was consulted on in March 2025; verify the final milestone wording against the published standard text before relying on a date.

workstreams.name: Company categorisation and SMEs
workstreams.status_label: Category A / Category B replaces the standard vs SME split
workstreams.summary: V2.0 replaces the binary large-company / SME routes with a formal Category A and Category B classification driven by turnover, headcount, emissions and geography. Category B carries a materially lighter obligation set, most importantly optional scope 3 target-setting and no mandatory assurance.
key_points: Category A: broadly, net turnover at or above EUR 450 million, or at least 1,000 full-time equivalents in any country; additional high-income-country tests capture companies with scope 1+2 at or above 10,000 tCO2e or meeting two of (balance sheet EUR 25m, turnover EUR 50m, 250 FTE). Confirm the exact combination logic against the Criteria document.
Category B is defined as everything that does not meet the Category A thresholds, and faces reduced scope 3 requirements.
Category B must set scope 1 and scope 2 targets; scope 3 target-setting is optional.
Category B is exempt from mandatory third-party assurance (recommended only) and from the mandatory transition plan publication that Category A must complete within 15 months.
Category B still requires a long-term net-zero target by 2050 at the latest and neutralisation of residual emissions at the net-zero target year.

The legacy SME definition (from 1 January 2024) requires under 10,000 tCO2e scope 1 + location-based scope 2, exclusion of FI and oil and gas sectors, and three or more of: under 250 employees, turnover under EUR 50m, assets under EUR 25m.

workstreams.name: Removals, neutralisation and ongoing emissions responsibility
workstreams.status_label: New OER framework; mandatory removals for Category A from 2035
workstreams.summary: V2.0 converts V1's neutralisation milestone recommendation into a structured 'ongoing emissions responsibility' framework, and for the first time makes carbon removals mandatory for large companies ahead of the net-zero year. Carbon credits are positioned as a complement to, never a substitute for, abatement.

Detailed new requirements cover expected storage durability of removal activities, responsibility for neutralising direct and indirect emissions, double-counting conditions and neutralisation reporting.
An optional recognition programme rewards companies making voluntary climate contributions for their ongoing emissions in the short term.
An implementation hierarchy prioritises direct activity-level reductions before actions in shared activity pools or at sector level, which are permitted only where structural constraints exist.

Integrity criteria now apply to all actions, projects and market instruments used to support target implementation, requiring accurate emissions attributes, volume matching and transparent, secure tracking registries.
Bio-based feedstocks used for implementation must meet recognised third-party and SBTi minimum sustainability criteria and must not be associated with deforestation or natural ecosystem conversion.

Net-zero requires reducing scopes 1, 2 and 3 to zero or a residual level consistent with eligible net-zero pathways, then neutralising residual emissions at and after the target date; no numeric residual percentage is specified.

frameworks.name: ISSB / IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards
frameworks.tagline: The investor-focused global baseline for sustainability and climate disclosure.
frameworks.description: The International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), part of the IFRS Foundation, issued IFRS S1 (general sustainability-related financial disclosures) and IFRS S2 (climate-related disclosures) on 26 June 2023, both effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024. The standards are not law anywhere by themselves; they take legal effect only when a jurisdiction adopts or otherwise incorporates them. The ISSB is now in an implementation-support phase, has issued its first amendments to IFRS S2 (December 2025, effective 2027), is overhauling the SASB Standards, and is preparing an Exposure Draft of a nature-related disclosures Practice Statement for October 2026.
frameworks.status_headline: IFRS S1/S2 stable and in force; first IFRS S2 amendments land for 2027; nature Practice Statement Exposure Draft due October 2026; SASB Standards under a two-part overhaul.

workstreams.name: IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 as issued
workstreams.status_label: Final and effective since 1 January 2024
workstreams.summary: IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information and IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures were issued on 26 June 2023 and apply to annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024, with earlier application permitted where both are applied together. The base text of both standards is unchanged apart from the December 2025 greenhouse gas amendments to IFRS S2. Neither standard imposes a legal obligation on its own; obligations arise from jurisdictional adoption.
key_points: Issued 26 June 2023; effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024; earlier application permitted if IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 are applied together.
IFRS S2 Appendix C paragraph C4(a) gives a first-year relief allowing an entity to keep using the GHG measurement method it used in the period immediately preceding initial application of IFRS S2.

IFRS S1 carries transition reliefs including a climate-first relief (report only climate in year one), relief from comparative information in the first year, and relief on the timing of reporting relative to the financial statements.

The ISSB created a Transition Implementation Group on IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 to field application questions; the ISSB received TIG updates at its January 2026 and April 2026 meetings without taking decisions.
No comprehensive post-implementation review of IFRS S1/S2 has been announced; the ISSB's stated posture is to avoid disrupting implementation.

confidence.reasoning: Issue date, effective date and the C4(a) transition relief are stated in the IFRS Foundation's own standard pages and its IFRS S2 greenhouse gas educational material.

workstreams.name: Amendments to Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosures (Amendments to IFRS S2)
workstreams.status_label: Issued 11 December 2025, effective 1 January 2027
workstreams.summary: The ISSB issued targeted amendments to the greenhouse gas emissions disclosure requirements in IFRS S2 on 11 December 2025, following an Exposure Draft published on 28 April 2025 with a 60-day comment period that closed on 27 June 2025. The amendments apply to annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with early application permitted. Consequential amendments were issued at the same time to three SASB Standards (Asset Management & Custody Activities, Commercial Banks, Insurance) to align financed emissions metrics.
key_points: Relief 1: entities may limit measurement and disclosure of Scope 3 Category 15 emissions to financed emissions, rather than reporting all Category 15 emissions; entities must describe the financial activities excluded, including derivatives.
Relief 2: entities may use a classification system other than the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) when disaggregating financed emissions, provided a commonly used system is applied.

Relief 3: the jurisdictional relief from using the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard now applies even where only part of an entity is required by a jurisdictional authority or exchange to use a different measurement basis.
Relief 4: jurisdictional relief is available from using global warming potential values from the latest IPCC Assessment Report where a jurisdiction mandates different GWP values.
Effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027; early application permitted — so a calendar-year 2026 reporter can take the reliefs a year early.
ISSB Vice-Chair Sue Lloyd: the amendments 'will bring real relief to companies applying ISSB Standards without significantly affecting the decision-usefulness of information for investors'.

confidence.reasoning: Final amendments were published by the ISSB on 11 December 2025 with the effective date and each relief set out in the IFRS Foundation's own announcement and completed-project page.

workstreams.name: GHG Protocol referencing in IFRS S2
workstreams.status_label: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004) remains the default basis, with widened jurisdictional relief from 2027
workstreams.summary: IFRS S2 paragraph 29(a)(i) requires absolute gross Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions to be measured in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (2004). Paragraph 29(a)(ii) permits a different basis where a jurisdictional authority, or an exchange on which the entity is listed, requires it. The December 2025 amendments widen that relief so it applies where only part of the entity is subject to such a requirement, and the ISSB has an observer seat on the GHG Protocol's Independent Standards Board under a 2024 Memorandum of Understanding.
key_points: Default measurement basis is the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004 edition) — an explicit, dated reference in IFRS S2 paragraph 29(a)(i).
Jurisdictional/exchange exception in paragraph 29(a)(ii) allows a different basis where mandated; from 2027 this applies even to partial application within an entity.
IFRS S2 Appendix C paragraph C4(a) separately lets an entity keep its pre-existing measurement method for the first annual reporting period it applies IFRS S2.

The ISSB announced a Memorandum of Understanding with the GHG Protocol in June 2024 and appoints an observer to the GHG Protocol's Independent Standards Board, so future GHG Protocol revisions feed back into ISSB thinking.
The ISSB has not announced any project to update the dated 2004 reference in IFRS S2 to a revised GHG Protocol edition.

workstreams.name: Nature-related Disclosures (proposed IFRS Practice Statement)
workstreams.status_label: Exposure Draft balloting under way; publication targeted October 2026
workstreams.summary: The ISSB's Biodiversity, Ecosystems and Ecosystem Services research project moved into standard-setting on 10 December 2025 and was renamed Nature-related Disclosures in February 2026. In April 2026 the ISSB decided the output should be an IFRS Practice Statement that supplements IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 rather than a new Standard, drawing on the TNFD framework. On 21 July 2026 all 12 ISSB members confirmed due process was met and agreed a 120-day comment period; publication of the Exposure Draft is targeted for October 2026.
key_points: Form of output: an IFRS Practice Statement, agreed 12-0 in April 2026 — a tool companies may choose to use, unless a jurisdiction requires it. It does not amend IFRS S1 or IFRS S2.
The ISSB has been explicit that nature disclosure is not new: Chair Emmanuel Faber said 'Providing material nature-related disclosures is not optional; IFRS S1 already requires that.'
Balloting permission granted 21 July 2026, all 12 members, no dissents; 120-day comment period agreed; Exposure Draft targeted October 2026, so comments would close around February 2027.

Content decided so far: 'environmental resources' replaces 'environmental assets'; defined nature-related transition and physical risks; entities may reference TNFD metrics where these meet IFRS S1 objectives; the TNFD LEAP approach is referenced in guidance but is optional.
First application: available from the issuance date, no comparative information required in the first year, and a full compliance statement only when all requirements are met.

Scenario analysis: no new requirement to disclose use of scenario analysis for nature-related risks, but an incremental requirement for opportunities and a tentative requirement to use nature-related scenario analysis for resilience assessment.

confidence.reasoning: The Practice Statement form, 120-day comment period and October 2026 target are formal ISSB decisions recorded in ISSB Updates, but the Exposure Draft itself has not yet been published.

workstreams.name: Enhancing the SASB Standards (Phase 1 and Phase 1—Continued)
workstreams.status_label: Both Exposure Drafts closed; redeliberations under way; Technology & Communications scoped for Phase 2
workstreams.summary: The ISSB is running the first substantive overhaul of the SASB Standards since it took them over from the Value Reporting Foundation in 2022. An Exposure Draft published 3 July 2025 proposed comprehensive amendments to 9 SASB Standards and targeted amendments to 41 others, closing 30 November 2025 after a 150-day period. A follow-up Exposure Draft published 26 March 2026 covered three further Standards plus consequential amendments to the Industry-based Guidance on Implementing IFRS S2, closing 24 July 2026. On 22 July 2026 the ISSB agreed unanimously to enhance six SASB Standards in the Technology & Communications sector next.
key_points: Phase 1 Exposure Draft (3 July 2025): comprehensive review of 9 industries — all 8 in Extractives & Minerals Processing plus Processed Foods — and targeted amendments to 41 more, on topics such as Water Management and Workforce Health & Safety. Comments closed 30 November 2025.

Phase 1—Continued Exposure Draft (26 March 2026): Agricultural Products, Meat, Poultry & Dairy, and Electric Utilities & Power Generators, plus consequential amendments to the Industry-based Guidance on Implementing IFRS S2. Comments closed 24 July 2026 after a 120-day period.
Together the two Exposure Drafts cover 12 prioritised SASB Standards.
Ratified effective date approach (February 2026 decision): 12-18 months after issuance of the final amendments, with early application permitted.

IFRS S2 paragraph 32 requires entities to refer to and consider the applicability of the SASB-derived industry-based disclosure topics, so SASB changes flow through to IFRS S2 reporters.

frameworks.name: European Union
frameworks.tagline: Omnibus I has cut CSRD scope to ~1,000-employee groups and pushed first mandatory reporting to FY2027.
frameworks.description: The EU's corporate sustainability regime is built on the CSRD (Directive (EU) 2022/2464) and the ESRS delegated act, backed by the EU Taxonomy, CBAM and the CSDDD. In 2025-2026 the Omnibus I simplification package rewrote all of it: Directive (EU) 2025/794 stopped the clock, and Directive (EU) 2026/470 (in force 18 March 2026) cut scope to undertakings with more than 1,000 employees and more than EUR 450 million net turnover, deleted sector standards and reasonable assurance, and created a statutory value-chain cap. The Commission adopted the revised ESRS and the value-chain-cap voluntary standard as delegated acts on 3 July 2026; both are still in European Parliament and Council scrutiny.
frameworks.status_headline: Level 1 is final (Directive (EU) 2026/470, in force 18 March 2026); Level 2 revised ESRS adopted 3 July 2026 and awaiting the end of scrutiny before entry into force.

workstreams.name: CSRD as amended by Omnibus I
workstreams.status_label: Final: Directive (EU) 2026/470 in force 18 March 2026
workstreams.summary: Directive (EU) 2026/470 of 24 February 2026 amends the Accounting Directive so that mandatory sustainability reporting applies only to undertakings exceeding both EUR 450 000 000 net turnover and an average of 1 000 employees. Listed SMEs, small and non-complex credit institutions and captive insurers are removed from scope entirely. The new regime bites for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027.
key_points: Scope test is cumulative: Article 19a(1) as amended covers undertakings that on their balance sheet date 'exceed a net turnover of EUR 450 000 000 and an average number of 1 000 employees during the financial year' - both limbs must be met.
Article 29a(1) applies the same two thresholds on a consolidated basis to parent undertakings of a group.
Listed SMEs are out: Recital 15 removes the empowerment to adopt an LSME standard and deletes references to Article 29c; Recital 16 deletes the two-year opt-out in Article 19a(7) as redundant.

workstreams.name: Voluntary standard and the value-chain cap

workstreams.summary: SB 253, as amended by SB 219, requires US-formed business entities with total annual revenues over $1 billion that do business in California to disclose Scope 1, 2 and eventually Scope 3 emissions to CARB. CARB withdrew the final package from the Office of Administrative Law after submitting it on 20 May 2026, and by notice of 24 June 2026 deferred the 2026 deadline, with staff proposing a new date of 10 November 2026.
key_points: Deadline in flux: the adopted regulation text says 'on or before August 10, 2026'; CARB's 24 June 2026 notice deferred the 2026 deadline and the July 2026 workshop proposes 10 November 2026 as the new date and as the recurring annual date.

Scope test: entity formed under the laws of a US state, DC or the federal government, with total annual revenue over $1,000,000,000, that does business in California (Rev. & Tax. Code s.23101(b)(1) or (b)(2)); revenue is 'gross receipts' under Rev. & Tax. Code s.25120(f)(2), not net of cost of goods sold, tested on the lesser of the two previous fiscal years.

Scope 3 begins in 2027; CARB staff propose mandating only five categories at first (purchased goods and services; fuel- and energy-related activities; waste generated in operations; business travel; employee commuting), with the other ten voluntary.

Assurance: limited assurance over Scope 1 and 2 begins with reports submitted in 2027 (ISAE 3410 for engagements before 15 December 2026, ISSA 5000 after); statutory reasonable assurance from 2030 is not part of this rulemaking.

Fees are flat-rate per entity, calculated as total required revenue divided by the number of regulated entities; CARB issues a fee determination notice on or by 10 September and payment is due within 60 days.
CARB has said it will exercise enforcement discretion for good-faith first-year submissions, echoing its December 2024 enforcement notice.

confidence.reasoning: The statute is in force and the regulation was Board-approved, but the exact 2026 deadline is not yet finally adopted (the OAL package was withdrawn on/after 20 May 2026) and the Ninth Circuit's pending merits decision in Chamber of Commerce v. Sanchez could still strike the law down.

workstreams.name: SEC climate-related disclosure rules
workstreams.status_label: Stayed since April 2024; rescission proposed 29 May 2026, comments closed 3 August 2026
workstreams.summary: The SEC adopted The Enhancement and Standardization of Climate-Related Disclosures for Investors on 6 March 2024, then stayed the rules on 4 April 2024 pending the consolidated Eighth Circuit petitions. The Commission stopped defending the rules on 27 March 2025 and the Eighth Circuit held the petitions in abeyance on 12 September 2025 pending reconsideration or renewed defence. On 29 May 2026 the Commission proposed to rescind the rules entirely; the comment period closed on 3 August 2026 and no final rescission has been adopted.
key_points: The 2024 rules have never taken effect: they have been stayed under Exchange Act s.25(c)(2) and APA s.705 since 4 April 2024 and no registrant has had to comply.
Rescission proposal: Release No. 33-11421, File No. S7-2026-19, RIN 3235-AN76, published at 91 FR 33296 on 3 June 2026; comments closed 3 August 2026.

The Commission's stated rationale is that the rules exceeded its statutory authority and imposed substantial costs without commensurate benefit, existing materiality-based disclosure obligations being sufficient.

Litigation: consolidated petitions in the Eighth Circuit, lead case State of Iowa v. SEC, No. 24-1522, held in abeyance since 12 September 2025 until the Commission reconsiders by notice-and-comment rulemaking or renews its defence.

Practical effect for UK and other foreign private issuers: no SEC climate line-items are in force, and the existing materiality-based climate disclosure expectations under Regulation S-K continue to apply.

workstreams.name: UK Sustainability Reporting Standards (UK SRS S1 and S2)
workstreams.status_label: Final text published, voluntary use only
workstreams.summary: The Department for Business and Trade published the finalised UK SRS S1 and UK SRS S2 on 25 February 2026, created by assessing and endorsing the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The FRC confirms that reporting against UK SRS is not currently mandatory. Effective-date clauses were deliberately stripped out of the standards so that regulators and legislation set the timing instead.
key_points: Published 25 February 2026 by DBT; available for voluntary use by any entity, in whole or in part.
Effective dates were removed from the standards themselves — implementation dates come from FCA rules or future legislation, not the standards.

The 'climate-first' relief (delaying non-climate sustainability reporting) was kept but with no fixed time limit, so voluntary users can use it indefinitely and regulators can set their own window.
The requirement to use GICS industry classification was removed, following the ISSB's December 2025 amendments.
Government will consider mandating UK SRS for private companies through a separate Modernising Corporate Reporting consultation.

workstreams.name: FCA listing rules: CP26/5 on listed issuers' sustainability disclosures
workstreams.status_label: Consultation closed 20 March 2026; policy statement due autumn 2026
workstreams.summary: CP26/5 proposes replacing the FCA's existing TCFD-aligned listing rules with requirements based on UK SRS, in force from 1 January 2027 for accounting periods beginning on or after that date. UK SRS S2 would be mandatory except Scope 3; Scope 3 and UK SRS S1 would sit on a comply-or-explain footing with transitional reliefs. The FCA aims to publish final rules in autumn 2026.
key_points: Rules would come into force 1 January 2027 and apply to accounting periods beginning on or after that date — first annual reports land in 2028.
UK SRS S2 mandatory (climate), except Scope 3 GHG emissions which are comply-or-explain with an optional one-year deferral.
UK SRS S1 (wider sustainability) is comply-or-explain, with an optional two-year deferral for non-climate matters.
Issuers must say whether and where they have published a climate transition plan, or explain why they have not — there is no proposed duty to have one.
No mandatory assurance, but issuers must state whether third-party assurance was obtained and, if so, name the provider, scope and standard used.
Scope covers UKLR 6 commercial companies, UKLR 14 secondary listings, UKLR 15 depositary receipts, UKLR 16 non-equity/non-voting shares and UKLR 22 transition category.
For periods beginning before 1 January 2027, issuers stay on the existing TCFD rules or may adopt UK SRS early.

workstreams.name: Mandatory climate-related financial disclosure in company law
workstreams.status_label: In force for financial years beginning on or after 6 April 2022
workstreams.summary: The Companies (Strategic Report) (Climate-related Financial Disclosure) Regulations 2022 and the parallel LLP regulations require the largest UK companies and LLPs to make eight TCFD-style climate disclosures in the non-financial and sustainability information statement. This is the only broad-based mandatory climate reporting duty in UK company law and it is unaffected by the publication of UK SRS.
key_points: In scope: UK companies with more than 500 employees that are relevant public interest entities (regulated-market issuers, banking or insurance companies); AIM-quoted companies with more than 500 employees; and other companies with more than 500 employees and turnover above £500 million.
Large LLPs with more than 500 employees and turnover above £500 million, plus traded or banking LLPs with more than 500 employees, are caught by the equivalent LLP regulations (SI 2022/46).

Eight disclosures: governance; risk identification and assessment processes; integration into overall risk management; principal risks and opportunities with time horizons; impact on business model and strategy; scenario resilience analysis; targets and performance against them; and KPIs with methodologies.
Applies to accounting periods starting on or after 6 April 2022 — so FY2026 filers are in their fifth cycle.
There is no assurance requirement attached to these disclosures.

workstreams.status_label: In force since 1 April 2019; post-implementation review published May 2026
workstreams.summary: SECR obliges quoted companies, large unquoted companies and large LLPs to report UK energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, an intensity ratio and energy efficiency measures in the directors' report. DESNZ published a post-implementation review on 26 May 2026 concluding SECR improved transparency but identifying scope to simplify and reduce administrative burden. No repeal or amendment has been announced.
key_points: Created by the Companies (Directors' Report) and LLPs (Energy and Carbon Report) Regulations 2018 (SI 2018/1155), effective 1 April 2019.
Quoted companies report global Scope 1 and 2 emissions and underlying global energy use; large unquoted companies and LLPs report UK energy use and associated emissions.

Low energy user exemption: organisations consuming 40,000 kWh or less in the period may state that instead of reporting.

'Large' follows the Companies Act test — for accounting periods beginning on or after 6 April 2025 a company exceeds two of: turnover £54m, balance sheet total £27m, 250 employees, so some companies drop out of SECR on the uplifted thresholds.

The 26 May 2026 post-implementation review found SECR improved transparency and consistency but flagged simplification opportunities; findings will inform future work rather than trigger immediate change.

workstreams.name: Climate-related transition plan requirements
workstreams.status_label: Consultation closed 17 September 2025; no government response yet
workstreams.summary: DESNZ consulted between 25 June and 17 September 2025 on requiring UK-regulated financial institutions and FTSE 100 companies to produce Paris-aligned transition plans. Two implementation routes were put forward: a disclose-or-explain approach, or a duty to develop and publish a plan. As at 25 August 2026 the government is still analysing responses and no outcome has been published.
key_points: Manifesto scope was UK-regulated financial institutions (banks, asset managers, pension funds, insurers) and FTSE 100 companies; the consultation floated widening this to 'economically significant entities' while excluding SMEs.
Option 1: entities explain why they have not disclosed a transition plan. Option 2: entities must develop and disclose one, potentially as a standalone document refreshed at least every three years.
The consultation also tested whether plans must be aligned to net zero by 2050 and 1.5°C, and whether delivery of commitments should be mandatory.
Frameworks referenced are the Transition Plan Taskforce disclosure framework and UK SRS S2.
Separately, FCA CP26/5 would only require listed issuers to say whether and where a transition plan exists — not to have one.

confidence.reasoning: The consultation page still states the government is analysing feedback, so scope, route and timing all remain genuinely open.

workstreams.name: Oversight regime for sustainability assurance
workstreams.status_label: Government response published 30 January 2026; interim register from mid-2026
workstreams.summary: The government confirmed on 30 January 2026 that it will create a voluntary, opt-in registration regime for sustainability assurance practitioners, operated by the FRC. Assurance itself is not being made mandatory. An interim, non-legislative register was to be operational by mid-2026, with a statutory regime to follow when parliamentary time allows.
key_points: Assurance of sustainability reporting is not mandated — the regime governs who may hold themselves out as a registered assurance provider, not whether companies must buy assurance.
Registration is voluntary and opt-in; practitioners register with the financial reporting regulator subject to meeting conditions.
The FRC operates the regime. The government confirmed it is not proceeding with the Audit Reform Bill, so ARGA will not be created.
Deliberately profession-agnostic: statutory auditors, sustainability specialists and independent providers can all register.
Interim register operational by mid-2026 on a non-legislative basis; primary legislation to formalise it when parliamentary time allows.
Over 80% of the 99 respondents supported the core proposal.

confidence.reasoning: The policy decision is published and final, but the statutory regime depends on primary legislation that has not been introduced.

jurisdictions.name: Australia
jurisdictions.regulator: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC); standards by AASB and AUASB
jurisdictions.standard: AASB S2 Climate-related disclosures (mandatory); AASB S1 available voluntarily
jurisdictions.who_is_in_scope: Chapter 2M reporting entities meeting at least two of three size tests, plus NGER registrants and large asset owners. Group 1: consolidated revenue ≥A$500m, gross assets ≥A$1bn, or ≥500 employees. Group 2: ≥A$200m revenue, ≥A$500m assets, or ≥250 employees, plus asset owners with ≥A$5bn under management. Group 3: ≥A$50m revenue, ≥A$25m assets, or ≥100 employees.
jurisdictions.first_reporting_period: Group 1: financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2025. Group 2: on or after 1 July 2026. Group 3: on or after 1 July 2027.
jurisdictions.assurance: Mandatory and phased under ASSA 5010. Year 1: limited assurance over governance, strategy risks and opportunities and Scope 1 and 2 emissions. Years 2-3: limited assurance over all disclosures. Year 4 onwards: reasonable assurance over the whole sustainability report (Group 1 from periods beginning 1 July 2028).
jurisdictions.notes: The sustainability report is a statutory report under s296A of the Corporations Act containing climate statements, notes, a directors' declaration and scenario analysis against two mandated temperature scenarios. Modified liability applies to financial years commencing between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2027, during which directors declare they took reasonable steps rather than giving absolute assurance. The Government announced in the 2026-27 Budget that it will consult on reforms to reduce reporting burden while keeping core requirements.

confidence.reasoning: The regime is in force under Schedule 4 of Act No. 87 of 2024 and Group 1 entities have already lodged 259 sustainability reports as at 6 May 2026.

updates.headline: EFRAG opens a fatal flaw review on its draft list of datapoints for the revised ESRS
updates.detail: The EFRAG Secretariat published a draft Excel workbook listing the datapoints of the revised European Sustainability Reporting Standards as adopted by the European Commission in the delegated act of 3 July 2026. It succeeds the IG 3 List of ESRS Datapoints published in 2024, and adds datapoint type categorisation, links into EFRAG's ESRS Knowledge Hub and cross references back to the 2023 ESRS. Stakeholders are asked to review the compilation methodology and report any fatal flaws through an online survey by 23 October 2026. EFRAG says it will publish the final resource by the end of 2026, and describes the workbook as a non-authoritative Secretariat resource rather than an amendment to the standards.
updates.so_what: Map your existing IG 3 based datapoint inventory against this draft and file any gaps through the survey before 23 October 2026, while the list can still be corrected.
updates.source_title: EFRAG Secretariat Releases 2026 Draft List of Datapoints for Revised ESRS

updates.headline: AASB decides to monitor rather than regulate disclosure of sustainability assurance fees
updates.detail: The Australian Accounting Standards Board published Action Alert No. 249 reporting decisions from its 222nd board meeting held on 27 August 2026. On the agenda item covering disclosure of sustainability related assurance fees, the board decided to adopt a monitoring approach for now, in response to differences in how those fees are disclosed in practice under AASB S2. No standard setting project was opened and no consultation document was issued.
updates.so_what: Continue disclosing sustainability assurance fees as you do now, but expect the AASB to revisit this if practice stays divergent.
updates.source_title: AASB Action Alert No. 249, Board Meeting 222

updates.headline: ASIC commits in its 2026-27 corporate plan to review Group 1 entities' sustainability reports
updates.detail: ASIC published its Corporate Plan 2026-27, which states under Strategic Priority 2 that it will improve the quality of sustainability reports by reviewing the reports of listed and unlisted Group 1 entities. Implementation of the mandatory climate reporting framework is named as a focus area. ASIC says it will continue a pragmatic and proportionate approach, assisting implementation through guidance, education and relief, and engaging with large audit firms on their audit methodologies. The plan sets no dates for these sustainability activities.
updates.so_what: If you are a Group 1 entity reporting in Australia, assume your first sustainability report will be selected for ASIC surveillance and assemble the supporting evidence now.
updates.source_title: 26-200MR ASIC sets plan to be easier to deal with, harder to avoid

updates.headline: GHG Protocol reissues its Scope 2 consultation feedback summary as version 1.1
updates.detail: GHG Protocol republished the Scope 2 Public Consultation Summary of Feedback as version 1.1, superseding the 29 July 2026 release. The document states on its face that version 1.1 contains minor edits to tables and figures and that the substantive findings are unchanged. It summarises responses from nearly 1,100 respondents across 56 countries, records divided views on anchoring Scope 2 in attributional accounting and on physical connection requirements, and flags administrative burden around hourly emission factors and uneven availability of granular data outside developed markets. GHG Protocol says the feedback will inform the next phase of technical working group development and Independent Standards Board review, but publishes no timeline for that phase.
updates.so_what: Re-download version 1.1 if your Scope 2 impact assessment quotes tables or figures from the 29 July version, and confirm none of the numbers you cited have moved.
updates.source_title: Scope 2 Public Consultation Summary of Feedback, Version 1.1

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation approves five year plan and confirms a new ISSB seat in Geneva
updates.detail: The IFRS Foundation Trustees announced an integrated five-year operating and financing plan covering both the IASB and the ISSB. A new seat of the ISSB will open in Geneva in mid-2027, with Frankfurt continuing as the EU engagement hub and Montreal retaining key functions. ISSB funding is secured through 2031 from philanthropic contributions, jurisdictional commitments and earned revenue, and proposed Constitution amendments would reduce each board to 10 members from 2028.
updates.so_what: Assume the ISSB remains a funded, permanent standard-setter through the end of the decade when setting your multi-year reporting roadmap.
updates.source_title: IFRS Foundation Trustees announce five-year plan including new seat of the ISSB in Geneva

updates.headline: SBTi opens four new consultations across power, FLAG and high emitting sectors
updates.detail: SBTi published a consolidated call for participation covering four live opportunities. A call for evidence on high-emitting sectors including aluminium, aviation and steel closes 11 September 2026. The second Power Sector Net-Zero Standard consultation closes 7 September 2026. FLAG regional convening expressions of interest close 8 September 2026 and the FLAG call for evidence closes 8 October 2026.

updates.headline: SBTi target statuses and terminology change from 24 September
updates.detail: SBTi announced that the public Target Dashboard will adopt revised company status terminology, updated commitment- and target-level status classifications and new status descriptions and reasons from 24 September 2026. Regional and territory classifications will move to the UN M49 standard. The revised Commitment and Target Status Document will supersede the existing Commitment Compliance Policy on implementation.

updates.headline: SBTi updates its five year review process and transition arrangements
updates.detail: SBTi explained the revised Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance. The review trigger commences at the end of the month five years after the most recent validation publication, with six months to submit the review form and up to 12 months to submit revised targets. Companies transitioning to Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0 or a new sector standard can request deadline extensions on a case-by-case basis, including scope 3 only extensions. Of more than 11,600 companies with validated targets, around 300 require review by end-2026.
updates.so_what: Calculate your trigger month from your validation publication date and lodge an extension request if you plan to jump straight to V2.0.
updates.source_title: Ten things companies need to know about the updated Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance and the Commitment and Target Statuses Document

updates.headline: GHG Protocol confirms AMI moving to drafting and Forest Carbon RFI open to February 2027
updates.detail: GHG Protocol's August 2026 Pulse recaps the 29 July consolidation announcement, the Scope 2 consultation findings and the LSR Guidance release. It confirms the Actions and Market Instruments Technical Working Group met in person in Amsterdam from 30 June to 2 July 2026 on market-based inventory design, GHG impact assessment, additionality and traceability, and is transitioning to drafting the standard. It also confirms the Forest Carbon Accounting Request for Information remains open for submissions through 1 February 2027.
updates.so_what: Treat the AMI multi-statement structure as the direction of travel now that its working group has moved from concept to drafting.
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol Pulse: August Update

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation names Steven Maijoor next Trustees Chair and Sam Woods IASB Chair
updates.detail: The IFRS Foundation announced that Steven Maijoor, former Chair of ESMA, will become Chair of the Trustees on 1 January 2027 for an initial three-year term, succeeding Erkki Liikanen. Sam Woods, former Deputy Governor of the Bank of England and CEO of the UK Prudential Regulation Authority, becomes IASB Chair on 1 October 2026 for a five-year term. Emmanuel Faber continues as ISSB Chair, and Laura Forzani takes up the Managing Director role on 1 September 2026.
updates.so_what: Expect continuity in ISSB technical direction but watch for a possible shift in Trustee-level tone on regulatory engagement from 2027.
updates.source_title: Steven Maijoor to serve as next Chair of the IFRS Foundation Trustees; Sam Woods appointed to chair the IASB

updates.headline: ISO 14068 carbon neutrality standard reaches stage 60.00, under publication
updates.detail: The replacement for ISO 14068-1:2023 moved to stage 60.00, International Standard under publication, on 7 August 2026, with a target publication date of September 2026. It drops the part number and is titled Climate change management - Carbon neutrality. It applies to organisations and products, prioritises value-chain reductions and removal enhancements over offsetting, and excludes territories and UNFCCC national reporting.
updates.so_what: Diarise a review of every carbon neutral claim you or your suppliers make against ISO 14068-1:2023 for September 2026.
updates.source_title: ISO 14068 - Climate change management - Carbon neutrality

updates.headline: CARB opens six listening sessions on the 2027-2030 climate disclosure rulemaking
updates.detail: CARB scheduled a series of stakeholder listening sessions on 5, 12, 19 and 26 August and 2 and 9 September 2026, covering six stakeholder categories, to inform the second phase of the climate disclosure rulemaking. That second rulemaking is expected to cover Scope 3 reporting requirements from 2027, the assurance regime and the 2030 reasonable-assurance step. The sessions follow CARB's July 2026 workshop, at which staff set out preliminary Scope 3 and assurance proposals.
updates.so_what: Put your Scope 3 data limitations on the record now, because the categories CARB mandates for 2027 are being decided in these sessions.
updates.source_title: SB 253 Public Workshop: California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (July 2026)

updates.headline: SEC comment period closes on the proposal to rescind its climate-related disclosure rules
updates.detail: The public comment period on Release No. 33-11421, Rescission of Climate-Related Disclosure Rules (File No. S7-2026-19), closed on 3 August 2026, sixty days after Federal Register publication at 91 FR 33296 on 3 June 2026. The Commission has not adopted a final rescission. The 2024 rules remain formally on the books but stayed, and the consolidated Eighth Circuit petitions remain in abeyance.
updates.so_what: Treat SEC climate line-items as dead for planning purposes but keep the stayed rules on your regulatory register until a final adopting release issues.
updates.source_title: Rescission of Climate-Related Disclosure Rules, 91 FR 33296

updates.headline: SBTi opens call for input on FLAG Standard Version 2
updates.detail: SBTi issued a call for input to inform the revision of the Forest, Land and Agriculture Standard. Version 2 will incorporate innovations from Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0, including the new categorisation approach, five-year review cycles and expanded target-setting options, and will align with the updated GHG Protocol Land Sector and Removals Standard. Expressions of interest for regional convenings close 8 September 2026 and the call for evidence closes 8 October 2026. Development is expected to span 12 or more months.
updates.so_what: Food, drink, agriculture and forestry companies with FLAG targets should submit evidence before 8 October 2026.
updates.source_title: SBTi issues call for input to inform revision of Forest, Land and Agriculture Standard

updates.headline: GHG Protocol merges four revisions into one GHGP-ISO corporate standard
updates.detail: GHG Protocol announced that the Corporate Standard, Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard and Actions and Market Instruments workstreams will be combined with ISO 14064-1 into a single co-branded global standard. Version 2.0 of the Standard Development Plan, published the same day, sets out a two-part structure - Part 1 general requirements and physical GHG inventory, Part 2 actions and market instruments - and estimates an integrated public consultation in Q2 2027 with publication in Q4 2028. The four separate Standard Development Plans published on 20 December 2024 are superseded.
updates.so_what: Rebase your standards-change roadmap on a single 2028 publication rather than four staggered revisions.
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol Announces Key Standard Development Updates

updates.headline: GHG Protocol reports no consensus on renewable energy in its Scope 2 consultation
updates.detail: Reporting on the consultation that closed on 31 January 2026, GHG Protocol said it received close to 1,100 responses from 56 countries. Respondents diverged sharply on renewable energy accounting but broadly supported improving the accuracy, comparability and integrity of electricity emissions accounting. The technical team is now exploring multiple reporting approaches rather than finalising the consulted text, and any revised Scope 2 provisions will surface in the consolidated consultation.
updates.so_what: Do not assume the consulted hourly-matching proposal is settled - the outcome is being re-opened, so keep procurement decisions flexible.
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol Announces Key Standard Development Updates: FAQ Resource

updates.headline: ISSB consults on taxonomy update reflecting the December 2025 IFRS S2 GHG amendments
updates.detail: The ISSB published IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy—Proposed Update 1: Amendments to Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosures. It adds and adjusts digital tagging elements so that disclosures made under the amended IFRS S2 greenhouse gas requirements can be tagged consistently. Comments close on 28 September 2026. The proposal introduces no new reporting requirements for companies.
updates.so_what: Pass this to your XBRL or structured-filing owner so tagging templates are updated before jurisdictions mandate the amended IFRS S2 elements.
updates.source_title: ISSB proposes updates to its digital sustainability taxonomy

updates.headline: ACRA opens consultation on localised Singapore sustainability disclosure standards
updates.detail: ACRA's Interim Sustainability Standards Committee published draft Singapore Sustainability Disclosure Standards for public consultation on 27 July 2026, comprising SFRS S1 covering broader sustainability disclosures on a voluntary basis and SFRS S2 covering mandatory climate-related disclosures. The drafts propose Singapore-specific adjustments to structure, transition reliefs, compliance statements and references to SASB material. The consultation closes on 25 October 2026 and no outcome has been published.
updates.so_what: If you report in Singapore, respond before 25 October 2026 — the transition reliefs in the draft are where the compliance cost is decided.
updates.source_title: Public Consultation on Singapore's Sustainability Disclosure Standards

updates.headline: SBTi updates the Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance after early-adopter feedback
updates.detail: SBTi published updates to the Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance, refining its 2025 resources after input from companies that went through the process first. The stated aim was to make navigation clearer and simpler while maintaining integrity, credibility and ambition. A five-year review does not automatically require a target update where existing targets still meet applicable criteria.
updates.so_what: Read the revised guidance before your review window opens, since the process now allows you to skip the review form and go straight to resubmission.
updates.source_title: What companies need to know about updates to the Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance

updates.headline: EFRAG opens 100-day consultation on ESRS-40a for third-country undertakings
updates.detail: EFRAG published the exposure draft of ESRS-40a, the separate sustainability reporting standard for non-EU parent undertakings captured by Article 40a of the Accounting Directive. The consultation runs from 23 July to 31 October 2026. The standard will apply to third-country undertakings with net turnover in the Union above EUR 450 million in each of the last two consecutive financial years and an EU branch or subsidiary with net turnover above EUR 200 million. First sustainability statements are expected in 2029 covering financial year 2028.
updates.so_what: If your non-EU parent clears EUR 450m of EU turnover, review the ESRS-40a draft and respond before 31 October 2026.
updates.source_title: European Sustainability Standards for Third-Country Undertakings (ESRS-40a)

updates.headline: ISSB agrees to enhance six SASB Standards in the Technology & Communications sector
updates.detail: At its 21-22 July 2026 meeting the ISSB decided unanimously (12 of 12 members) to enhance six SASB Standards within the Technology & Communications sector of the Sustainable Industry Classification System. Staff will now prepare an Exposure Draft of proposed amendments to those Standards. This extends the SASB enhancement programme beyond the 12 prioritised Standards already consulted on in the two Phase 1 Exposure Drafts.
updates.so_what: Technology and telecoms reporters should expect their SASB-derived IFRS S2 industry metrics to be reopened for consultation within the next year.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update July 2026

updates.headline: SBTi appoints 16 Technical Council members under a new staggered renewal model
updates.detail: SBTi announced Technical Council appointments for the new term: 16 members in total, comprising 10 reappointed members on one- or two-year terms and 6 new members on initial three-year terms, with 5 members completing their terms. Laura Draucker was appointed Chair, having previously served as Vice-Chair, with Piers Forster as Vice-Chair. The staggered annual renewal model was approved in December 2025 to maintain continuity of expertise.
updates.so_what: Track Technical Council minutes as the earliest reliable signal of forthcoming criteria changes.
updates.source_title: The SBTi announces Technical Council appointments for the new term

updates.headline: ISSB clears the nature-related disclosures Exposure Draft for balloting
updates.detail: All 12 ISSB members confirmed that due process requirements had been met for the Exposure Draft of the proposed nature-related disclosures Practice Statement, and none indicated an intention to dissent from its publication. The ISSB agreed unanimously to a 120-day comment period. The board also discussed an analysis of the likely effects of the proposals, which required no decisions. Balloting now begins ahead of publication targeted for October 2026.
updates.so_what: Diarise a consultation response window running from roughly October 2026 to February 2027 if nature-related risks are material to your business.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update July 2026

updates.headline: CARB proposes 10 November as the new Scope 1-2 reporting date and sets out Scope 3 plans
updates.detail: At a virtual public workshop on 21 July 2026 CARB staff confirmed that the final rulemaking package submitted to the Office of Administrative Law on 20 May 2026 had been withdrawn to allow limited clarifying changes and would be resubmitted. Staff proposed a new 2026 Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting deadline of 10 November 2026 and regulation text providing that emissions be disclosed 'on or before November 10 of the reporting year'. Staff also proposed that mandatory Scope 3 reporting from 2027 be limited initially to five categories - purchased goods and services, fuel- and energy-related activities, waste generated in operations, business travel and employee commuting - with the remaining ten voluntary, and confirmed that limited assurance over Scope 1 and 2 begins with reports submitted in 2027.
updates.so_what: Move your California submission plan to a 10 November 2026 date and scope your 2027 assurance engagement now.
updates.source_title: SB 253 Public Workshop: California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (July 2026)

updates.headline: SBTi opens a second consultation on the draft Power Sector Net-Zero Standard
updates.detail: SBTi launched the second public consultation on the updated draft Power Sector Net-Zero Standard, running to 7 September 2026. The draft aligns the sector standard with Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0, clarifies the treatment of transmission and distribution, heat and power generation and excludes electricity trading, revises the low-carbon generation definition to an emissions-intensity basis and adds regional pathways based on the IEA 2024 World Energy Outlook. Biomass sustainability requirements were removed because they are now covered by the corporate standard.
updates.so_what: Energy suppliers and generators should review the retail electricity target treatment and respond before 7 September 2026.
updates.source_title: The SBTi launches second public consultation on updated draft Power Sector Net-Zero Standard

updates.headline: SBTi Services launches a V2.0 readiness service
updates.detail: SBTi announced that SBTi Services has launched a new service to help companies understand their readiness for Corporate Net-Zero Standard Version 2.0. The announcement follows the June 2026 publication of V2.0 and precedes the opening of V2.0 validations in Q1 2027.
updates.so_what: Consider a readiness assessment during 2026 while you still have a year of runway before V2.0 validations open.
updates.source_title: SBTi Services launches new service to help companies understand their readiness for the Corporate Net-Zero Standard Version 2.0

updates.headline: GHG Protocol opens recruitment for new Independent Standards Board members
updates.detail: GHG Protocol launched a call for applications to its Independent Standards Board, the body that oversees the standards development process and approves final standards. It sought applicants from civil society, academia and research institutions and from North America, Latin America and Africa. Applications closed on 8 August 2026 at 23:59 ET.
updates.so_what: Track who joins the ISB, because this board's votes decide which proposals survive consultation.
updates.source_title: ANNOUNCEMENT: GHG Protocol Launches Call for Independent Standards Board Applications

updates.headline: Commission adopts revised ESRS and the value-chain-cap voluntary standard as delegated acts
updates.detail: The Commission adopted two delegated regulations: C(2026) 5010 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 to simplify the ESRS, and C(2026) 5011 establishing sustainability reporting standards for voluntary use by undertakings protected by the value chain cap. Mandatory datapoints fall by more than 60% and total datapoints by more than 70%, with expected cost savings above 30% per company. Both acts are subject to a European Parliament and Council scrutiny period of two months, extendable to four, and the ESRS act provides it shall not enter into force earlier than four months after adoption.
updates.so_what: Start rebuilding your ESRS datapoint mapping against the revised standards now rather than waiting for Official Journal publication.
updates.source_title: Commission adopts revised sustainability reporting standards to reduce administrative burdens for EU businesses

updates.headline: SBTi updates the Buildings Sector Criteria to Version 1.2
updates.detail: SBTi published Version 1.2 of the Buildings Sector Science-Based Target-Setting Criteria, dated July 2026, succeeding Version 1.1 of June 2025. An accompanying Buildings Criteria FAQs document and Buildings Sector Explanatory Document were issued at Version 1.2. The buildings standard is separately listed as in scoping for a fuller revision aligned to Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0.
updates.so_what: Real estate and construction groups should confirm they are working from the July 2026 Version 1.2 criteria, not the 2025 edition.
updates.source_title: Buildings Sector Science-Based Target-Setting Criteria, Version 1.2, July 2026

updates.workstream: Land Sector and Removals Standard and Guidance
updates.headline: GHG Protocol publishes LSR Guidance v1.0 and opens a Forest Carbon Accounting RFI
updates.detail: GHG Protocol released the Land Sector and Removals Guidance version 1.0 as a companion to the LSR Standard, with worked examples, equations, calculation guidance and 10 corporate case studies, plus a sample reporting template and a reporting requirements checklist. A minor v1.1 update to the Standard was issued at the same time. On the same day GHG Protocol opened a Request for Information on forest carbon accounting seeking scientifically robust and practically implementable proposals, open until 1 February 2027, and advised organisations disclosing forest carbon in the meantime to be transparent about methodology.
updates.so_what: Download the LSR reporting requirements checklist and run it against your FY2027 data plan before year end.
updates.source_title: Announcement: GHG Protocol Launches Land Sector and Removals (LSR) Guidance to Support LSR Standard Implementation

updates.headline: ISSB previews its nature proposals: a Practice Statement, with consultation later in 2026
updates.detail: Speaking at the IFRS Foundation Conference in London, ISSB Vice-Chair Sue Lloyd previewed the nature-related disclosure proposals. She confirmed the output will be a Practice Statement subject to the same due process as a Standard, targeted for Exposure Draft publication in October 2026, drawing on the TNFD framework and working alongside IFRS S1 and IFRS S2. Lloyd said the Practice Statement 'will be a tool that companies can choose to use when providing nature-related information to investors, although a jurisdiction could decide to require companies to use it', and that this approach avoids disrupting ongoing ISSB implementation.
updates.so_what: Treat nature reporting as optional at ISSB level but check whether your jurisdiction signals an intention to mandate the Practice Statement.
updates.source_title: Sue Lloyd previews nature-related disclosure proposals at IFRS Foundation Conference

updates.headline: ISSB settles nature terminology, TNFD metric references and first-application provisions
updates.detail: At its 24-25 June 2026 meeting the ISSB decided to replace 'environmental assets' with 'environmental resources' (12 of 12) and to define nature-related transition risks and nature-related physical risks (8 of 12). It agreed entities may reference TNFD metrics where these meet IFRS S1 objectives and do not conflict with the Standards (11 of 12), and to retain the CDSB Framework Application Guidance reference in IFRS S1 (12 of 12). On first application (12 of 12), the Practice Statement will be available from its issuance date, no comparative information is required in the first year, and a full compliance statement is required only when all requirements are met.
updates.so_what: If you already report TNFD metrics, keep them — the ISSB is explicitly permitting them as a source rather than replacing them.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update June 2026

updates.headline: CARB issues notice deferring the 2026 SB 253 reporting deadline
updates.detail: CARB published a Notice on Upcoming Rulemaking Update and 2026 Reporting Deadline Deferral on 24 June 2026, deferring the first Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting deadline that the Board-approved regulation had set at 10 August 2026. CARB's July 2026 workshop materials direct reporting entities to that notice and propose 10 November 2026 as the replacement date. CARB also committed to publish additional guidance materials supporting 2026 Scope 1 and 2 reporting by 1 September 2026.
updates.so_what: Confirm your internal deadline has been reset to November and do not stand down the reporting workstream.
updates.source_title: SB 253 Public Workshop: California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (July 2026)

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation says UK SRS is finalised but mandatory application remains undecided
updates.detail: The IFRS Foundation's United Kingdom jurisdictional snapshot, updated 18 June 2026, records the UK's status as 'In progress'. The UK government published final UK Sustainability Reporting Standards on 25 February 2026, endorsing IFRS S1 and IFRS S2; these are currently available for voluntary use and do not themselves create legal obligations. The FCA consulted on amendments to the UK Listing Rules from 30 January 2026 to 20 March 2026, with final decisions expected in autumn 2026. Application to entities outside the listed sector remains a matter for future UK government decision under the Companies Act.
updates.so_what: UK reporters should prepare against UK SRS S1 and S2 now and treat the FCA's autumn 2026 policy statement as the date that fixes first mandatory reporting periods.
updates.source_title: Jurisdictional snapshot: United Kingdom

updates.headline: ISO opens a 12-week consultation on ISO/DIS 14060, its net zero alignment standard
updates.detail: ISO launched the DIS ballot on ISO/DIS 14060, Net zero aligned organizations, describing it as the world's first international independently verifiable standard supporting credible and comprehensive net zero transition plans. The 12-week consultation runs to early September 2026, with comments submitted through national standards bodies. The standard replaces IWA 42:2022, the ISO Net Zero Guidelines, and sits alongside ISO 32212 on transition planning for financial institutions.
updates.so_what: Submit comments through BSI now - the window closes in early September 2026 and this standard will become the yardstick for transition plan credibility.
updates.source_title: ISO launches public consultation on the world's first International Standard for net zero alignment today

updates.headline: Council agrees negotiating position on extending CBAM to downstream goods
updates.detail: The Council adopted its negotiating mandate on the Commission's December 2025 proposal to extend CBAM to selected downstream products and add anti-circumvention measures. The Council refined the product list and asked the Commission to review annually which further downstream products should be added. Pre-consumer metal scrap is brought into scope and the Commission would gain powers to tackle deceptive reporting by high-risk companies. Trilogues start once Parliament adopts its position, with a target of concluding before the end of 2026.
updates.so_what: Inventory the CBAM-material content of your imported finished goods before the downstream list is fixed.
updates.source_title: Council moves to strengthen the EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism

updates.headline: SBTi publishes Corporate Net-Zero Standard Version 2.0
updates.detail: SBTi released Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0, describing it as a shift of focus from target-setting to implementation. It introduces differentiated approaches for smaller companies and companies in lower-income countries, context-specific target options, a best-efforts basis acknowledging factors outside company control, an implementation hierarchy prioritising direct reductions before market instruments, continuous assessment through annual reporting and periodic reviews, and a balanced treatment of carbon credits as a complement rather than a substitute. The initiative said the standard draws on a decade of experience supporting more than 11,000 companies.
updates.so_what: Commission a V1.3.1 to V2.0 gap analysis this financial year rather than at your next renewal.
updates.source_title: The SBTi releases Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0 to accelerate corporate climate action

updates.headline: SBTi sets out the V2.0 rollout roadmap and confirms V1 targets stay valid
updates.detail: Alongside publication, SBTi set out what follows. The methods and pathways document was open for feedback until 31 July 2026 with a final version due Q4 2026, alongside interpretation guidance, preliminary interim accounting and reporting guidance and an initial Interoperability and Recognition Framework. A Claims Policy is due Q1 2027 and validation against V2.0 opens 1 February 2027. Existing validated targets remain fully valid throughout their target cycle, with early access to selected V2.0 innovations to come via a Renewal Policy expected Q4 2026.
updates.so_what: Plan your V2.0 build around the Q4 2026 interpretation guidance rather than attempting to interpret the standard text alone.
updates.source_title: The Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0 is here: what comes next

updates.headline: SSBJ issues practical standard on using Japanese GHG reporting system data
updates.detail: The Sustainability Standards Board of Japan issued a Practical Sustainability Disclosure Standard covering the use of disclosures made under the Japanese GHG reporting system when complying with the SSBJ's climate standard. It is aimed at reducing duplicate measurement effort for companies already reporting emissions to Japanese authorities. The standard supplements the three inaugural SSBJ Standards issued in March 2025.
updates.so_what: Japanese subsidiaries should check whether existing statutory GHG filings can be reused for SSBJ climate disclosures before commissioning new measurement work.
updates.source_title: SSBJ Standards

updates.headline: ISO closes the comment period on the second working draft of ISO 14064-2
