updates.detail: The second working draft study for ISO/WD 14064-2.2, the third edition of the project-level GHG quantification standard, closed its comment period on 6 June 2026. The project was approved on 14 October 2024 and the second study opened on 3 April 2026. The document remains at stage 20.60 and will replace ISO 14064-2:2019.
updates.so_what: Note that project-level accounting is being revised at ISO, not at GHG Protocol, and follow the ISO track if you deal in carbon credits.
updates.source_title: ISO/WD 14064-2.2 - Greenhouse gases - Part 2: project level

updates.headline: SBTi Chemical Sector Pathways and Implementation Criteria take effect
updates.detail: The SBTi Chemical Sector Pathways and Implementation Criteria Version 1.0, published on 2 December 2025, became effective on 2 June 2026. One pathway is mandatory: companies must address scope 1 N2O emissions from nitric acid production where those emissions are at least 5% of total scope 1 emissions. Optional pathways cover ammonia, methanol and high-value chemical production, non-primary chemical production, nitrogen fertiliser use-phase emissions and alternative feedstock sourcing. The criteria apply modularly at activity level.
updates.so_what: Chemicals companies should map their activities against the modular pathways to see which criteria bind them.
updates.source_title: SBTi Chemical Sector Pathways and Implementation Criteria, Version 1.0

updates.headline: GHG Protocol closes the AMI Request for Information with nearly 500 responses
updates.detail: The 60-day Request for Information on the Actions and Market Instruments Phase 1 White Paper closed on 31 May 2026. GHG Protocol reported nearly 500 stakeholder responses, with preliminary findings supporting the proposed multi-statement reporting approach that separates physical inventory emissions, market-instrument-linked emissions and consequentially assessed climate action impacts. A formal draft standard consultation is planned for Q3 2027.
updates.so_what: Prepare to report market-based claims as a separate statement rather than as an inventory variant.
updates.source_title: Actions and Market Instruments Standard

updates.headline: SEC proposes to rescind its climate-related disclosure rules in full
updates.detail: On 29 May 2026 the SEC proposed to rescind the climate-related disclosure rules it adopted in March 2024, issuing Release No. 33-11421. The Commission's stated rationale is that the rules exceeded its statutory authority and, as a matter of policy, imposed substantial costs on public companies without adequate justification given existing materiality-based disclosure obligations. The proposal responds to the Eighth Circuit's 12 September 2025 order holding the consolidated petitions in abeyance until the Commission either reconsiders the rules through notice-and-comment rulemaking or renews its defence of them.
updates.so_what: Close out any residual SEC climate readiness spend and reallocate it to California and EU obligations.
updates.source_title: SEC Proposes Rescission of Climate-Related Disclosure Rules

updates.headline: DESNZ publishes post-implementation review of the SECR regulations
updates.detail: The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero published its 2026 post-implementation review of the Companies (Directors' Report) and LLPs (Energy and Carbon Report) Regulations 2018 on 26 May 2026. The review concluded that SECR has contributed to improved transparency and consistency in company-level energy and carbon reporting, while identifying opportunities to simplify and reduce administrative burden. It announced no decision to keep, amend or repeal SECR, saying the findings will inform future work on the proportionality of energy and carbon reporting and how SECR fits with wider corporate reporting obligations.
updates.so_what: Keep reporting SECR unchanged for FY2026 and treat simplification as a possibility to monitor, not a change to plan around.
updates.source_title: 2026 post-implementation review of the SECR regulations 2018
updates.source_publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

updates.headline: CARB submits the climate disclosure final rulemaking package to OAL, then withdraws it
updates.detail: CARB submitted the final rulemaking package for the California Greenhouse Gas Reporting and Climate-Related Financial Risk Disclosure initial regulation to the Office of Administrative Law on 20 May 2026. CARB subsequently withdrew the package to allow for limited further clarifying changes and stated it will resubmit. Until OAL approves and the regulation is filed, the deadline and fee provisions are approved but not yet legally operative.
updates.so_what: Do not treat any CARB deadline as legally fixed until the regulation clears OAL.
updates.source_title: SB 253 Public Workshop: California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (July 2026)

updates.headline: ASIC publishes early observations from the first mandatory sustainability reports
updates.detail: ASIC reviewed sustainability reports lodged by 31 December 2025 and reported on 18 May 2026 that 259 reports had been lodged as at 6 May 2026, 34 from listed and 225 from unlisted entities, concentrated in mining, construction and manufacturing, financial services, oil and gas and energy. ASIC set out six observations for 30 June 2026 reporters: avoid conflicting disclaimers that discourage reliance on the report; use available historical data when identifying climate risks; clearly disclose assumptions and measurement uncertainty; do not obscure material information with excess voluntary content; meet cross-referencing requirements precisely; and recognise regulatory obligations such as the Safeguard Mechanism as climate-related targets. Final observations are due in the second half of 2026.
updates.so_what: Strip reliance-limiting disclaimers out of any Australian climate statement — ASIC has named them as its first observation.
updates.source_title: ASIC issues early observations on sustainability reporting ahead of 30 June 2026

updates.headline: ASIC flags Government plan to consult on reducing sustainability reporting burden
updates.detail: In setting its financial reporting, audit and sustainability focus areas for FY2026-27, ASIC noted that the Government announced in the Budget that it proposes to commence consultation on reforms to reduce reporting burden while maintaining core sustainability reporting requirements. The 2026-27 Budget regulatory reform factsheet describes clarifying how key concepts such as 'undue cost or effort' apply in practice, adjusting assurance settings and setting clearer boundaries on requests for supplier information. ASIC's own administration in FY2026-27 focuses on Group 1 sustainability reports and engagement with large audit firms on assurance methodology.
updates.so_what: Do not slow your Group 2 preparation on the strength of a promised simplification consultation — the core requirements are explicitly being kept.
updates.source_title: 26-098MR ASIC sets financial reporting, audit and sustainability focus areas for FY 2026-27

updates.headline: ISSB decides nature scenario analysis is required for resilience, not risk identification
updates.detail: At its 13 May 2026 meeting the ISSB decided against adding a specific requirement to disclose whether an entity uses scenario analysis to identify nature-related risks. It approved an incremental requirement to disclose whether scenario analysis is used to inform identification of nature-related opportunities, and tentatively decided to require nature-related scenario analysis for assessing resilience, noting such assessments are more location- and asset-specific than climate scenario analysis. The TNFD LEAP approach will be referenced in guidance material but remains optional. The same meeting reviewed stakeholder feedback on the Phase 1 SASB proposals for Extractives & Mineral Processing and Processed Foods without taking decisions.
updates.so_what: Budget for location-level nature scenario work if the Practice Statement is finalised as drafted; it is more granular than your existing climate scenario analysis.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update May 2026

updates.headline: ISO closes the comment period on the second working draft of ISO 14064-1 third edition
updates.detail: ISO/WD 14064-1.2, the third edition of the organization-level GHG quantification and reporting standard, closed the comment period on its second working draft study on 12 May 2026, reaching stage 20.60. The second study opened on 1 April 2026 following a first comment period that closed on 26 August 2025. The next step is approval for registration as a Committee Draft. It will replace ISO 14064-1:2018, which has been flagged to be revised since 14 October 2024.
updates.so_what: Continue verifying against ISO 14064-1:2018 - the replacement is still two ballot stages from publication.
updates.source_title: ISO/WD 14064-1.2 - Greenhouse gases - Part 1

updates.headline: ISO 14068-1:2023 moves to stage 90.92, International Standard to be revised
updates.detail: The carbon neutrality standard published on 30 November 2023 was formally flagged for revision at stage 90.92 on 8 May 2026, ahead of its replacement by the new single-part ISO 14068. The 2023 edition remains available and in force until the replacement publishes.
updates.so_what: Flag any ISO 14068-1:2023 based carbon neutral claim in your supply chain as time-limited.
updates.source_title: ISO 14068-1:2023 - Climate change management - Part 1: Carbon neutrality

updates.headline: Commission publishes explanatory note on how the value-chain cap works
updates.detail: Alongside the consultation on the draft revised reporting standards, the Commission issued additional explanatory information on the value chain cap. A CSRD reporter may request but not require information beyond the voluntary standard's necessary disclosures from an undertaking with 1,000 or fewer employees, must flag which requested items exceed the cap, and must tell the counterparty of its statutory right to decline. Critically, the Commission states the cap applies only to CSRD reporting and does not affect information requests for other purposes.
updates.so_what: Add the required exceeds-the-cap flag and right-to-decline notice to every supplier sustainability request template.
updates.source_title: Feedback on sustainability reporting standards: additional explanatory information regarding the value chain cap

updates.headline: Fourth Commission Notice interprets the simplified Taxonomy Disclosures Delegated Act
updates.detail: The Commission published in the OJ C series its fourth interpretative notice on the Disclosures Delegated Act under Article 8 of the EU Taxonomy Regulation, as amended by the Omnibus Delegated Act. It covers how undertakings should report Taxonomy-eligible and Taxonomy-aligned economic activities and assets under the simplified regime. The notice is the Commission's operational guidance for preparers applying Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73.
updates.so_what: Check your taxonomy KPI methodology against the fourth notice before finalising your next Article 8 disclosure.
updates.source_title: Commission Notice on the interpretation and implementation of certain legal provisions of the Disclosures Delegated Act under Article 8 of the EU Taxonomy Regulation (fourth notice)
updates.source_publisher: Official Journal of the European Union (C series)

updates.headline: SBTi revises the Absolute Contraction Approach, effective immediately
updates.detail: SBTi updated how annual reduction rates are calculated under the Absolute Contraction Approach, accounting for the interval between a company's base year and its net-zero target year so reductions are spread consistently across the full pathway to 2050. The minimum annual reduction rate floor of 4.2% between base year and target year is retained. The change applies to Corporate Net-Zero Standard V1.3.1 and Corporate Near-Term Criteria V5.3 and takes effect immediately for energy and industrial as well as FLAG targets, covering companies setting targets in 2026 and 2027, including first-time setters and those renewing at a mandatory five-year review.
updates.so_what: Rerun any 2026 or 2027 target model on the revised approach before submitting, since the required rate above the 4.2% floor may have moved.
updates.source_title: The SBTi updates the Absolute Contraction Approach to improve consistency and implementation, while maintaining net-zero ambition

updates.headline: GHG Protocol appoints Tim Mohin as its first Chief Executive Officer
updates.detail: GHG Protocol announced the appointment of Tim Mohin as its first CEO, effective 1 June 2026. The release notes that GHG Protocol and ISO have been mandated by the COP30 Presidency to lead global harmonisation of greenhouse gas accounting through the 2028 Global Stocktake, and that GHG Protocol established a Steering Committee and Independent Standards Board in 2024 and formalised partnerships with the ISSB and ISO.
updates.so_what: Expect the pace and formality of the revision programme to increase now that GHG Protocol has a dedicated executive and a 2028 mandate.
updates.source_title: RELEASE: Greenhouse Gas Protocol Appoints Tim Mohin as CEO, Marking New Phase in Global Standards Evolution

updates.headline: EFRAG submits its 2026 sustainability reporting work programme to the Commission
updates.detail: EFRAG's Sustainability Reporting Board approved and submitted the 2026 work programme. Priorities are the non-EU undertakings standard (N-ESRS / ESRS-40a) with an exposure draft in July 2026 and technical advice by early 2027, continued SME ecosystem and voluntary reporting support, implementation support, interoperability with ISSB, GRI and the GHG Protocol, and XBRL taxonomy and ESRS Knowledge Hub updates. Sector-specific standards are absent from the programme.
updates.so_what: Use EFRAG's interoperability workstream to justify a single global disclosure dataset rather than parallel EU and ISSB reporting builds.
updates.source_title: EFRAG submits its Sustainability Reporting Work Programme 2026 to the European Commission

updates.headline: ISSB decides nature requirements will be a Practice Statement, not a new Standard
updates.detail: At its April 2026 meeting in Beijing the ISSB unanimously decided to propose nature-related disclosure requirements as an IFRS Practice Statement complementing IFRS S1 and IFRS S2, rather than amending them or issuing a new Standard. Stakeholders will be asked to comment on the appropriateness of the Practice Statement format itself. The board also unanimously approved guidance on how asset and site locations relate to identifying nature-related risks, and required disclosure of the percentage of assets vulnerable to identified nature-related risks with a proportionality mechanism. Ten of 12 members agreed to provide guidance on engagement with Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities. Chair Emmanuel Faber said: 'Providing material nature-related disclosures is not optional; IFRS S1 already requires that.'
updates.so_what: Do not wait for a nature Standard — audit whether nature-related risks are already material under IFRS S1 in your current reporting.
updates.source_title: ISSB agrees on the proposed way forward for nature-related disclosures

updates.headline: ISO 14060 registered as a Draft International Standard
updates.detail: Following approval of the committee draft for DIS registration on 24 March 2026, ISO 14060 Net zero aligned organizations was registered as a DIS on 21 April 2026. The project had been approved on 27 May 2024 with the working draft study initiated on 6 September 2024. The DIS ballot subsequently opened on 17 June 2026.
updates.so_what: Note that the substance of ISO 14060 was locked at committee draft in March 2026, so consultation comments now change details rather than architecture.
updates.source_title: ISO/DIS 14060 - Net zero aligned organizations

updates.workstream: Product Standard / joint ISO-GHGP product-level standard
updates.headline: ISO and GHG Protocol finalise Joint Working Group for a product-level accounting standard
updates.detail: ISO and GHG Protocol confirmed the membership of their Joint Working Group to develop an updated, harmonised product-level GHG accounting standard, building on ISO 14067 and the GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard. More than 450 applicants from over 50 countries and 410 organisations were considered. The announcement frames the work as supporting value-chain transparency and mechanisms such as carbon border adjustment mechanisms, and flagged a public webinar for 24 April 2026. No completion date was given.
updates.so_what: Carry on with ISO 14067 based product footprints - there is no dated successor to wait for.
updates.source_title: ANNOUNCEMENT: ISO and GHG Protocol Finalize Joint Working Group to Develop Product-Level Accounting Standard

updates.headline: FSA publishes the English roadmap on sustainability disclosure and assurance
updates.detail: The Financial Services Agency published the report of the Financial System Council's Working Group on Disclosure and Assurance of Sustainability-related Financial Information together with the English version of the Japanese Roadmap on 9 April 2026. The roadmap phases mandatory SSBJ application across the TSE Prime Market by five-year average market capitalisation: ¥3 trillion and above from the fiscal year ending March 2027, ¥1-3 trillion from March 2028, and ¥500 billion to ¥1 trillion from March 2029. Mandatory assurance begins one year after each company's first mandatory application, limited to specified information for the first two years. A two-year transitional accommodation permits sustainability disclosures to be published after the financial statements.
updates.so_what: Japanese-listed groups above ¥3 trillion should be running a dry-run SSBJ report this year for the March 2027 year end.
updates.source_title: Japanese Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure and Assurance

updates.headline: SBTi publishes Corporate Net-Zero Standard V1.3.1 and Near-Term Criteria V5.3.1
updates.detail: SBTi issued Corporate Net-Zero Standard Version 1.3.1 and Corporate Near-Term Criteria Version 5.3.1, both dated April 2026, carrying the revised Absolute Contraction Approach. These remain the documents against which all target validations run through 2026 and are available for submissions until 31 January 2028.
updates.so_what: Confirm your submission is built against V1.3.1 and V5.3.1, not the earlier V1.3 and V5.3 editions.
updates.source_title: SBTi Corporate Near-Term Criteria, Version 5.3.1, April 2026

updates.headline: GHG Protocol opens a Request for Information on AMI, proposing multi-statement reporting
updates.detail: GHG Protocol published the Actions and Market Instruments Phase 1 White Paper and an explanatory memo, opening a 60-day Request for Information from 31 March to 31 May 2026. The white paper proposes a shift from a single physical inventory to four reporting components: physical inventory, market-based inventory, a GHG impact statement using consequential accounting, and non-GHG indicators. It covers virtual PPAs, green steel, chemicals and cement certificates, biomethane, sustainable aviation fuel and carbon credits.
updates.so_what: Read the AMI white paper before deciding how to present any certificate-backed low-carbon commodity claim.
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol Actions and Market Instruments Phase 1 White Paper (Request for Information)

updates.headline: GHG Protocol proposes a 95 percent Scope 3 boundary threshold and a new Category 16
updates.detail: GHG Protocol published its Scope 3 Standard Revisions Phase 1 Progress Update covering work from September 2024 to end-2025 across 42 Technical Working Group meetings. Series B proposes a prescriptive 95 percent inclusion threshold requiring companies to quantify total required scope 3 emissions to justify exclusions, and introduces a new Category 16 for facilitated activities. Series C narrows Category 15 to investment-related activities only. Series A adds requirements to disaggregate emissions by data type, disclose verification status, and restrict allocation of corporate-level supplier data to homogeneous suppliers. The document states all revisions remain under development and subject to change.
updates.so_what: Quantify your currently excluded scope 3 categories now so you can test whether you would clear a 95 percent threshold.
updates.source_title: Scope 3 Standard Revisions: Phase 1 Progress Update, March 2026

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation publishes its 2025 Annual Report, 'Fit for the future'
updates.detail: The IFRS Foundation published its 2025 Annual Report on 31 March 2026, reporting total comprehensive income of £1.3 million and reserves increased to £49.2 million, helped by cost-reduction initiatives and deferred technology spending. ISSB highlights for the year included supporting jurisdictions adopting IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, clarifying aspects of IFRS S2, continuing the SASB Standards enhancement work, and advancing research on Human Capital and Nature-related Disclosures. Trustees Chair Erkki Liikanen said 'IFRS Standards have become a global public good' while highlighting the need for transformational change.
updates.so_what: Use the annual report as the Foundation's own evidence base if you need to justify ISSB-aligned investment internally.
updates.source_title: IFRS Foundation publishes 2025 Annual Report—Fit for the future

updates.headline: SSBJ and ISSB confirm their standards remain aligned
updates.detail: The SSBJ and the ISSB jointly confirmed on 31 March 2026 that alignment between the SSBJ Standards and the ISSB Standards has been maintained following the SSBJ's March 2026 amendments. The SSBJ published an updated table of concordance and schedule of differences between the two sets of standards. This matters for groups that report under IFRS S1 and S2 elsewhere and want to reuse that reporting in Japan.
updates.so_what: Multinationals can continue to run one ISSB-based reporting process and map it into SSBJ rather than maintaining two.
updates.source_title: SSBJ and ISSB Confirm the Maintained Alignment between SSBJ Standards and ISSB Standards

updates.headline: ISSB proposes amendments to three further SASB Standards and IFRS S2 guidance
updates.detail: The ISSB published an Exposure Draft proposing amendments to the SASB Standards for Agricultural Products, Meat, Poultry & Dairy, and Electric Utilities & Power Generators, with consequential amendments to the Industry-based Guidance on Implementing IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures. The proposals aim to align language and concepts with ISSB Standards and improve international applicability and decision-usefulness. The comment deadline was 24 July 2026, a 120-day period. Vice-Chair Sue Lloyd noted 'The SASB Standards are the only complete set of industry-based disclosure standards available'.
updates.so_what: Agriculture, food and power reporters should compare the proposed metrics against what they currently disclose under IFRS S2 paragraph 32.
updates.source_title: ISSB seeks feedback on proposed amendments to three SASB Standards

updates.headline: CARB sets out the 10 August Scope 1-2 deadline and preliminary Scope 3 options
updates.detail: CARB held a virtual public workshop on 23 March 2026 giving staff's update on the then-current 10 August 2026 Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting deadline and preliminary options for Scope 3 reporting across 2027-2030. Staff confirmed that entities with fiscal years ending on or before 1 February 2026 would report FY25-26 data, that annual reporting starts in 2027, that limited assurance for Scope 1 and 2 commences in 2027, and that the statutory 2030 assurance step was not part of the initial rulemaking. Staff also referenced fee assessment on 10 September 2026.
updates.so_what: Fix which fiscal year of data your first California report covers, because it turns on your year-end date.
updates.source_title: SB 253 March 2026 Workshop Slides

updates.headline: FCA consultation CP26/5 on listed issuers' sustainability disclosures closes
updates.detail: The FCA's consultation on aligning listed issuers' sustainability disclosures with international standards closed on 20 March 2026, having opened on 30 January 2026. The FCA said it aims to finalise its rules and publish a policy statement in autumn 2026, contingent on the Government's final UK SRS publication and the feedback received. Until then the existing TCFD-aligned comply-or-explain listing rules remain in force.
updates.so_what: Diarise autumn 2026 for the FCA policy statement and hold your FY2027 reporting plan open until the final rules land.
updates.source_title: CP26/5: Aligning listed issuers' sustainability disclosures with international standards

updates.headline: Directive (EU) 2026/470 enters into force
updates.detail: The Omnibus I content directive entered into force on 18 March 2026, the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal. From this date the amended CSRD scope thresholds, the deletion of sector standards and reasonable assurance, and the value-chain cap empowerment are part of EU law. Member States have one year from entry into force to transpose the provisions, except Article 4 on the level of harmonisation, which they must comply with by 26 July 2028.
updates.so_what: Diarise 18 March 2027 as the national transposition date and start tracking each Member State's implementing law.
updates.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470
updates.source_publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

updates.headline: SSBJ amends three standards to reflect the ISSB's amendments to IFRS S2
updates.detail: The SSBJ amended its three Sustainability Disclosure Standards on 13 March 2026 as part of Amendments to Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosures, responding to the ISSB's own amendments to IFRS S2. The amendments cover the greenhouse gas emissions measurement and disclosure requirements. They apply to the Universal Standard and Theme-based Standards No. 1 and No. 2 issued in March 2025.
updates.so_what: Check whether your Japanese GHG measurement basis needs updating before your first SSBJ report rather than after.
updates.source_title: SSBJ Standards

updates.headline: EPA extends the reporting-year 2025 GHG reporting deadline to 30 October 2026
updates.detail: EPA issued a final rule, effective on publication at 91 FR 9712 on 27 February 2026, changing the reporting deadline for annual greenhouse gas reports for reporting year 2025 from 31 March 2026 to 30 October 2026. The rule addresses only the deadline; EPA said it will address the remainder of its September 2025 proposal, which would remove programme obligations for 46 source categories, in one or more subsequent final actions.
updates.so_what: Reschedule Part 98 submissions to October and check whether your source categories are on EPA's removal list.
updates.source_title: Extending the Reporting Deadline Under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Rule for 2025, 91 FR 9712

updates.headline: ISO and GHG Protocol launch joint public webinar series on harmonisation
updates.detail: ISO and GHG Protocol held the first of a joint webinar series on 26 February 2026 to explain their work to harmonise global carbon accounting standards under the COP Action Agenda, with a product-level session scheduled for April 2026 and further sessions through the year. ISO's Marco Rossi described the goal as one coherent set of definitions, datasets and language so that organisations need not navigate competing systems. Progress is intended to be demonstrated at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey.
updates.so_what: Use the joint webinar series as the primary official channel for tracking timeline changes between formal announcements.
updates.source_title: ISO and GHG Protocol launch webinars to advance global carbon accounting

updates.headline: ISSB ratifies the second SASB Exposure Draft and sets a 12-18 month effective date approach
updates.detail: At its 25-26 February 2026 meeting, 11 of 12 ISSB members approved ratification of the prospective Exposure Draft covering amendments to three SASB Standards, with a 120-day comment period and publication expected in March 2026. The ISSB decided the final amendments would become effective 12 to 18 months after issuance, with early application permitted. All 12 members confirmed due process compliance for consequential amendments to the Industry-based Guidance on Implementing IFRS S2, on the same effective-date timeline.
updates.so_what: Plan for as little as 12 months between final SASB amendments being issued and their effective date.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update February 2026

updates.headline: Omnibus I content directive published in the Official Journal as Directive (EU) 2026/470
updates.detail: The directive amending Directives 2006/43/EC, 2013/34/EU, (EU) 2022/2464 and (EU) 2024/1760 as regards certain corporate sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements was published in the Official Journal. It sets the CSRD scope at more than EUR 450 000 000 net turnover and an average of more than 1 000 employees, removes listed SMEs from scope, deletes the sector standards mandate and the reasonable assurance pathway, and creates the value-chain cap.
updates.so_what: Treat the OJ text, not the press releases, as the authority for your scope determination and board reporting.
updates.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470 - full OJ text

updates.headline: CARB approves the initial climate transparency regulation by Resolution 26-1
updates.detail: At its 26 February 2026 hearing the CARB Board approved for adoption sections 96070 to 96077 of Title 17 of the California Code of Regulations, establishing the fee programme, the key definitions for fee assessment and the reporting deadlines for SB 253 and SB 261 as amended by SB 219. The regulation set 10 August 2026 as SB 253's first-year Scope 1 and Scope 2 deadline, with Scope 3 beginning in 2027, and adopted a flat-rate fee structure. CARB announced that more than 120 climate-related financial risk reports had already been voluntarily submitted and that it would use enforcement discretion for good-faith first-year SB 253 submissions.
updates.so_what: Treat the regulation's definitions of covered entity, revenue and 'doing business in California' as the operative scoping test for your group.
updates.source_title: CARB approves climate transparency regulation for entities doing business in California

updates.headline: DBT publishes final UK SRS S1 and UK SRS S2
updates.detail: The Department for Business and Trade published the finalised UK Sustainability Reporting Standards, UK SRS S1 on general requirements and UK SRS S2 on climate-related disclosures, on 25 February 2026, together with the response to the consultation that ran from 25 June to 17 September 2025. The standards endorse the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards with a small number of UK amendments: the relief allowing sustainability information to be published separately from the financial statements in year one was removed, the climate-first relief was retained without a fixed time limit, the GICS classification requirement was dropped, and effective date clauses were deleted so that timing is set by regulation instead. The standards are available for voluntary use by any entity and impose no new mandatory obligations.
updates.so_what: Adopt UK SRS S2 voluntarily for FY2026 as a rehearsal — the standard will not change before the FCA mandates it.
updates.source_title: UK Sustainability Reporting Standards: UK SRS S1 and UK SRS S2

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation publishes a Jurisdictional Readiness Assessment Guide
updates.detail: The IFRS Foundation published a Jurisdictional Readiness Assessment Guide and accompanying tool as part of its Regulatory Implementation Programme, described as a toolkit of resources to support jurisdictions designing their journeys to use ISSB Standards. The guide helps jurisdictions determine the pace, scope and sequencing of regulatory action and identify capacity-building priorities, using practical examples from jurisdictions already implementing. The Foundation stated that nearly 40 jurisdictions have taken steps to adopt or use ISSB Standards and that requirements in 19 jurisdictions have already come into effect.
updates.so_what: Check whether any of the 19 live jurisdictions already captures a group entity you file for.
updates.source_title: Jurisdictional Readiness Assessment Guide and tool added to ISSB adoption toolkit

updates.headline: Council gives final sign-off to the Omnibus I simplification package
updates.detail: The Council formally adopted the directive simplifying sustainability reporting and due diligence, completing the legislative procedure begun in February 2025. The Council confirmed CSRD scope at more than 1,000 employees and above EUR 450 million turnover, third-country parent thresholds of EUR 450 million EU turnover with a EUR 200 million subsidiary or branch, CSDDD scope at more than 5,000 employees and EUR 1.5 billion turnover, removal of the climate transition plan obligation and the EU harmonised liability regime, and a penalty cap of 3% of net worldwide turnover.
updates.so_what: Close out any Omnibus scenario planning and move to a single post-Omnibus compliance baseline.
updates.source_title: Council signs off simplification of sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements to boost EU competitiveness

updates.headline: ISO 14064-5:2026 published, enabling remote verification of GHG statements
updates.detail: ISO published the first edition of ISO 14064-5:2026, Greenhouse gases - Part 5: Guidance on activities and techniques used remotely in conducting verification and validation of greenhouse gas statements, at stage 60.60. It applies where verifiers determine in-person site visits are unnecessary or validators can gather evidence remotely without compromising assessment quality, and permits fully remote or hybrid approaches.
updates.so_what: Raise remote and hybrid verification with your assurance provider at the next scoping meeting to cut site-visit cost.
updates.source_title: ISO 14064-5:2026 - Greenhouse gases - Part 5

updates.headline: GHG Protocol sets out its delivery plan for the COP30 harmonisation mandate
updates.detail: GHG Protocol published a letter from its Steering Committee Chair on delivering the COP30 Action Agenda mandate to harmonise carbon accounting. It was followed on 26 February 2026 by a published summary of the joint ISO-GHG Protocol webinar on harmonising global carbon accounting under the COP30 Action Agenda.
updates.so_what: Read the Steering Committee letter for the governance rationale behind the July 2026 consolidation decision.
updates.source_title: Delivering on the COP30 Action Agenda Mandate to Harmonise Carbon Accounting: Letter from GHG Protocol Steering Committee Chair

updates.headline: New York Senate passes the Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act, S9072A, 40-22
updates.detail: The New York State Senate passed S9072A, sponsored by Senator Pete Harckham, by 40 ayes to 22 on 10 February 2026 and referred it to the Assembly. The bill would require entities doing business in New York with total revenues over $1 billion in the preceding fiscal year to report Scope 1 and 2 emissions starting in 2028 and Scope 3 starting in 2029, with limited assurance from 2028 and reasonable assurance from 2032. It directs the department to adopt regulations on or before 31 December 2027 and requires a public-facing digital platform by 1 July 2028. The bill remains in the Assembly Codes Committee and has not been enacted.
updates.so_what: If you clear the $1bn California threshold, assume New York will catch you too and design one emissions ledger for both.
updates.source_title: NY State Senate Bill 2025-S9072A, Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act

updates.headline: FRC publishes updated Guidance on the Strategic Report
updates.detail: The Financial Reporting Council published an updated Guidance on the Strategic Report on 4 February 2026, revised to reflect changes to legislative and regulatory requirements and developments in sustainability-related and wider corporate reporting practice. The guidance is intended to help entities address reporting obligations in a way that is practical and proportionate. It is the FRC's principal non-mandatory reference for the narrative front half of a UK annual report, including the climate-related financial disclosures required by law.
updates.so_what: Re-read the strategic report guidance before the FY2026 drafting cycle — it is the reference the FRC's reviewers use.
updates.source_title: FRC publishes updated strategic report guidance

updates.headline: GHG Protocol closes its Scope 2 and consequential accounting consultations
updates.detail: The two public consultations opened on 20 October 2025 closed on 31 January 2026, having been extended from an original 19 December 2025 deadline. The Scope 2 consultation covered revisions to the 2015 Scope 2 Guidance including hourly matching, deliverability and a new location-based emission factor hierarchy. The parallel consultation covered consequential methods for estimating system-wide impacts of clean energy procurement, kept separate from inventory reporting.
updates.so_what: Note that the consulted text is not the final text - GHG Protocol has since said it is exploring multiple approaches.
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol Public Consultations

updates.workstream: Land Sector and Removals Standard and Guidance
updates.headline: GHG Protocol publishes its first global standard for land-sector emissions and removals
updates.detail: The Land Sector and Removals Standard was published on 30 January 2026, GHG Protocol's first global standard for corporate accounting of land-sector emissions and CO2 removals. It covers land management and land use change, CO2 removals stored in land and geologic carbon pools, and emissions from biogenic products and technological CO2 removal products across supply chains. It becomes effective on 1 January 2027, with accompanying FAQs, an executive summary, a reporting requirements checklist and sample inventory templates.
updates.so_what: Scope LSR data collection into your FY2027 inventory build now - this is the only dated requirement in the whole programme.
updates.source_title: RELEASE: GHG Protocol Launches Its First-Ever Global Standard for Corporate Accounting of Land-Sector Emissions and Removals

updates.headline: FCA opens CP26/5 proposing UK SRS-based rules for listed issuers from 2027
updates.detail: The FCA published CP26/5 on 30 January 2026, proposing to replace its TCFD-aligned listing rules with requirements based on UK SRS, in force from 1 January 2027 for accounting periods beginning on or after that date. UK SRS S2 would be mandatory except for Scope 3 emissions, which would be comply-or-explain with an optional one-year deferral; UK SRS S1 would be comply-or-explain with a two-year deferral for non-climate matters. Issuers would have to state whether and where they have published a climate transition plan, and whether they obtained third-party assurance, naming the provider, scope and standard. Assurance itself would not be mandatory.
updates.so_what: Build the Scope 3 inventory now — the deferral buys one year, not an exemption.
updates.source_title: Consultation Paper CP26/5: Aligning listed issuers' sustainability disclosures with international standards

updates.headline: DBT confirms a voluntary FRC-run register for sustainability assurance providers
updates.detail: DBT published its response to the consultation on developing an oversight regime for assurance of sustainability-related financial disclosures on 30 January 2026. Practitioners will be able to opt in by registering with the financial reporting regulator subject to meeting registration conditions, and the regime will be profession-agnostic so that statutory auditors, sustainability specialists and independent providers can all register. The FRC will operate it; the government confirmed it is not proceeding with the Audit Reform Bill, so ARGA will not be created. An interim non-legislative register was to be operational by mid-2026, with primary legislation to follow when parliamentary time allows. Over 80% of the 99 respondents supported the core proposal.
updates.so_what: Ask your assurance provider whether they will join the FRC interim register before you sign the next engagement letter.
updates.source_title: Developing an oversight regime for assurance of sustainability-related financial disclosures: government response to consultation

updates.headline: ISSB confirms an unrestricted scope for the nature standard-setting project
updates.detail: At its 28 January 2026 meeting the ISSB unanimously (12 of 12) agreed the nature project should address all material nature-related information that could reasonably be expected to affect an entity's prospects, rather than restricting the scope. It also agreed the new requirements would build on and supplement IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 rather than replace them. The board received a Transition Implementation Group update on IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 implementation but made no decisions on that item.
updates.so_what: Expect nature coverage broader than biodiversity alone — water, land use, ocean and pollution all fall inside the project scope.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update January 2026

updates.headline: Ninth Circuit sets merits argument in the SB 253 and SB 261 First Amendment appeal
updates.detail: The Ninth Circuit scheduled oral argument in Chamber of Commerce of the United States of America v. Sanchez, No. 25-5327, for 9 January 2026, by order of 30 October 2025. The merits panel had earlier been assigned the challengers' motion for an injunction pending appeal after a motions panel referred it on 23 October 2025. As at 25 August 2026 no merits opinion had been published on the Ninth Circuit's opinions page.
updates.so_what: Build in a decision-response plan: a ruling could reinstate SB 261 duties or vacate the California regime with little notice.
updates.source_title: Emergency Application for Injunction Pending Appeal, No. 25A561
updates.source_publisher: Supreme Court of the United States

updates.headline: Taxonomy simplification delegated act published as Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73
updates.detail: The Commission delegated regulation of 4 July 2025 was published in the Official Journal. It amends Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178 to simplify the content and presentation of Article 8 disclosures, and Delegated Regulations (EU) 2021/2139 and (EU) 2023/2486 to simplify technical screening criteria. Undertakings may omit assessing activities below 10% of a KPI denominator, may skip the OpEx KPI where immaterial, and the fossil gas and nuclear templates are deleted. Financial undertakings may opt out of full taxonomy reporting until 31 December 2027.
updates.so_what: Apply the 10% materiality filter and drop the deleted templates from your taxonomy reporting pack immediately.
updates.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73 of 4 July 2025
updates.source_publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

updates.headline: CBAM definitive regime begins; transitional reporting ends
updates.detail: CBAM became applicable under its definitive regime on 1 January 2026, ending the transitional reporting period that ran from October 2023 to 31 December 2025. The definitive regime introduces authorisation requirements for importers, the annual CBAM declaration and the purchase and surrender of CBAM certificates. Importers below the 50-tonne annual de minimis introduced by Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 are exempt from these obligations.
updates.so_what: If you import more than 50 tonnes of CBAM goods a year, secure authorised CBAM declarant status now.
updates.source_title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism

updates.headline: CARB leaves SB 261's 1 January first-report deadline unenforced
updates.detail: The statutory deadline for covered entities to publish their first climate-related financial risk report under Health and Safety Code section 38533 fell on 1 January 2026. Because of the Ninth Circuit injunction granted on 18 November 2025, CARB confirmed it would not enforce the requirement against covered entities for failing to post and submit by that date. CARB said it would provide further information, including an alternate reporting date as appropriate, after the appeal is resolved.
updates.so_what: Do not treat the missed 1 January date as a permanent reprieve - CARB has reserved the right to set a new mandatory date.
updates.source_title: SB 261 Enforcement Advisory

updates.headline: CARB posts the notice of public hearing, staff report and proposed regulation text
updates.detail: CARB posted its rulemaking materials for the climate disclosure initial regulation, including the Notice of Public Hearing dated 9 December 2025, the Staff Report: Initial Statement of Reasons and the proposed regulation text for Article 6, sections 96070-96077. The notice set the hearing for 26 February 2026 at 9:00am, a comment period from 26 December 2025 to 9 February 2026, and projected fee revenue of about $90.2 million over five years. The proposed text defined 'doing business in California' by reference to Revenue and Taxation Code section 23101(b)(1) or (b)(2) and 'revenue' as gross receipts under section 25120(f)(2).
updates.so_what: Run your revenue test on gross receipts, not net revenue, and on the lesser of the two prior fiscal years.
updates.source_title: Article 6: California Climate Disclosures - proposed regulation text

updates.headline: European Parliament adopts the Omnibus I compromise by 428 votes to 218
updates.detail: Parliament voted 428 in favour, 218 against and 17 abstentions to adopt the revised sustainability reporting and due diligence rules agreed with the Council. The text sets CSRD scope at more than 1,000 employees and more than EUR 450 million net turnover, restricts CSDDD to companies with more than 5,000 employees and EUR 1.5 billion turnover applying from 26 July 2029, makes sector-specific reporting voluntary, and protects suppliers with fewer than 1,000 employees from excessive information demands.
updates.so_what: Use the December 2025 vote as the point at which EU scope stopped moving and lock your scope assessment to it.
updates.source_title: Simplified sustainability reporting and due diligence rules for businesses

updates.headline: ISSB issues the first amendments to IFRS S2, effective 1 January 2027
updates.detail: The ISSB issued Amendments to Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosures (Amendments to IFRS S2), providing four targeted reliefs: entities may limit Scope 3 Category 15 measurement and disclosure to financed emissions; may use a classification system other than GICS for disaggregating financed emissions; may apply the jurisdictional relief from the GHG Protocol Standard where only part of the entity is required to use a different basis; and may use jurisdictionally mandated global warming potential values that are not from the latest IPCC Assessment Report. The amendments are effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027 with early application permitted. Consequential amendments to three SASB Standards were issued at the same time to align financed emissions metrics.
updates.so_what: Financial-sector reporters should reassess Scope 3 Category 15 scope immediately, since the relief can be taken early for FY2026.
updates.source_title: ISSB issues targeted amendments to IFRS S2 to support implementation

updates.headline: ISSB moves its nature project into standard-setting and skips the discussion paper
updates.detail: At its 10 December 2025 meeting the ISSB voted 11 of 12 to move the Biodiversity, Ecosystems and Ecosystem Services project from research into standard-setting, aiming to develop disclosure requirements responding to primary users' needs on nature-related risks and opportunities and building on IFRS S1 and IFRS S2. A further 11 of 12 agreed to proceed directly to an Exposure Draft rather than first publishing a discussion paper. All 12 agreed to use existing advisory structures rather than form a dedicated consultative group. The board also received a Human Capital project update without taking decisions.
updates.so_what: Skipping the discussion paper compresses the timeline — the first formal consultation on nature is the Exposure Draft itself.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update December 2025

updates.headline: Council and Parliament reach provisional agreement on Omnibus I
updates.detail: Negotiators struck a provisional deal on the CSRD and CSDDD simplification directive. Reporting is limited to companies with more than 1,000 employees and turnover above EUR 450 million, with EUR 450 million of EU turnover for non-EU companies. Due diligence is confined to companies with more than 5,000 employees and EUR 1.5 billion turnover, the business model transition plan requirement is removed and liability moves to national law with fines up to 3% of worldwide turnover. Reporting requirements become more quantitative and sector-specific reporting becomes voluntary.
updates.so_what: Note that Parliament's 1,750-employee demand did not survive - plan on the 1,000-employee test.
updates.source_title: Council and Parliament strike a deal to simplify sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements

updates.headline: EFRAG delivers technical advice on the simplified ESRS with a 61% datapoint cut
updates.detail: EFRAG submitted its technical advice on the draft simplified ESRS to the European Commission. It reports a 61% reduction in datapoints required if material and the elimination of all voluntary disclosures. Design changes include a streamlined materiality assessment with reduced documentation and better alignment with audit standards, a fair presentation filter, wider proportionality and phase-ins, and permission to use estimates for value-chain data. EFRAG also launched an ESRS Knowledge Hub.
updates.so_what: Use EFRAG's advice to identify which of your current ESRS datapoints will disappear before you invest further in collecting them.
updates.source_title: EFRAG provides its technical advice on draft simplified ESRS to the European Commission

updates.headline: GHG Protocol and ISO advance harmonisation at the ISO/TC 207 plenary
updates.detail: GHG Protocol reported on joint work with ISO at the 2025 ISO Environmental Management International Plenary, the annual meeting of ISO/TC 207 and its subcommittees. The plenary followed the September 2025 partnership announcement and the November 2025 COP30 Action Agenda mandate, and preceded the integration of ISO/TC 207/SC 7/WG4 members into GHG Protocol Technical Working Groups in Q1 2026.
updates.so_what: Note that the technical merger was agreed at committee level in late 2025, well before the public consolidation announcement.
updates.source_title: GHG Protocol and ISO Advance Global Harmonization at ISO Environmental Management International Plenary 2025

updates.headline: SBTi publishes Chemical Sector Pathways and Implementation Criteria Version 1.0
updates.detail: SBTi released Version 1.0 of the Chemical Sector Pathways and Implementation Criteria on 2 December 2025, with a six-month lead time before it became effective on 2 June 2026. The document states that companies shall adhere to the Corporate Net-Zero Standard and Corporate Near-Term Criteria except where explicitly superseded by the chemicals criteria.
updates.so_what: Chemicals groups should treat the sector criteria as an overlay on, not a replacement for, the cross-sector criteria.
updates.source_title: SBTi Chemical Sector Pathways and Implementation Criteria, Version 1.0

updates.headline: CARB opens the SB 261 docket and issues an enforcement advisory in light of the injunction
updates.detail: CARB opened its public docket for climate-related financial risk report links on 1 December 2025 and issued an enforcement advisory the same day. The advisory states that because of the Ninth Circuit's injunction CARB will not enforce Health and Safety Code section 38533 against covered entities for failing to post and submit reports by the 1 January 2026 statutory deadline, and that entities wishing to report voluntarily may do so through the docket. The docket page states submissions are accepted from 1 December 2025 through 31 December 2026.
updates.so_what: Decide deliberately whether to file voluntarily now or wait, and document the reasoning for your audit committee.
updates.source_title: Climate-Related Financial Risk Reports (SB 261) Docket

updates.headline: ISO/TS 14064-4:2025 published, replacing ISO/TR 14069:2013
updates.detail: ISO published the first edition of ISO/TS 14064-4:2025, Greenhouse gases - Part 4: Guidance for the application of ISO 14064-1, in November 2025 at stage 60.60. It replaces the withdrawn ISO/TR 14069:2013 and provides guidance on establishing organizational boundaries under a control approach (financial or operational) or an equity share approach, and on identifying and quantifying emission categories.
updates.so_what: If you report under ISO 14064-1, switch your boundary-setting reference from ISO/TR 14069 to ISO/TS 14064-4:2025.
updates.source_title: ISO/TS 14064-4:2025 - Greenhouse gases - Part 4: Guidance for the application of ISO 14064-1

updates.headline: QFMA makes IFRS S1 and S2 reporting mandatory for Main Market companies
updates.detail: The Qatar Financial Markets Authority published Guidance on Corporate Sustainability Reporting for Companies Listed on the Main Market on 23 November 2025, implementing the mandatory sustainability disclosure provision in the Governance Code for Listed Companies. Companies must apply IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 from financial year 2026, reported in 2027, with transition reliefs available in the first year including a climate-first option to report only under IFRS S2 initially. External assurance by the external auditor is mandatory, based on international standards including ISSA 5000. Companies may additionally use GRI or ESRS at their discretion provided this does not conflict with or obscure the ISSB requirements.
updates.so_what: Any Qatari Main Market subsidiary needs an IFRS S2-ready FY2026 dataset and an assurance engagement booked now.
updates.source_title: Guidance on Corporate Sustainability Reporting For Companies Listed on the Main Market

updates.headline: Chamber of Commerce withdraws its Supreme Court application in the California challenge
updates.detail: Application No. 25A561, Chamber of Commerce of the United States, et al. v. Lauren Sanchez, et al., was formally withdrawn on 19 November 2025 after applicants filed a withdrawal letter on 18 November 2025. The emergency application for an injunction pending appeal had been filed with Justice Kagan on 10 November 2025 and docketed on 14 November 2025, with an amicus brief from the State of Iowa. The withdrawal followed the Ninth Circuit's grant of an injunction against SB 261.
updates.so_what: Note that no Supreme Court merits engagement is pending - the action is entirely in the Ninth Circuit.
updates.source_title: Supreme Court docket, Chamber of Commerce v. Sanchez, No. 25A561
updates.source_publisher: Supreme Court of the United States

updates.headline: Ninth Circuit enjoins enforcement of SB 261 pending appeal; SB 253 unaffected
updates.detail: On 18 November 2025 the Ninth Circuit granted an injunction against the enforcement of SB 261 during the pendency of the appellate proceedings in Chamber of Commerce v. Sanchez. The court did not enjoin SB 253, leaving the greenhouse gas reporting obligation in force. CARB responded by announcing it would not enforce the 1 January 2026 SB 261 deadline and would set an alternate date after the appeal is resolved.
updates.so_what: Keep SB 253 work fully resourced - only the financial risk report was paused.
updates.source_title: Climate-Related Financial Risk Reports (SB 261) Docket

updates.headline: CARB concedes its preliminary covered-entity list has major holes
updates.detail: At its 18 November 2025 virtual public workshop CARB staff reviewed the preliminary list of reporting and covered entities built from California Secretary of State data and a proprietary dataset, acknowledging that the list has 'major holes' with several major companies missing and that revenue estimates are imprecise. Staff presented programme costs of about $13.9 million annually plus a one-time set-up cost of about $20.7 million temporarily funded through a loan, with per-entity fees derived by dividing annual programme cost by the number of regulated entities. Staff confirmed the SB 261 deadline of 1 January 2026, the SB 253 Scope 1 and 2 deadline of 10 August 2026, a fee assessment date of 10 September 2026, and that limited assurance was not required for 2026 data submission.
updates.so_what: Do your own scoping assessment - absence from CARB's preliminary list is not evidence you are out of scope.
updates.source_title: SB 253/261/219 Public Workshop: Update on California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting

updates.headline: CARB updates its climate disclosure FAQs and publishes an SB 261 report checklist
updates.detail: CARB updated its FAQs Regarding California Climate Disclosure Requirements and its Climate Related Financial Risk Report Checklist on 17 November 2025. The FAQs set out the 'doing business in California' test, including in-state sales exceeding $735,019 for 2024 or 25 per cent of total sales, the gross receipts revenue definition, parent-subsidiary consolidated reporting with subsidiaries remaining individually responsible, and that foreign parents may file consolidated reports for their US subsidiaries. The checklist confirms an SB 261 report may follow the TCFD June 2017 recommendations, IFRS S2 or an equivalent report required by law or a regulated exchange, must be posted on the entity's own website and its link lodged with CARB.
updates.so_what: A UK parent can file one consolidated report covering its US subsidiaries, but each subsidiary stays individually on the hook and is separately fee-assessed.
updates.source_title: FAQs Regarding California Climate Disclosure Requirements

updates.headline: Parliament adopts a negotiating position demanding a 1,750-employee CSRD threshold
updates.detail: Parliament adopted its negotiating mandate by 382 votes to 249 with 13 abstentions. MEPs wanted sustainability reporting limited to businesses with more than 1,750 employees on average and net turnover above EUR 450 million, due diligence limited to companies with more than 5,000 employees and EUR 1.5 billion turnover, Paris-aligned transition plans dropped, liability moved to national level, sector reporting made voluntary, and information requests to smaller partners permitted only as a last resort. It also proposed a digital portal with free templates.
updates.so_what: Treat the 1,750 figure as historical - it was Parliament's opening position, not the law.
updates.source_title: Sustainability reporting and due diligence: MEPs back simplification changes

updates.headline: COP30 Action Agenda mandates GHG Protocol and ISO to lead carbon accounting harmonisation
updates.detail: At COP30 in Belem, GHG Protocol and ISO welcomed the COP30 Action Agenda's call to accelerate carbon accounting solutions with the goal of delivering accelerated quantified emissions reductions by 2030. The two organisations committed to establishing the standards infrastructure required for harmonised emissions reporting, functioning carbon markets and interoperable regulation by 2028, covering consistent frameworks across product, entity and project accounting.
updates.so_what: Anchor your standards-change planning on the 2028 COP30 deadline, which is what the Q4 2028 publication target is built around.
updates.source_title: ANNOUNCEMENT: GHG Protocol and ISO Welcome COP30 Action Agenda to Harmonize Carbon Accounting

updates.headline: SBTi releases the second consultation draft of Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2
updates.detail: SBTi published the second draft of Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2 for public consultation, running from 6 November to 12 December 2025, with the deadline extended to allow adequate review. The draft retained separate scope 1 and scope 2 requirements, offered flexible pathways rather than one-size-fits-all rules, introduced a recognition mechanism for early voluntary action on ongoing emissions and required validated companies to publish transition plans linking near-term actions to long-term objectives.
updates.so_what: Compare your consultation response against the final text to see which of your concerns were accepted.
updates.source_title: SBTi releases second draft corporate net-zero standard V2 for consultation

updates.headline: ISSB agrees to draw on the TNFD framework for nature-related disclosure work
updates.detail: At its 6 November 2025 meeting the ISSB agreed unanimously among the 11 members present to draw on the TNFD framework to meet primary users' common information needs on nature-related risks and opportunities, building on existing IFRS S1 requirements. All 11 members voted to proceed with developing new disclosure requirements addressing nature-related matters not currently covered by IFRS S1 and IFRS S2. Ten of 11 approved creating educational materials to help entities apply the Standards when reporting nature-specific information.
updates.so_what: Existing TNFD-aligned reporting is the best head start available for whatever the ISSB proposes on nature.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update November 2025

updates.headline: FSA publishes its interim report and roadmap on sustainability disclosure and assurance
updates.detail: The Financial Services Agency published the interim report of the Financial System Council's Working Group on Disclosure and Assurance of Sustainability-related Financial Information, together with a roadmap for sustainability disclosures and assurance in Japan, on 6 November 2025. The interim report was issued in Japanese with the roadmap available in English. It set out the phased mandatory application of SSBJ Standards across the TSE Prime Market and the accompanying assurance timetable, later confirmed in the final report of April 2026.
updates.so_what: Use the November 2025 roadmap and its April 2026 successor together — the phasing thresholds did not change between them.
updates.source_title: Publication of Interim Report of the Working Group on Disclosure and Assurance of Sustainability-related Financial Information and Roadmap for sustainability disclosures and assurance in Japan

updates.workstream: Product Standard / joint ISO-GHGP product-level standard
updates.headline: ISO and GHG Protocol announce a jointly developed product-level GHG accounting standard
updates.detail: ISO and GHG Protocol announced they would jointly develop a new product-level GHG accounting standard and issued a call for experts to join the joint working group. The work builds on ISO 14067 and the GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard. Membership was finalised on 9 April 2026.
updates.so_what: Register interest in product-level developments if you publish product carbon footprints or face carbon border adjustment.
updates.source_title: ANNOUNCEMENT: ISO-GHG Protocol to Jointly Develop New Product-Level GHG Accounting Standard

updates.headline: GHG Protocol opens consultations on Scope 2 and consequential accounting
updates.detail: GHG Protocol opened two public consultations on 20 October 2025. The Scope 2 consultation proposed retaining both location-based and market-based methods while requiring market-based claims to align with the time and location of consumption through hourly and geographic matching, with load-profile approximation of hourly data, exemption thresholds for smaller organisations, legacy clauses for existing long-term contracts and a multi-year phased implementation. It also proposed a new emission factor hierarchy for the location-based method. The parallel consultation covered consequential accounting for system-wide impacts of clean energy procurement, deliberately kept outside the corporate inventory.
updates.so_what: Review the consultation document to understand the shape of hourly matching before signing any long-dated electricity contract.
updates.source_title: RELEASE: GHG Protocol Opens Public Consultations on Scope 2 and Electricity Sector Consequential Accounting

updates.headline: CBAM simplification regulation published and enters into force
updates.detail: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 of 8 October 2025 amending the CBAM Regulation was officially published and entered into force on 20 October 2025. It introduces a 50-tonne annual de minimis threshold that exempts approximately 182,000 importers, mostly SMEs and individuals, while still covering more than 99% of emissions in scope. It also simplifies declarant authorisation, emissions calculation and financial liability, and reduces the quarterly certificate holding requirement to 50% of embedded emissions.
updates.so_what: Re-run your import tonnage against the 50-tonne threshold before assuming you are still in CBAM scope.
updates.source_title: Officially published: Simplifications for the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)

updates.headline: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 signed, moving the first CBAM declaration to 30 September 2027
updates.detail: The regulation amending Regulation (EU) 2023/956 was signed by Parliament and Council. It provides that by 30 September of each year, and for the first time in 2027 for the year 2026, each authorised CBAM declarant must submit a CBAM declaration for the preceding calendar year and surrender the corresponding certificates. Member States begin selling CBAM certificates on a common central platform from 1 February 2027.
updates.so_what: Build your CBAM data collection to a 30 September 2027 deadline for 2026 imports, not the original 31 May date.
updates.source_title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/956
updates.source_publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

updates.headline: Council signs off the CBAM simplification
updates.detail: The Council formally adopted the regulation simplifying the carbon border adjustment mechanism, following the provisional agreement with Parliament reached on 18 June 2025 and the Council's negotiating position of 27 May 2025. The package centres on the new mass-based de minimis threshold and administrative simplifications for authorised CBAM declarants ahead of the definitive regime starting on 1 January 2026.
updates.so_what: Confirm your CBAM registry authorisation status now that the simplified rules are settled.
updates.source_title: CBAM: Council signs off simplification to the EU carbon leakage instrument

updates.headline: ISSB membership updates confirm the board will shrink from 14 to 10 members by end-2028
updates.detail: The IFRS Foundation announced reappointments of Sue Lloyd as Vice-Chair for a second four-year term effective 1 March 2026, Elizabeth Seeger for a second five-year term effective 1 October 2025, and Hiroshi Komori for a second one-year term effective 1 October 2025. Michael Jantzi and Tae-Young Paik stepped down with terms ending 30 September 2025, with Paik becoming Senior Advisor to the ISSB Chair for one year. The ISSB will gradually transition from 14 to 10 members by the end of 2028, a plan the Trustees announced in June 2025, while maintaining geographical balance.
updates.so_what: No action required, but a smaller board means a narrower work plan — expect the ISSB to keep prioritising implementation over new Standards.
updates.source_title: IFRS Foundation announces updates to inaugural ISSB membership

updates.headline: ISSB tentatively finalises the IFRS S2 GHG reliefs and sets a 1 January 2027 effective date
updates.detail: At its 24-26 September 2025 meeting the ISSB tentatively agreed the substance of the IFRS S2 greenhouse gas amendments. It finalised relief from measuring Scope 3 Category 15 emissions beyond financed emissions, with a requirement to describe the excluded financial activities including derivatives; replaced the prescriptive GICS hierarchy with a flexible approach requiring a commonly used classification system; and extended jurisdictional relief for alternative measurement methods and global warming potential values. The effective date was set at 1 January 2027 with early application permitted. Twelve of the 14 members present supported all decisions with no dissent indicated.
updates.so_what: This meeting is where the final relief wording was fixed — read it alongside the December 2025 text if you need the ISSB's reasoning.
updates.source_title: ISSB Update September 2025

updates.headline: CARB publishes a preliminary list of SB 253 and SB 261 reporting and covered entities
updates.detail: CARB published a preliminary list of reporting and covered entities on 24 September 2025 as a spreadsheet on its climate disclosure resources page. The list was compiled from California Secretary of State data and a proprietary dataset. CARB staff later acknowledged the list is materially incomplete.
updates.so_what: Check whether your California-registered entities appear, but scope yourself against the statutory tests regardless.
updates.source_title: Climate Disclosure Resources - Preliminary List of Reporting/Covered Entities

updates.headline: UK consultations on UK SRS exposure drafts and transition plan requirements close
updates.detail: The DBT consultation on the exposure drafts of UK SRS S1 and S2 and the DESNZ consultation on climate-related transition plan requirements both closed at 11:59pm on 17 September 2025, having opened on 25 June 2025. The UK SRS consultation produced a government response and final standards on 25 February 2026. As at 25 August 2026 the transition plan consultation response has not been published and the government's page still states it is analysing feedback.
updates.so_what: Track the transition plan outcome separately from UK SRS — the two consultations ran together but only one has been answered.
updates.source_title: Climate-related transition plan requirements
updates.source_publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

updates.headline: EPA publishes its proposal to end most of the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program
updates.detail: EPA's Reconsideration of the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program proposal was published in the Federal Register on 16 September 2025, four days after EPA announced it. The proposal would permanently remove programme obligations for 46 source categories, retaining reporting only for facilities subject to the Waste Emissions Charge under Clean Air Act section 136. EPA estimated savings of up to $2.4 billion in regulatory costs.
updates.so_what: Plan for the possibility that EPA facility data disappears as a cross-check on your US Scope 1 inventory.
updates.source_title: EPA Releases Proposal to End the Burdensome, Costly Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program

updates.headline: Eighth Circuit holds the SEC climate rule petitions in abeyance
updates.detail: On 12 September 2025 the Eighth Circuit issued an order holding the consolidated petitions for review of the SEC's climate-related disclosure rules in abeyance until such time as the Commission reconsiders the challenged rules by notice-and-comment rulemaking or renews its defence of them. The lead case is State of Iowa v. Securities and Exchange Commission, No. 24-1522. The order effectively froze the litigation and set up the Commission's May 2026 rescission proposal.
updates.so_what: Expect no judicial resolution of the SEC rules - their fate is now a rulemaking question, not a litigation one.
updates.source_title: Fact Sheet: Rescission of Climate-Related Disclosure Rules

updates.headline: District court denies an injunction pending appeal in the California climate challenge
updates.detail: On 11 September 2025 the Central District of California denied the challengers' motion for an injunction pending appeal in Chamber of Commerce of the United States of America v. California Air Resources Board, No. 2:24-cv-00801. This followed the court's 13 August 2025 denial of a preliminary injunction. The challengers then sought relief in the Ninth Circuit, filing an injunction motion on 16 September 2025.
updates.so_what: Note that no court has yet found the California laws unconstitutional on the merits.
updates.source_title: Emergency Application for Injunction Pending Appeal, No. 25A561
updates.source_publisher: Supreme Court of the United States

updates.headline: ISO and GHG Protocol announce strategic partnership to deliver unified global standards
updates.detail: ISO and GHG Protocol announced a strategic partnership to harmonise existing GHG standards and co-develop new ones, combining the ISO 1406X family with the GHG Protocol Corporate, Scope 2 and Scope 3 standards and a new joint product carbon footprint standard. ISO Secretary-General Sergio Mujica called it a new era for the carbon accounting landscape, and GHG Protocol Steering Committee Chair Geraldine Matchett said the partnership establishes a new mechanism for long-term collaboration. The announcement was backed by the ISSB, the B7 community and COP30 leadership.
updates.so_what: Stop planning for permanently divergent GHG Protocol and ISO 14064-1 reporting workflows.
updates.source_title: ISO and GHG Protocol announce strategic partnership to deliver unified global standards for greenhouse gas emissions accounting

updates.headline: SBTi issues Corporate Near-Term Criteria Version 5.3
updates.detail: SBTi published Version 5.3 of the Corporate Near-Term Criteria dated September 2025, the edition that governed near-term target validations until the April 2026 V5.3.1 revision incorporating the updated Absolute Contraction Approach.
updates.so_what: Check the version stamp on any near-term criteria document held in your evidence pack, as V5.3 has been superseded.
updates.source_title: SBTi Corporate Near-Term Criteria, Version 5.3, September 2025

updates.headline: ACRA and SGX RegCo defer most Singapore climate reporting requirements
updates.detail: ACRA and SGX RegCo announced on 25 August 2025 that most climate reporting requirements would be deferred to help companies build capability. Scope 1 and 2 emissions reporting remains mandatory for all listed issuers from FY2025, but other ISSB-based climate disclosures were deferred to FY2028 for non-STI issuers with market capitalisation of S$1bn or more and to FY2030 for those below S$1bn, with STI constituents unchanged at FY2025. Scope 3 remains mandatory only for STI constituents from FY2026 and voluntary for everyone else. External limited assurance was deferred to FY2029 for listed issuers. For large non-listed companies, ISSB-based climate disclosures including Scope 1 and 2 were deferred to FY2030 and assurance to FY2032.
updates.so_what: Singapore-listed subsidiaries outside the STI now only need Scope 1 and 2 for FY2025 — reallocate effort to jurisdictions with harder deadlines.
updates.source_title: Extended Timelines for Most Climate Reporting Requirements to Support Companies

updates.headline: CARB sets out the draft fee regulation and covered entity definitions
updates.detail: CARB held a virtual public workshop on 21 August 2025 on the draft framework for a fee regulation under Health and Safety Code sections 38532 and 38533. It covered definitions for covered entities including revenue, doing business in California and parent-subsidiary relationships, the regulatory development timeline, assurance requirements and minimum Scope 3 reporting requirements. CARB estimated the number of regulated entities using California Secretary of State data and a proprietary dataset.
updates.so_what: Map your group structure against CARB's parent-subsidiary definitions before the fee notice lands.
updates.source_title: SB 253/261/219 Public Workshop: Regulation Development and Additional Guidance

updates.headline: District court denies a preliminary injunction against SB 253 and SB 261
updates.detail: On 13 August 2025 the United States District Court for the Central District of California denied the challengers' motion for a preliminary injunction against SB 253 and SB 261 in Chamber of Commerce of the United States of America v. California Air Resources Board, No. 2:24-cv-00801. The challenge is framed as compelled speech under the First Amendment. The appeal was docketed in the Ninth Circuit as No. 25-5327 on 21 August 2025.
updates.so_what: Proceed on the basis that both California laws are presumptively valid until an appellate court says otherwise.
updates.source_title: Emergency Application for Injunction Pending Appeal, No. 25A561
updates.source_publisher: Supreme Court of the United States

updates.headline: GHG Protocol approves Scope 2 revisions for consultation, rejects Marginal Impact Method
updates.detail: GHG Protocol reported that on 14 July 2025 the Independent Standards Board voted to approve the location-based and market-based method revisions for public consultation, by 10 votes to 1 on each. The Board declined to advance the proposed Marginal Impact Method in its current form by 7 votes to 4, while affirming the importance of consequential accounting for avoided emissions and directing that work to the cross-sectoral Actions and Market Instruments workstream rather than Scope 2.
updates.so_what: Do not build avoided-emissions claims into your scope 2 reporting - that work moved to the AMI workstream and will not land before 2028.
updates.source_title: Scope 2 Standard Advances: ISB Approves Consultation on Market- and Location-Based Revisions; Signals Cross-Sectoral Work Ahead on Avoided Emissions

updates.headline: HKFRS S1 and HKFRS S2 take effect in Hong Kong
updates.detail: The HKFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, issued by the HKICPA on 12 December 2024 and fully aligned with the ISSB Standards, became effective on 1 August 2025. HKEX treats reports prepared under IFRS S1 and S2, or their HKFRS equivalents, as complying with its new climate requirements in Part D of Appendix C2. The Government's roadmap targets full ISSB adoption by large publicly accountable entities by 2028.
updates.so_what: Hong Kong issuers already reporting under IFRS S1/S2 can rely on that to satisfy HKEX's climate requirements without a separate exercise.
updates.source_title: HKICPA publishes HKFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards

updates.headline: EFRAG publishes revised ESRS exposure drafts and opens a 60-day consultation
updates.detail: EFRAG released 12 revised exposure drafts covering ESRS 1 and 2, E1 to E5, S1 to S4 and G1, with a consultation running from 31 July to 29 September 2025. At exposure draft stage EFRAG reported mandatory datapoints cut by 57%, the full set of mandatory and voluntary disclosures reduced by 68%, and the standards shortened by more than 55%. Final technical advice was targeted for 30 November 2025.
updates.so_what: Compare the exposure draft reductions with the final act to see which datapoints were reinstated.
updates.source_title: EFRAG shares revised ESRS Exposure Drafts and launches 60-day public consultation

updates.headline: Commission publishes the VSME voluntary standard as Recommendation (EU) 2025/1710
