updates.detail: The Commission adopted a recommendation presenting the voluntary sustainability reporting standard for non-listed micro, small and medium-sized undertakings, based on EFRAG's VSME. It is intended to give smaller companies a single proportionate framework for responding to data requests from banks, investors and large customers. Directive (EU) 2026/470 later required the Commission to convert it into a binding value-chain cap via delegated act under the new Article 29ca.
updates.so_what: Adopt VSME as your standard supplier data request format so you are already aligned when the cap becomes binding.
updates.source_title: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2025/1710 on a voluntary sustainability reporting standard for non-listed micro-, small- and medium-sized undertakings
updates.source_publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

updates.headline: SEC tells the Eighth Circuit it has no intention of revisiting the climate rules
updates.detail: Responding to the Eighth Circuit's 24 April 2025 direction, the SEC filed a status report on 23 July 2025 stating it had no intention of revisiting the climate-related disclosure rules at that time. The Commission declined to say whether it would adhere to the rules if the petitions for review were denied. The court had specifically asked whether the Commission intended to review or reconsider the rules.
updates.so_what: Treat the SEC's ambiguity in 2025 as the precursor to the 2026 rescission proposal, not as a signal the rules would revive.
updates.source_title: Statement on the Commission's Status Report in the Climate-Related Disclosure Rules Litigation

updates.headline: SBTi launches the Financial Institutions Net-Zero Standard
updates.detail: SBTi opened its net-zero standard for the finance industry, covering banks, asset owners and managers, private equity firms and other financial institutions across lending, investment, insurance and capital markets activities. The standard requires clear steps and timelines for ceasing new financial activities and insurance services to the fossil fuel industry, and requires institutions to assess and monitor portfolio deforestation exposure with engagement plans for significant risks. Institutions may focus on portfolio alignment with net-zero for their customers as an alternative to financed emissions reduction pathways. Nearly 135 financial institutions across six continents had already committed.
updates.so_what: UK financial institutions must decide between the FI Near-Term Criteria and FINZ before the July 2027 dual-route window closes.
updates.source_title: The SBTi opens net-zero standard for finance industry

updates.headline: Commission adopts the ESRS 'quick fix' for wave-one reporters
updates.detail: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1416 amended the ESRS delegated act so that wave-one companies face no additional information requirements for financial years 2025 and 2026 compared with 2024. They may continue omitting information on anticipated financial effects of certain sustainability-related risks, and those with more than 750 employees receive most of the phase-ins otherwise reserved for undertakings with up to 750 employees. The quick fix was needed because stop-the-clock gave wave-one companies no relief.
updates.so_what: Wave-one reporters should apply the quick-fix phase-ins to FY2026 statements rather than expanding disclosure voluntarily.
updates.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1416 of 11 July 2025
updates.source_publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

updates.headline: Commission adopts the EU Taxonomy simplification delegated act
updates.detail: The Commission adopted a delegated act amending the Taxonomy Disclosures, Climate and Environmental Delegated Acts to simplify application of the EU Taxonomy. The Commission stated the measures would apply as of 1 January 2026 and cover the 2025 financial year, with undertakings able to opt to begin in the 2026 financial year instead. The act was later published as Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73 on 8 January 2026 after the scrutiny period.
updates.so_what: Decide whether to apply the simplified taxonomy rules from FY2025 or defer to FY2026 and disclose the choice.
updates.source_title: Commission to cut EU taxonomy red tape for companies

updates.headline: ISSB opens the first comprehensive consultation on SASB Standards content
updates.detail: The ISSB published two Exposure Drafts proposing a comprehensive review of the SASB Standards for 9 industries — all 8 in the Extractives & Minerals Processing sector plus Processed Foods — and targeted amendments to 41 further industries on topics including Water Management and Workforce Health & Safety. Consequential updates were proposed to the Industry-based Guidance on Implementing IFRS S2 for 9 prioritised industries and 37 of the 41 others. The comment deadline was 30 November 2025, a 150-day period. Vice-Chair Sue Lloyd called it 'the first noteworthy opportunity to weigh in comprehensively on the content of the SASB Standards in the context of the ISSB Standards'.
updates.so_what: Check whether your industry sits in the 50 Standards covered, because SASB-derived metrics feed directly into IFRS S2 reporting.
updates.source_title: ISSB proposes comprehensive review of priority SASB Standards and targeted amendments to others

updates.headline: UK publishes UK SRS exposure drafts alongside transition plan and assurance consultations
updates.detail: On 25 June 2025 the UK government published exposure drafts of UK SRS S1 and UK SRS S2 for consultation, together with a DESNZ consultation on climate-related transition plan requirements and a DBT consultation on developing an oversight regime for assurance of sustainability-related financial disclosures. The transition plan consultation set out two implementation routes: requiring entities to explain why they have not disclosed a transition plan, or requiring them to develop and disclose one, potentially as a standalone document refreshed at least every three years. Scope centred on UK-regulated financial institutions and FTSE 100 companies, with the government considering widening it to economically significant entities while excluding SMEs. All three consultations closed on 17 September 2025.
updates.so_what: The three June 2025 consultations are the origin of every UK obligation now landing — read them together rather than in isolation.
updates.source_title: Exposure drafts: UK Sustainability Reporting Standards

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation publishes non-mandatory guidance on climate transition plan disclosures
updates.detail: The IFRS Foundation published 'Disclosing information about an entity's climate-related transition, including information about transition plans, in accordance with IFRS S2'. The document explicitly does not add to or change the requirements in IFRS S2. It builds on materials developed by the Transition Plan Taskforce, for which the IFRS Foundation assumed responsibility in 2024, tailored for global application and informed by stakeholder roundtables held in February and March 2025. IFRS S2 does not require an entity to have a transition plan, but requires disclosure of material information about climate-related risks and opportunities, covering both mitigation and adaptation.
updates.so_what: Use this guidance to structure transition plan narrative under IFRS S2 without assuming a transition plan is itself mandatory.
updates.source_title: IFRS Foundation publishes guidance on disclosures about transition plans

updates.headline: Council agrees its negotiating position on the Omnibus I content directive
updates.detail: The Council adopted its mandate for negotiations with Parliament on simplifying sustainability reporting and due diligence. Its position proposed limiting CSRD to undertakings with more than 1,000 employees and turnover above EUR 450 million and confining CSDDD to the largest companies. These were the thresholds that ultimately survived trilogue and appear in Directive (EU) 2026/470.
updates.so_what: The Council mandate was the best early predictor of the final thresholds - track Council positions closely in future files.
updates.source_title: Simplification: Council agrees position on sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements

updates.headline: Council and Parliament strike a deal on CBAM simplification
updates.detail: Negotiators reached provisional agreement on simplifying CBAM, centred on the new mass-based de minimis threshold for occasional importers and administrative simplifications to authorisation, emissions calculation and financial liability. The agreement was formally signed off by the Council on 29 September 2025 and published as Regulation (EU) 2025/2083.
updates.so_what: Small and occasional importers should have re-tested CBAM applicability from this point rather than assuming continued obligations.
updates.source_title: Carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM): Council and Parliament strike a deal on its simplification

updates.headline: SBTi consults on a draft Automotive Sector Net-Zero Standard
updates.detail: SBTi opened a 60-day public consultation on a draft standard for the automotive sector, running 12 June to 11 August 2025. The draft applies to automakers producing over 10,000 vehicles annually and to parts manufacturers earning at least 20% of revenue from automotive components, covering scopes 1, 2 and 3. It builds on the March 2024 Land Transport Guidance and adds a new aggregated cross-scope indicator, regional emissions pathways and an enhanced well-to-wheel methodology with default data inputs.
updates.so_what: Automotive suppliers should test whether the 20% revenue threshold pulls them into sector criteria.
updates.source_title: SBTi Opens Consultation on New Standard to Accelerate Automotive Industry's Net-Zero Transition

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation publishes its first jurisdictional profiles on ISSB Standards adoption
updates.detail: The IFRS Foundation published 17 jurisdictional profiles complemented by 16 snapshots, covering Australia, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Ghana, Hong Kong SAR, Jordan, Kenya, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Chinese Taipei, Tanzania, Türkiye and Zambia. It reported that 36 jurisdictions had adopted, were using, or were finalising steps towards adopting ISSB Standards. Of the 17 profiled, 14 target full adoption, 2 target only climate-related requirements and 1 targets partial incorporation. Among the 16 snapshot jurisdictions, 12 proposed standards fully or functionally aligned with ISSB Standards including Canada and Japan.
updates.so_what: Replace third-party adoption trackers with these profiles as your primary source for jurisdictional scope decisions.
updates.source_title: IFRS Foundation publishes jurisdictional profiles providing transparency and evidencing progress towards adoption of ISSB Standards

updates.headline: SBTi publishes Buildings Sector Criteria Version 1.1
updates.detail: SBTi issued Version 1.1 of the Buildings Sector Science-Based Target-Setting Criteria in June 2025, the edition in force until Version 1.2 replaced it in July 2026. Accompanying Buildings Criteria FAQs were subsequently updated to Version 1.2 in February 2026.
updates.so_what: Property portfolios validated against Version 1.1 should check what Version 1.2 changed before their next review.
updates.source_title: Buildings Sector Science-Based Target-Setting Criteria, Version 1.1, June 2025

updates.headline: ADX publishes updated voluntary ESG disclosure guidance recommending IFRS S1 and S2
updates.detail: The Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange published ESG Disclosure Guidance for Listed Companies in June 2025, setting out 38 ESG metrics across environmental, social, governance and integrated KPI categories. The guide is explicitly voluntary and recommends alignment with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards S1 and S2 and with GRI. It complements the SCA Corporate Governance Code, which incorporates sustainability disclosure requirements for listed companies. Third-party assurance is described as optional.
updates.so_what: For UAE listings, use the ADX 38-metric set as the floor and IFRS S2 as the target — the mandatory layer names neither.
updates.source_title: ESG Disclosure Guidance for Listed Companies

updates.headline: Council agrees negotiating position on CBAM simplification
updates.detail: The Council adopted its mandate for negotiations on the Commission's February 2025 CBAM simplification proposal. The core element was replacing the previous EUR 150 value-based de minimis with a single mass-based threshold designed to exclude occasional and small importers while retaining coverage of the overwhelming majority of embedded emissions.
updates.so_what: Note that the exemption test changed from a value basis to a mass basis - recalculate against tonnes, not euros.
updates.source_title: Simplifying EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism: Council agrees negotiating position

updates.headline: ISSB publishes Exposure Draft proposing targeted IFRS S2 greenhouse gas reliefs
updates.detail: The ISSB published an Exposure Draft proposing four targeted reliefs to IFRS S2: removing the need to measure and disclose Scope 3 Category 15 emissions tied to derivatives and certain financial activities; allowing alternatives to GICS when disaggregating financed emissions; clarifying jurisdictional authority to permit alternatives to the GHG Protocol for measuring emissions; and permitting jurisdiction-mandated global warming potential values that are not from the latest IPCC assessment. The comment deadline was 27 June 2025, a 60-day period, with the ISSB aiming to finalise the amendments by the end of 2025.
updates.so_what: This is the source document for the Basis for Conclusions if you need to argue how a relief applies to your facts.
updates.source_title: ISSB publishes Exposure Draft proposing targeted amendments to IFRS S2 to ease application for companies

updates.headline: CSA pauses work on a mandatory Canadian climate-related disclosure rule
updates.detail: The Canadian Securities Administrators announced on 23 April 2025 that it was pausing work on developing a mandatory climate-related disclosure rule, and on its diversity-related disclosure project, citing increased uncertainty and rising competitiveness concerns for Canadian issuers arising from global economic and geopolitical change. The CSA said it will monitor domestic and international regulatory developments and expects to revisit both projects in future years, giving issuers appropriate notice ahead of any changes. It emphasised that existing securities legislation still requires disclosure of material climate risks and pointed issuers to the CSSB's voluntary standards, issued December 2024, as an interim framework.
updates.so_what: Canada is now a voluntary market — report material climate risk under existing continuous disclosure rules and use CSDS 2 as the template.
updates.source_title: CSA updates market on approach to climate-related and diversity-related disclosure projects
updates.source_publisher: Canadian Securities Administrators / Ontario Securities Commission

updates.headline: Stop-the-clock directive published as Directive (EU) 2025/794
updates.detail: Directive (EU) 2025/794 of 14 April 2025 was published in the Official Journal and entered into force the following day. It postponed CSRD wave 2 to financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027 and wave 3 to financial years starting on or after 1 January 2028, and moved CSDDD transposition to 26 July 2027 with first application phased from 26 July 2028. Parliament had approved the fast-tracked text by 531 votes to 69 with 17 abstentions. Member States had to transpose it by 31 December 2025.
updates.so_what: Use 2025/794 only for dates, and always check whether Directive (EU) 2026/470 has since overwritten them.
updates.source_title: Directive (EU) 2025/794 as regards the dates from which Member States are to apply certain corporate sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements
updates.source_publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

updates.headline: QFMA resolves to require external assurance of sustainability reporting
updates.detail: A QFMA Board of Directors' resolution dated 7 April 2025 established the requirement for external assurance of the sustainability reporting framework by the external auditor, based on international auditing standards including ISSA 5000 and the IESSA ethical requirements. The requirement was subsequently set out in the QFMA's November 2025 guidance for Main Market listed companies. It applies alongside the mandatory application of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 from financial year 2026.
updates.so_what: Qatar mandates assurance from the first reporting year, so scope the auditor engagement at the same time as the reporting project.
updates.source_title: Guidance on Corporate Sustainability Reporting For Companies Listed on the Main Market

updates.headline: SBTi pauses development of the Oil and Gas Standard
updates.detail: SBTi paused development of an Oil and Gas Standard in order to prioritise other standards and to ensure technical viability and market readiness, with re-scoping planned to commence in 2027. In the interim the fossil fuel policy continues to prevent companies with direct involvement in exploration, extraction, mining or production of fossil fuels from committing or having targets validated, subject to limited revenue-based exceptions.
updates.so_what: Groups with any upstream fossil fuel activity should confirm eligibility under the fossil fuel policy before starting an SBTi process.
updates.source_title: Oil and Gas

updates.headline: ASIC issues Regulatory Guide 280 on sustainability reporting
updates.detail: ASIC published Regulatory Guide 280 Sustainability reporting on 31 March 2025, explaining how it will exercise its powers under the sustainability reporting provisions of Chapter 2M of the Corporations Act. RG 280 sets out the Group 1, 2 and 3 size thresholds, the NGER registration trigger and the A$5bn asset owner threshold, the content of the sustainability report, ASIC's approach to relief, and the modified liability arrangements. It is the operative reference for determining whether and when an Australian entity must report.
updates.so_what: Run every Australian entity in the group through the RG 280 two-of-three size test before assuming it falls outside Group 2.
updates.source_title: Regulatory Guide 280 Sustainability reporting

updates.headline: SEC votes to end its defence of the climate-related disclosure rules
updates.detail: On 27 March 2025 the Commission voted to end its defence of the climate-related disclosure rules in the Eighth Circuit litigation, withdrawing from the defence while leaving the rules formally in place. Commissioner Crenshaw dissented, describing the action as the Commission letting the rule stand while abandoning it in court. The rules had already been stayed since April 2024.
updates.so_what: This is the point at which SEC climate reporting stopped being a credible planning assumption.
updates.source_title: Statement Regarding Climate-Related Disclosures Rule Litigation: The Commission has Left the Building

updates.headline: SBTi opens the first consultation on draft Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2
updates.detail: SBTi launched the first draft of Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2 for public consultation from 18 March to 1 June 2025. The draft split scope 1 and scope 2 and proposed a commitment to move to low-carbon electricity no later than 2040. On scope 3 it proposed flexible alternatives to direct reduction targets including green procurement and revenue-based options with supplier engagement in high-emissions sectors. It formally recognised beyond value chain mitigation, introduced interim carbon removal targets for unabated emissions, added a requirement to assess and communicate progress, and simplified requirements for medium-sized companies in developing markets and for SMEs. More than 1,800 stakeholders responded.
updates.so_what: Use the consultation drafts and feedback reports to understand why V2.0 landed where it did on scope 3.
updates.source_title: SBTi launches draft Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2 for consultation

updates.headline: SSBJ issues Japan's three inaugural sustainability disclosure standards
updates.detail: The Sustainability Standards Board of Japan issued its inaugural standards on 5 March 2025: the Universal Sustainability Disclosure Standard on application of the standards, Theme-based Standard No. 1 on General Disclosures and Theme-based Standard No. 2 on Climate-related Disclosures. Entities could voluntarily apply them to annual reporting periods ending on or after that date. The standards themselves do not prescribe which entities must apply them or when — that is set by the FSA's roadmap and Japanese securities law.
updates.so_what: Voluntary early SSBJ application has been available since March 2025; use it to test data readiness before the March 2027 mandate.
updates.source_title: About SSBJ Standards

updates.headline: Commission tables the Omnibus I sustainability simplification package
updates.detail: The Commission published COM(2025) 80 and COM(2025) 81, splitting the reform into a fast-track directive postponing application dates and a content directive amending the Accounting, Audit, CSRD and CSDDD Directives. The content proposal targeted a roughly 80% reduction in the number of companies in CSRD scope and a value-chain cap protecting undertakings below the threshold. This started the twelve-month legislative process that ended with Directive (EU) 2026/470.
updates.so_what: Anchor any historical comparison of your scope position to the pre-26 February 2025 CSRD baseline.
updates.source_title: Proposal for a Directive amending the Accounting, Audit, CSRD and CSDDD Directives - COM(2025) 81 final

updates.headline: SEC asks the Eighth Circuit not to schedule argument on the climate rules
updates.detail: On 11 February 2025 Acting Chairman Mark Uyeda directed Commission staff to notify the Eighth Circuit of changed circumstances and to request that the court not schedule the case for argument, to give the Commission time to deliberate on next steps. This was the first formal signal that the Commission would not continue defending the March 2024 rules. The Commission committed to inform the court promptly of its ultimate position.
updates.so_what: Mark this as the start of the federal retreat when reconstructing your compliance timeline.
updates.source_title: Acting Chairman Statement on Climate-Related Disclosure Rules

updates.headline: Australia's mandatory climate reporting begins for Group 1 entities
updates.detail: Mandatory sustainability reporting under Chapter 2M of the Corporations Act commenced for Group 1 entities for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2025. Group 1 comprises entities meeting at least two of consolidated revenue of A$500m or more, consolidated gross assets of A$1bn or more, and 500 or more employees, plus entities registered or required to register under the NGER Act. Reports must comply with AASB S2 and include climate statements, notes, a directors' declaration and scenario analysis against two mandated temperature scenarios. Limited assurance over governance, strategy risks and opportunities and Scope 1 and 2 emissions applies in year one under ASSA 5010.
updates.so_what: Australia is the first of EcoLedger's markets with a hard statutory climate report and audit trail — treat it as the reference implementation.
updates.source_title: Who must prepare a sustainability report?

updates.headline: HKEX's new climate requirements take effect for Main Board issuers
updates.detail: The enhanced climate-related disclosure requirements in Part D of Appendix C2 of the HKEX ESG Reporting Code took effect for financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2025. LargeCap issuers, being Hang Seng Composite LargeCap Index constituents, must disclose Scope 1 and 2 emissions on a mandatory basis from FY2025, with the remaining new climate requirements mandatory from FY2026. Other Main Board issuers report on comply-or-explain from FY2025 and GEM issuers on a voluntary basis. The requirements are structured around governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets, closely reflecting IFRS S2.
updates.so_what: Hong Kong LargeCap issuers face full mandatory climate disclosure from FY2026, so the comply-or-explain year is already over.
updates.source_title: Exchange Publishes Conclusions on Climate Disclosure Requirements

updates.headline: GHG Protocol publishes four Standard Development Plans for the corporate suite revision
updates.detail: GHG Protocol published Standard Development Plans for four workstreams - Corporate Standard, Scope 2, Scope 3, and Actions and Market Instruments - on 20 December 2024, under the Standard Development and Revision Procedure adopted on 26 November 2024. These four plans were superseded on 29 July 2026 by version 2.0 of a single Consolidated Corporate Standard Standard Development Plan.
updates.so_what: Discard any internal roadmap built on the four December 2024 plans - they no longer describe the programme.
updates.source_title: Consolidated Corporate Standard - Standard Development Plan (SDP), version 2.0

updates.headline: UK Sustainability Disclosure TAC recommends endorsing IFRS S1 and S2
updates.detail: The FRC announced on 18 December 2024 that the UK Sustainability Disclosure Technical Advisory Committee had issued its final recommendations, agreed on 5 December 2024, that the UK endorse IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 for use in the UK. The TAC recommended lengthening the climate-first reporting relief from one year to two, and asked the UK Sustainability Disclosure Policy and Implementation Committee to develop guidance on aligning IFRS S1 with existing UK sustainability-related disclosure requirements. It concluded that adoption would support long-term public good in the UK with only minor modifications.
updates.so_what: The TAC recommendations explain why UK SRS differs from IFRS S1/S2 — read them when reconciling group and UK reporting.
updates.source_title: UK Sustainability TAC issues final recommendations

updates.headline: HKICPA publishes HKFRS S1 and HKFRS S2
updates.detail: The HKICPA published HKFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information and HKFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures on 12 December 2024, with an effective date of 1 August 2025. The Institute stated that the HKFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards are fully aligned with the ISSB Standards. Publication completed the standard-setting step in the Hong Kong Government's roadmap, which targets full adoption by large publicly accountable entities by 2028.
updates.so_what: Hong Kong entities can adopt HKFRS S1/S2 and satisfy both the local standard and HKEX's climate requirements in one pass.
updates.source_title: HKICPA publishes HKFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards

updates.headline: Hong Kong Government launches its roadmap on sustainability disclosure
updates.detail: The Hong Kong SAR Government launched the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong on 10 December 2024, requiring publicly accountable entities to adopt the ISSB Standards over time. Key milestones are HKICPA finalising Hong Kong-aligned standards by end-2024 with effect from 1 August 2025, all Main Board issuers disclosing climate information on comply-or-explain from 1 January 2025, LargeCap Index constituents facing mandatory climate disclosure from 1 January 2026, and full adoption by large publicly accountable entities including non-listed financial institutions by 2028. HKEX will consult the market in 2027 on mandating sustainability reporting for listed publicly accountable entities from 1 January 2028. The AFRC leads the sustainability assurance workstream.
updates.so_what: Plan Hong Kong on a 2028 horizon — non-listed financial institutions are in scope even though no listing rule touches them.
updates.source_title: Government launches roadmap on sustainability disclosure in Hong Kong
updates.source_publisher: Government of the Hong Kong SAR

updates.headline: CARB issues its SB 253 enforcement notice for the first reporting cycle
updates.detail: CARB issued the Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act Enforcement Notice in December 2024, addressing enforcement discretion for the first reporting cycle in 2026 for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions. CARB also published a set of questions on Senate Bills 253 and 261 as amended by SB 219 as part of an information solicitation. The notice remains posted on CARB's climate disclosure resources page.
updates.so_what: Rely on CARB's stated good-faith enforcement posture only for genuine first-cycle data gaps, not for failure to file.
updates.source_title: Climate Disclosure Resources - SB 253 Enforcement Notice (12/2024)

updates.headline: ISO approves third editions of ISO 14064-1 and 14064-2 and flags ISO 14067 for revision
updates.detail: On 14 October 2024 ISO approved and registered new projects for the third editions of ISO 14064-1 (organization level) and ISO 14064-2 (project level), moving both published standards to stage 90.92, International Standard to be revised. ISO 14067:2018 on product carbon footprints was moved to the same stage on the same date. These projects predate the September 2025 GHG Protocol partnership and were subsequently aligned to the joint programme.
updates.so_what: Recognise that ISO started revising 14064 independently a year before the partnership, which is why the ISO drafts are ahead of the GHG Protocol ones.
updates.source_title: ISO 14064-1:2018 - Greenhouse gases - Part 1

updates.headline: Australia's mandatory climate reporting legislation receives Royal Assent
updates.detail: The Treasury Laws Amendment (Financial Market Infrastructure and Other Measures) Act 2024, Act No. 87 of 2024, received Royal Assent on 17 September 2024. Schedule 4 introduces climate-related financial disclosure and sustainability reporting requirements into the Corporations Act 2001, including the sustainability report under s296A, the obligation to comply with sustainability standards made by the AASB, audit requirements, and the modified liability arrangements. It also amends the ASIC Act to provide for sustainability standards and assurance standards.
updates.so_what: Australia's requirement is primary legislation, not regulator guidance — it will not be softened by a policy shift.
updates.source_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Financial Market Infrastructure and Other Measures) Act 2024

updates.headline: ISSB sets its two-year work plan and takes on the Transition Plan Taskforce materials
updates.detail: The ISSB announced its 2024-2026 work plan, prioritising support for implementation of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 alongside new research on nature and human capital. The IFRS Foundation assumed responsibility for the disclosure-specific materials of the Transition Plan Taskforce. A Memorandum of Understanding with the GHG Protocol was announced, under which the ISSB appoints an observer to the GHG Protocol's Independent Standards Board. CDP aligned its 2024 questionnaire with IFRS S2, GRI committed to full interoperability, and the ISSB confirmed it would incorporate TNFD recommendations into its biodiversity research. The ISSB reported that over 20 jurisdictions representing 55% of global GDP had adopted or were adopting ISSB Standards.
updates.so_what: This is the origin of the current work plan — everything now in flight on nature, human capital and SASB traces back to it.
updates.source_title: ISSB delivers further harmonisation of the sustainability disclosure landscape as it embarks on new work plan

updates.headline: UAE launches Principles for Sustainability-Related Disclosures for reporting entities
updates.detail: The UAE Sustainable Finance Working Group, whose members include the Central Bank of the UAE, the securities regulator and other federal authorities, issued the Principles for Sustainability-Related Disclosures on 14 June 2024. They apply to domestic entities and to branches and subsidiaries of foreign entities falling under the purview of UAE authorities. Crucially, implementation discretion rests with each individual authority, which may choose voluntary, comply-or-explain or mandatory routes and set its own timeline. The Principles acknowledge the international movement towards the ISSB standards as a potential global baseline but do not adopt them.
updates.so_what: Do not treat the UAE Principles as a reporting standard — identify which specific UAE regulator binds each of your entities.
updates.source_title: Principles for Sustainability-Related Disclosures
updates.source_publisher: Central Bank of the UAE / UAE Sustainable Finance Working Group

updates.headline: SBTi publishes its plan for a major revision of the Corporate Net-Zero Standard
updates.detail: SBTi set out plans for the major revision that became V2.0, covering four areas: alignment with the latest science including IPCC reports and UN guidance, scope 3 target-setting challenges, integrating continuous improvement and target delivery, and interoperability with other standards and frameworks. The plan also flagged an assessment of environmental attribute certificates in corporate climate targets. The provisional timeline anticipated a scope 3 discussion paper and EAC evidence assessment in Q3 2024 and a draft V2 public consultation in Q4 2024, which ultimately ran in March 2025.
updates.so_what: Note that the published timetable slipped by roughly two quarters, so treat SBTi's projected dates as indicative.
updates.source_title: SBTi releases plans for the Corporate Net-Zero Standard major revision

updates.headline: HKEX publishes conclusions mandating IFRS S2-aligned climate disclosures
updates.detail: HKEX published its consultation conclusions on enhancement of climate-related disclosures under the ESG framework on 19 April 2024, following 115 responses showing broad-based support. The amended Listing Rules take effect from 1 January 2025 and introduce a new Part D of Appendix C2 reflecting IFRS S2 more closely, phased by issuer type with proportionality and scaling-in reliefs. HKEX also published Implementation Guidance referencing IFRS S1 principles to help issuers meet the new requirements.
updates.so_what: HKEX's implementation guidance is the practical bridge from IFRS S2 to Appendix C2 — use it rather than mapping from scratch.
updates.source_title: Exchange Publishes Conclusions on Climate Disclosure Requirements

updates.headline: SEC stays its climate-related disclosure rules pending Eighth Circuit review
updates.detail: By order of 4 April 2024, Securities Act Release No. 11280 and Exchange Act Release No. 99908, the Commission stayed the climate-related disclosure rules pending completion of judicial review of the consolidated Eighth Circuit petitions, exercising discretion under Exchange Act section 25(c)(2) and Administrative Procedure Act section 705. The delay of effective date was published in the Federal Register on 12 April 2024. No registrant has been required to comply with the rules at any point since adoption.
updates.so_what: Any statement that US issuers 'must' make SEC climate disclosures is wrong and has been since April 2024.
updates.source_title: Order issuing stay, Securities Act Release No. 11280

updates.headline: SEC adopts The Enhancement and Standardization of Climate-Related Disclosures for Investors
updates.detail: On 6 March 2024 the SEC adopted rules requiring registrants to disclose material climate-related risks, mitigation expenditures, board oversight and risk management processes, climate targets, severe weather costs and carbon offset expenses. Large accelerated and accelerated filers that were not otherwise exempted would also have had to disclose material Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, with limited assurance phasing to reasonable assurance for large accelerated filers. Compliance dates were to be phased by filer status. The rules were stayed less than a month later and never took effect.
updates.so_what: Retain the 2024 rule text as a reference for what materiality-based climate disclosure looks like, not as an obligation.
updates.source_title: SEC Adopts Rules to Enhance and Standardize Climate-Related Disclosures for Investors

changes.topic: Structure of the corporate accounting rulebook
changes.old: Separate GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004), Scope 2 Guidance (2015) and Scope 3 Standard (2011), plus a separate ISO 14064-1:2018.
changes.new: One co-branded GHGP-ISO consolidated corporate standard in two parts: Part 1 general requirements and physical GHG inventory, Part 2 actions and market instruments.
changes.source_title: Consolidated Corporate Standard - Standard Development Plan (SDP), version 2.0

changes.old: Annual matching of energy attribute certificates to consumption within a defined market boundary.
changes.new: Consulted proposal required market-based claims to match the time and location of consumption (hourly and geographic matching) for voluntary claims, with load-profile approximation, small-organisation exemptions, legacy contract clauses and a multi-year phase-in. GHG Protocol says it is now exploring multiple reporting approaches following consultation.
changes.source_title: RELEASE: GHG Protocol Opens Public Consultations on Scope 2 and Electricity Sector Consequential Accounting

changes.old: Companies determine which of the 15 categories are relevant using qualitative screening criteria and may exclude categories judged not relevant.
changes.new: A prescriptive 95 percent inclusion threshold for required scope 3 emissions, requiring companies to quantify total required scope 3 emissions in order to justify any exclusion.
changes.source_title: Scope 3 Standard Revisions: Phase 1 Progress Update, March 2026

changes.old: Category 15 Investments covers investments and a broad range of financial services.
changes.new: Category 15 narrowed to investment-related activities only, with other financial services moved to a new Category 16 for facilitated activities.
changes.source_title: Scope 3 Standard Revisions: Phase 1 Progress Update, March 2026

changes.topic: Reporting architecture for market instruments and climate actions
changes.old: A single inventory reported in location-based and market-based variants, with actions and instruments absorbed into the market-based figure.
changes.new: A multi-statement structure separating the physical inventory, a market-based inventory, a GHG impact statement using consequential methods, and non-GHG indicators.
changes.source_title: Actions and Market Instruments Standard

changes.old: No dedicated GHG Protocol standard; land-sector emissions and removals handled inconsistently within scope 1 and scope 3 accounting.
changes.new: Land Sector and Removals Standard (published 30 January 2026, v1.1 June 2026) with companion Guidance v1.0, effective 1 January 2027.
changes.source_title: Land Sector and Removals Standard

changes.topic: Avoided emissions from clean electricity procurement
changes.old: No accepted GHG Protocol method; claims made ad hoc outside the inventory.
changes.new: The proposed Marginal Impact Method was declined by the Independent Standards Board in July 2025; consequential avoided-emissions work moved to the cross-sectoral Actions and Market Instruments workstream, with a draft consultation indicated for Q3 2027.
changes.source_title: Scope 2 Standard Advances: ISB Approves Consultation on Market- and Location-Based Revisions

changes.old: ISO 14068-1:2023, Climate change management - Transition to net zero - Part 1: Carbon neutrality.
changes.new: ISO 14068, Climate change management - Carbon neutrality, single part, at stage 60.00 under publication with a September 2026 target date; ISO 14068-1:2023 moved to stage 90.92 on 8 May 2026.
changes.source_title: ISO 14068 - Climate change management - Carbon neutrality

changes.old: IWA 42:2022 ISO Net Zero Guidelines - a non-normative international workshop agreement, not independently verifiable.
changes.new: ISO/DIS 14060 Net zero aligned organizations - an independently verifiable International Standard covering net zero strategy, targets and delivery, out for a 12-week DIS ballot from 17 June 2026.
changes.source_title: ISO launches public consultation on the world's first International Standard for net zero alignment today

changes.old: ISO/TR 14069:2013 technical report on applying ISO 14064-1 (now withdrawn).
changes.new: ISO/TS 14064-4:2025, published November 2025, covering organizational boundaries under control (financial or operational) or equity share approaches and quantification of emission categories.
changes.source_title: ISO/TS 14064-4:2025 - Greenhouse gases - Part 4

changes.old: No dedicated international standard for remote verification; ISO 14064-3:2019 alone governs verification and validation.
changes.new: ISO 14064-5:2026, published 12 February 2026, provides guidance on remote and hybrid verification and validation techniques for GHG statements.
changes.source_title: ISO 14064-5:2026 - Greenhouse gases - Part 5

changes.topic: Who approves the corporate accounting standard
changes.old: GHG Protocol standards approved through WRI/WBCSD governance; ISO standards approved separately through ISO/TC 207/SC 7 ballots.
changes.new: The consolidated standard requires concurrent ratification by the GHG Protocol Independent Standards Board and a two-thirds majority of permanent members of ISO/TC 207/SC 7, with ISO sitting as Observing Entity to the ISB.
changes.source_title: Consolidated Corporate Standard - Standard Development Plan (SDP), version 2.0

changes.topic: Publication timetable for the corporate suite
changes.old: Four separate revisions on staggered timetables; the October 2025 Scope 2 release anticipated a second consultation in 2026 and final publication in 2027.
changes.new: One integrated consultation estimated for Q2 2027 and one publication estimated for Q4 2028.
changes.source_title: GHG Protocol Announces Key Standard Development Updates

changes.old: Parallel and partly inconsistent regimes: ISO 14067:2018 and the GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard (2011).
changes.new: A single jointly developed ISO-GHG Protocol product-level standard, with the Joint Working Group finalised 9 April 2026 and ISO 14067:2018 flagged for revision as ISO/WD 14067.2. No draft or target date published.
changes.source_title: ANNOUNCEMENT: ISO and GHG Protocol Finalize Joint Working Group to Develop Product-Level Accounting Standard

changes.old: A single combined scope 1 and 2 target covering at least 95% of scope 1 and 2 emissions.
changes.new: Separate scope 1 and scope 2 targets, each covering 100% of the relevant emissions, reflecting their different decarbonisation levers.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Fixed-percentage coverage thresholds determining how much of scope 3 had to be covered by targets.
changes.new: Significance-based approach: targets must cover every scope 3 category representing at least 5% of categories 1-14 emissions.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Economic and physical intensity target methods available, based on approximately 7% year-on-year intensity reduction.
changes.new: Both methods removed, on the grounds that science-based reference pathways do not exist for them.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Supplier engagement targets, typically expressed as a share of suppliers by emissions with their own science-based targets.
changes.new: Broader supplier and customer alignment pathways measuring the share of suppliers or customers that are 'in transition' or 'net-zero aligned', plus new volume, product use and product end-of-life alignment methods.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Category 11 targets generally required where material, with limited flexibility.
changes.new: A tightly constrained exception may be sought subject to SBTi approval where no downstream option is viable, conditional on a mandatory long-term target and annual reporting.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Targets could be set against either the location-based or the market-based scope 2 inventory, with a renewable electricity focus.
changes.new: Scope 2 targets are set only against the physical, location-based inventory; the framing moves from renewable to low-carbon electricity, and the scope 2 intensity target option is removed.
changes.source_title: Understanding Scope 2 in the Updated Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Market-based instruments could drive reported target progress with comparatively limited quality criteria.
changes.new: Market instruments move into the implementation hierarchy under a 'near, new, now' test: same synchronous grid, generator generally no more than 15 years old, and annual temporal matching, with transparent registry tracking and volume matching.
changes.source_title: Understanding Scope 2 in the Updated Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Standard route for large companies plus a separate simplified SME target-setting route.
changes.new: Formal Category A and Category B classification with differentiated obligations based on turnover, geography, emissions and employee thresholds; scope 3 target-setting is optional for Category B.
changes.source_title: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0 Criteria for Category B companies

changes.old: Assurance recommended but not mandatory.
changes.new: Mandatory limited assurance for Category A companies over inventories and target-setting metrics, delivered under a formal SBTi Assurance Model; recommended only for Category B.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: A historical base year selected from company records.
changes.new: A target base year set to the most recent year for which comprehensive emissions and other applicable data are available; companies may still communicate against an earlier historical reference year if equivalence is validated.
changes.source_title: SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard Version 2.0 Criteria

changes.old: Mandatory five-year target review of targets set over longer horizons.
changes.new: The mandatory five-year review requirement is retired because all targets are now set on a five-year basis, replaced by continuous evaluation focused on identifying significant changes that trigger recalculation.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Long-term net-zero targets required for all companies seeking net-zero validation, including for scope 3.
changes.new: Long-term targets required only for companies setting near-term intensity or asset transition targets; long-term scope 3 targets become optional for all companies.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.topic: Carbon removals before the net-zero year
changes.old: Neutralisation milestones were a recommendation, with basic criteria for carbon removal activities.
changes.new: A structured 'ongoing emissions responsibility' framework with a mandatory carbon removal requirement for Category A companies from 2035, plus detailed storage durability, double-counting and reporting requirements.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: No explicit implementation hierarchy in the standard.
changes.new: An implementation hierarchy prioritises direct activity-level reductions, then actions within shared activity pools, then sector-level action, the latter permitted only where structural constraints exist.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Not explicit criteria in V1.
changes.new: Mandatory governance, board accountability, transition planning and disclosure requirements, with Category A companies required to publish a transition plan within 15 months of validation.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Basic annual progress reporting following validation.
changes.new: Significantly expanded annual disclosure of actions taken and barriers faced, plus a new end-of-cycle assessment requiring full-scope inventories, separate reporting of actions and market instruments, and third-party assurance for Category A companies.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: No formal requirement to identify emissions-intensive activities.
changes.new: Category A companies must identify and quantify emissions-intensive activities and report any representing at least 5% of scope 3 emissions.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: No specific sustainability requirements for bio-based inputs used to meet targets.
changes.new: Bio-based feedstocks used for target implementation must meet recognised third-party and SBTi minimum sustainability criteria and must not be associated with deforestation or conversion of natural ecosystems.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Addressed through separate criteria C36 and C37.
changes.new: Restrictions formalised into the scope section of the standard and linked explicitly to a dedicated Fossil Fuel Policy, replacing C36 and C37.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Criterion-by-criterion structure carried through V1.0 to V1.3.1.
changes.new: Six chapters with headline criteria and sub-criteria; 42% of V2.0 sections are entirely new and 58% modify or expand existing approaches, and SBTi states a direct criterion-by-criterion mapping to V1.3.1 is not feasible.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Annual linear reduction rate applied without adjustment for the length of the interval between base year and net-zero target year.
changes.new: Rates calculated to spread reductions consistently across the full pathway to 2050 based on the company's own base year to target year interval, retaining the 4.2% minimum annual reduction floor.
changes.source_title: The SBTi updates the Absolute Contraction Approach

changes.old: No differentiated treatment of companies with fast-growing electricity consumption.
changes.new: Category A companies with electricity demand growth above 20% per annum must set scope 2 emissions reduction targets rather than low-carbon electricity alignment targets.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Not addressed.
changes.new: Category A companies with significant electricity consumption must measure and publicly disclose low-carbon electricity performance on hourly accounting intervals; hourly matching is not required for target progress but attracts voluntary recognition.
changes.source_title: Understanding Scope 2 in the Updated Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Land sector and removals accounting not systematically integrated into the corporate inventory requirements.
changes.new: Inventory requirements reference GHG Protocol Land Sector and Removals Standard aligned accounting, alongside low-carbon electricity metrics, physical inventories and separately reported market instruments.
changes.source_title: Main Changes Document: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0

changes.old: Entities had to measure and disclose all Scope 3 Category 15 (investments) emissions.
changes.new: Entities may limit measurement and disclosure to financed emissions, and must describe the financial activities excluded, including derivatives. Effective for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, early application permitted.
changes.source_title: ISSB issues targeted amendments to IFRS S2 to support implementation

changes.topic: Industry classification for disaggregating financed emissions
changes.old: IFRS S2 set a prescriptive hierarchy requiring the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS).
changes.new: Entities may use an alternative, commonly used classification system when disaggregating financed emissions information.
changes.source_title: ISSB issues targeted amendments to IFRS S2 to support implementation

changes.topic: Jurisdictional relief from the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004)
changes.old: Relief in IFRS S2 paragraph 29(a)(ii) applied where a jurisdictional authority or listing exchange required a different measurement basis, read as applying to the entity as a whole.
changes.new: The relief applies even where only part of an entity is required to use a different measurement basis.
changes.source_title: ISSB issues targeted amendments to IFRS S2 to support implementation

changes.old: GHG emissions had to be converted using global warming potential values from the latest IPCC Assessment Report.
changes.new: Jurisdictional relief is available to use different, jurisdictionally mandated GWP values.
changes.source_title: ISSB issues targeted amendments to IFRS S2 to support implementation

changes.old: Nature sat in a research project (Biodiversity, Ecosystems and Ecosystem Services) with no decided output.
changes.new: An IFRS Practice Statement supplementing IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 — a tool companies may choose to use unless a jurisdiction requires it. Exposure Draft targeted for October 2026 with a 120-day comment period.
changes.source_title: ISSB agrees on the proposed way forward for nature-related disclosures

changes.topic: Nature terminology in the draft Practice Statement
changes.old: Draft used the term 'environmental assets'.
changes.new: Draft uses 'environmental resources'; nature-related transition risks and nature-related physical risks are separately defined.
changes.source_title: ISSB Update June 2026

changes.old: SASB Standards as inherited from the Value Reporting Foundation in 2022, largely unrevised in ISSB terms.
changes.new: Two Exposure Drafts (3 July 2025 and 26 March 2026) propose amendments to 12 prioritised SASB Standards plus targeted amendments to 41 more and consequential changes to the IFRS S2 Industry-based Guidance; six Technology & Communications Standards added to scope on 22 July 2026. Final amendments would be effective 12-18 months after issuance.
changes.source_title: Enhancing the SASB Standards—Phase 1—Continued

changes.old: 14 ISSB members.
changes.new: Transition to 10 members, with the Trustees expecting each board to comprise 10 members from 2028, subject to Constitution amendments.
changes.source_title: IFRS Foundation Trustees announce five-year plan including new seat of the ISSB in Geneva

changes.old: Multi-location model anchored on Frankfurt and Montreal, with Beijing and Tokyo offices.
changes.new: A new seat of the ISSB in Geneva expected to open mid-2027; Frankfurt continues as the EU engagement hub and Montreal retains key functions.
changes.source_title: IFRS Foundation Trustees announce five-year plan including new seat of the ISSB in Geneva

changes.old: Taxonomy as published April 2024, tagging the 2023 text of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2.
changes.new: Proposed Update 1 adds tagging for the December 2025 Amendments to Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosures; comments close 28 September 2026.
changes.source_title: ISSB proposes updates to its digital sustainability taxonomy

changes.old: Large undertakings meeting 2 of 3 criteria including more than 250 employees were in scope
changes.new: Only undertakings with an average of more than 1 000 employees during the financial year are in scope
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470, amended Article 19a(1) of Directive 2013/34/EU

changes.old: Net turnover above EUR 50 million as one of the 'large undertaking' size criteria
changes.new: Net turnover must exceed EUR 450 000 000, and it must be met cumulatively with the 1 000-employee test
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470, amended Article 19a(1) of Directive 2013/34/EU

changes.topic: How the size test is applied
changes.old: Two of three size criteria (balance sheet total, net turnover, employees) had to be exceeded
changes.new: Both the turnover and the employee threshold must be exceeded; balance sheet total no longer drives scope
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470, amended Articles 19a(1) and 29a(1)

changes.old: Listed SMEs were wave 3, due to report for financial years from 2026 (later 2028) using a proportionate LSME standard, with a two-year opt-out
changes.new: Removed from mandatory scope entirely; the empowerment to adopt an LSME standard is deleted and the two-year opt-out in Article 19a(7) is deleted as redundant
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470, recitals 15 and 16

changes.topic: Small and non-complex credit institutions and captive insurers
changes.old: In wave 3 alongside listed SMEs
changes.new: Out of mandatory scope unless they independently exceed the 1 000 employee and EUR 450m turnover thresholds
changes.source_title: Simplified sustainability reporting and due diligence rules for businesses

changes.topic: First mandatory reporting year for the reduced scope
changes.old: Wave 2 large undertakings reported for FY2025; wave 3 for FY2026
changes.new: Stop-the-clock moved these to FY2027 and FY2028; Directive (EU) 2026/470 then set FY2027 (financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027) as the first year for the reduced scope
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470

changes.topic: Wave-one reporters for FY2025 and FY2026
changes.old: Wave-one companies (first reported FY2024) continued reporting annually without interruption
changes.new: Member States MAY exempt wave-one undertakings from reporting for financial years beginning between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2026 - a national option, not an automatic EU-wide exemption
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470, recital 31

changes.old: Limited assurance initially, with the Commission required to assess and potentially move to reasonable assurance
changes.new: Limited assurance is permanent; the reasonable assurance requirement is removed to avoid increased costs
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470, recital 5

changes.old: Commission to adopt limited assurance standards by 1 October 2026
changes.new: Commission shall, no later than 1 July 2027, adopt delegated acts providing for limited assurance standards
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470

changes.old: Commission required to adopt sector-specific sustainability reporting standards by 30 June 2026
changes.new: Mandate deleted - Article 29b(1) third, fourth and sixth subparagraphs removed; sector reporting is voluntary
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470

changes.old: A value-chain cap existed only as an ESRS-level relief tied to the LSME standard; no statutory right to refuse
changes.new: Statutory cap: a reporter may not require a protected undertaking (average 1 000 or fewer employees) to supply more than the voluntary standard specifies, must flag requests exceeding the cap, and must inform the counterparty of its statutory right to decline
changes.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation of 3.7.2026 establishing standards for voluntary use by undertakings protected by the value chain cap

changes.topic: Scope of the value chain cap
changes.old: Not applicable
changes.new: The cap applies only to CSRD reporting obligations and does not restrict information requests made for due diligence, contractual, customer or other legal purposes
changes.source_title: Additional explanatory information regarding the value chain cap

changes.old: ESRS Set 1 under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772, with over a thousand datapoints and extensive voluntary disclosures
changes.new: Mandatory datapoints reduced by more than 60% and total datapoints by more than 70%; voluntary disclosures removed and quantitative datapoints prioritised over narrative text
changes.source_title: Commission adopts revised sustainability reporting standards

changes.old: ESRS Set 1 as amended by the quick fix applied to all reporters
changes.new: Revised ESRS are mandatory only from financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027; early application is permitted for financial years beginning in 2026 if the undertaking states which version it applied
changes.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation of 3.7.2026 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772

changes.old: More than 1 000 employees (phased from 5 000 / 3 000) under Directive (EU) 2024/1760
changes.new: More than 5 000 employees, with no lower phase-in tiers
changes.source_title: Corporate sustainability due diligence

changes.old: Net worldwide turnover above EUR 450 million (phased from EUR 1.5bn / EUR 900m)
changes.new: Net worldwide turnover above EUR 1 500 million, or EUR 1.5 billion generated in the EU for non-EU companies
changes.source_title: Corporate sustainability due diligence

changes.old: Companies had to adopt a transition plan for climate change mitigation aligned with the Paris Agreement
changes.new: Obligation removed
changes.source_title: Council signs off simplification of sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements

changes.old: EU-harmonised civil liability regime with a mandated right to full compensation
changes.new: EU harmonised liability regime removed; liability and enforcement determined by national law
changes.source_title: Council signs off simplification of sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements

changes.old: Maximum penalty of not less than 5% of net worldwide turnover
changes.new: Penalties capped at 3% of the company's net worldwide turnover for the most serious violations
changes.source_title: Council signs off simplification of sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements

changes.old: Full risk-based due diligence across the chain of activities including indirect business partners
changes.new: Companies may prioritise direct business partners where adverse impacts are equally likely, and act on 'reasonably available information', reducing requests down the chain
changes.source_title: Council signs off simplification of sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements

changes.old: Transposition by 26 July 2026, first application 26 July 2027 for the largest companies
changes.new: Transposition by 26 July 2028; obligations apply from 26 July 2029, with Article 16 reporting for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2030
changes.source_title: Corporate sustainability due diligence

changes.old: Consignments with an intrinsic value not exceeding EUR 150 were excluded
changes.new: An importer is exempt where the net mass of imported CBAM goods in a calendar year does not cumulatively exceed 50 tonnes (Annex VII point 1); exceeding it pulls all that year's imports into scope
changes.source_title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/956

changes.old: By 31 May of each year for the preceding calendar year
changes.new: By 30 September of each year, and for the first time in 2027 for the year 2026
changes.source_title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083, amended Article 6 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956

changes.old: Certificate sales expected to begin alongside the definitive regime in 2026
changes.new: From 1 February 2027 Member States sell CBAM certificates on a common central platform, so nothing is purchased for 2026 emissions until 2027
changes.source_title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083, amended Article 20 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956

changes.old: At least 80% of embedded emissions in goods imported since the start of the calendar year at the end of each quarter
changes.new: At least 50% of embedded emissions in goods imported since the start of the calendar year at the end of each quarter
changes.source_title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083, amended Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956

changes.old: Cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen
changes.new: Council position of 12 June 2026 would add selected downstream products and pre-consumer metal scrap, with annual Commission review of further additions - not yet agreed with Parliament
changes.source_title: Council moves to strengthen the EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism

changes.old: All economic activities had to be assessed for eligibility and alignment regardless of size
changes.new: Undertakings may omit assessing non-material activities where cumulative turnover, CapEx or OpEx is below 10% of the relevant KPI denominator
changes.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73

changes.old: OpEx KPI mandatory for all non-financial undertakings
changes.new: OpEx reporting may be skipped entirely where not material to the business model, provided the total value is disclosed and the immateriality explained
changes.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73, Article 2(1c)

changes.old: Long templates plus separate mandatory fossil gas and nuclear disclosure templates
changes.new: Templates significantly shortened and simplified; the fossil gas and nuclear templates are deleted
changes.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73, recital 13

changes.topic: EU Taxonomy reporting by financial undertakings
changes.old: Full green asset ratio and taxonomy KPI reporting required
changes.new: Until 31 December 2027 financial undertakings may opt out by stating that no activities are claimed as qualifying as environmentally sustainable
changes.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73, Article 7(9)

changes.old: Article 40a report expected to follow standards adopted by 30 June 2026
changes.new: EFRAG's ESRS-40a exposure draft issued 23 July 2026 with consultation to 31 October 2026 and technical advice due early 2027; first statements expected in 2029 for FY2028
changes.source_title: European Sustainability Standards for Third-Country Undertakings (ESRS-40a)

changes.topic: Parliament's negotiating demand vs final law
changes.old: Parliament's 13 November 2025 position required more than 1 750 employees plus EUR 450m turnover for CSRD scope
changes.new: Final law sets the employee threshold at more than 1 000, so more companies are in scope than Parliament wanted
changes.source_title: Sustainability reporting and due diligence: MEPs back simplification changes

changes.old: No routine review of CSRD monetary thresholds
changes.new: The Commission shall at least every five years review and, where appropriate, amend the thresholds to account for inflation
changes.source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470, amended Article 3(13) of Directive 2013/34/EU

changes.topic: SB 253 first Scope 1 and 2 reporting deadline
changes.old: 10 August 2026 (as set in the Board-approved regulation text, 17 CCR s.96076(a))
changes.new: Deferred by CARB notice of 24 June 2026; staff propose 10 November 2026, and regulation text providing for reporting 'on or before November 10 of the reporting year'
changes.source_title: SB 253 Public Workshop: California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (July 2026)

changes.old: 1 January 2026 statutory deadline (HSC s.38533)
changes.new: Not enforced; CARB will provide an alternate date after the Ninth Circuit appeal is resolved
changes.source_title: SB 261 Enforcement Advisory

changes.old: Adopted 6 March 2024 (Release Nos. 33-11275 / 34-99678), stayed since 4 April 2024
changes.new: Rescission proposed 29 May 2026 (Release No. 33-11421, 91 FR 33296); comments closed 3 August 2026; no final action
changes.source_title: Rescission of Climate-Related Disclosure Rules

changes.old: All fifteen GHG Protocol Scope 3 categories implied by the statute
changes.new: CARB staff propose mandating five categories initially - purchased goods and services, fuel- and energy-related activities, waste generated in operations, business travel, employee commuting - with the other ten voluntary
changes.source_title: SB 253 Public Workshop: California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (July 2026)

changes.old: Approved for adoption by CARB Board Resolution 26-1 on 26 February 2026
changes.new: Final package submitted to the Office of Administrative Law on 20 May 2026, then withdrawn by CARB for limited clarifying changes; to be resubmitted
changes.source_title: SB 253 Public Workshop: California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (July 2026)

changes.topic: Limited assurance over SB 253 Scope 1 and 2
changes.old: Not required for the 2026 data submission
changes.new: Required beginning with reports submitted in 2027 (ISAE 3410 for engagements before 15 December 2026; ISSA 5000 after)
changes.source_title: SB 253 Public Workshop: California Corporate Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (July 2026)

changes.topic: EPA reporting-year 2025 greenhouse gas reporting deadline
changes.old: 31 March 2026
changes.new: 30 October 2026
changes.source_title: Extending the Reporting Deadline Under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Rule for 2025, 91 FR 9712

changes.topic: New York Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act vehicle
changes.old: S3456 (Hoylman-Sigal), reported to Senate Finance 2 April 2025, now recorded as not active in session
changes.new: S9072A (Harckham), passed the Senate 40-22 on 10 February 2026, now in the Assembly Codes Committee
changes.source_title: NY State Senate Bill 2025-S9072A
