scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: EU undertakings which, on their balance sheet dates, 'exceed a net turnover of EUR 450 000 000 and an average number of 1 000 employees during the financial year' (amended Article 19a(1) of Directive 2013/34/EU). Both limbs must be met.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: Financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027 (first reports published in 2028).
scope_tests.assurance: Limited assurance. The EU limited assurance standard is due by delegated act no later than 1 July 2027; national assurance standards apply until then. Reasonable assurance has been removed.

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: EU parent undertakings of a group which, on the consolidated balance sheet date, exceed on a consolidated basis a net turnover of EUR 450 000 000 and an average of 1 000 employees during the financial year (amended Article 29a(1)).
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: Financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027, reported on a consolidated basis with subsidiary exemptions available.
scope_tests.assurance: Limited assurance on the consolidated sustainability statement.

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: Wave-one undertakings that first reported for financial year 2024. Member States 'should be able to exempt such undertakings from reporting obligations as regards the financial years beginning between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2026' - so relief depends on the national transposing law, not on EU law directly.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: FY2024 already reported. FY2025 and FY2026 exempt only where the Member State exercises the option; otherwise reporting continues with the quick-fix reliefs of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1416. FY2027 onwards only if the new thresholds are met.

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: Third-country undertakings under Article 40a: a non-EU parent generating net turnover in the Union exceeding EUR 450 000 000 in each of the last two consecutive financial years, which has either an EU branch with net turnover above EUR 200 000 000 or an EU subsidiary meeting that threshold.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: Financial year 2028, with the first sustainability statements expected in 2029, using the separate ESRS-40a standard still in exposure draft.
scope_tests.assurance: Not yet fixed; the ESRS-40a standard and the associated assurance arrangements are still in development.
scope_tests.source_title: European Sustainability Standards for Third-Country Undertakings (ESRS-40a)

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: Undertakings with an average of 1 000 or fewer employees in the preceding financial year that sit in a reporting company's value chain ('protected undertakings'). They have no reporting obligation and may decline requests exceeding the voluntary standard.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: No mandatory reporting period. The value-chain cap in Article 3 of the voluntary standard delegated act applies for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027.
scope_tests.assurance: None. Voluntary use of the standard carries no assurance requirement.
scope_tests.source_title: Commission Delegated Regulation of 3.7.2026 establishing standards for voluntary use by undertakings protected by the value chain cap

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: Importers of CBAM goods into the EU customs territory where the net mass of imported goods in a given calendar year cumulatively exceeds the single mass-based threshold in Annex VII point 1 (50 tonnes). Below that, the importer is exempt from CBAM obligations.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: Calendar year 2026, declared by 30 September 2027 ('by 30 September of each year, and for the first time in 2027 for the year 2026').
scope_tests.assurance: Embedded emissions must be verified by an accredited verifier; the declarant must hold CBAM certificates covering at least 50% of embedded emissions at the end of each quarter and surrender the full amount by 30 September.

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: Undertakings subject to sustainability reporting under Articles 19a or 29a of Directive 2013/34/EU must make Article 8 Taxonomy disclosures. After Omnibus I this means the same 1 000-employee and EUR 450m turnover population; companies outside CSRD scope have no Article 8 obligation.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: The simplification measures apply as of 1 January 2026 and cover financial year 2025, with an option to begin in financial year 2026 instead. Mandatory Article 8 reporting for the reduced CSRD population starts with FY2027.
scope_tests.assurance: Taxonomy disclosures form part of the sustainability statement and are covered by the same limited assurance engagement.

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: Financial undertakings within CSRD scope. Until 31 December 2027 they may opt out of full taxonomy reporting by stating that no activities are claimed as being associated with economic activities that qualify as environmentally sustainable.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: Financial year 2025 onwards under the simplified regime, with the opt-out available until 31 December 2027.
scope_tests.assurance: Limited assurance as part of the sustainability statement where reported.

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: A 'reporting entity': a partnership, corporation, limited liability company or other business entity formed under the laws of a US state, the District of Columbia or the federal government, with total annual revenues in excess of one billion dollars ($1,000,000,000), that does business in California. 'Doing business in California' means meeting either of the criteria in California Revenue and Taxation Code section 23101(b)(1) (organised or commercially domiciled in California) or (b)(2) (in-state sales exceeding the indexed threshold - $735,019 for 2024 - or 25 per cent of total sales); the property and payroll tests in section 23101 were deliberately excluded. 'Revenue' has the same meaning as 'gross receipts' under Revenue and Taxation Code section 25120(f)(2) - gross amounts realised on the sale or exchange of property, the performance of services, or the use of property or capital, not reduced by cost of goods sold - tested on the lesser of the two previous fiscal years. A parent may file a consolidated report covering subsidiaries, including a foreign parent for its US subsidiaries, but each subsidiary remains individually responsible and is separately fee-assessed.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for the prior fiscal year - entities with fiscal years ending on or before 1 February 2026 report FY25-26 data; entities with later fiscal year ends report FY24-25 data. Scope 3 from 2027.
scope_tests.assurance: No limited assurance required for the 2026 data submission. Limited assurance over Scope 1 and 2 begins with reports submitted in 2027 (ISAE 3410 for engagements before 15 December 2026, ISSA 5000 after). Statutory reasonable assurance from 2030 is not yet the subject of rulemaking.
scope_tests.source_title: Article 6: California Climate Disclosures - proposed regulation text (17 CCR 96070-96077)

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: A 'covered entity': a business entity formed under the laws of a US state, the District of Columbia or the federal government, with total annual revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000), that does business in California, using the same 'doing business in California' and gross-receipts revenue definitions as SB 253 and the lesser of the two previous fiscal years. Every SB 253 reporting entity is also an SB 261 covered entity; the converse is not true.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: A climate-related financial risk report following the TCFD June 2017 recommendations or IFRS S2 (or an equivalent report required by law, regulation or a regulated exchange), published on the entity's own website with the link lodged in CARB's public docket; biennial thereafter.
scope_tests.assurance: No third-party assurance requirement. Note: the statutory 1 January 2026 deadline is not being enforced because the Ninth Circuit enjoined enforcement of SB 261 on 18 November 2025; CARB will set an alternate date after the appeal is resolved.
scope_tests.source_title: Climate Related Financial Risk Report Checklist

scope_tests.who_is_in_scope: Registrants filing registration statements and annual reports under the Securities Act of 1933 and Securities Exchange Act of 1934, with material Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions disclosure limited to large accelerated filers and accelerated filers that were not otherwise exempted, phased by filer status.
scope_tests.first_reporting_period: None. The rules adopted 6 March 2024 have been stayed since 4 April 2024 and no compliance date has ever taken effect.
scope_tests.assurance: Would have required limited assurance over Scope 1 and 2 for large accelerated and accelerated filers, rising to reasonable assurance for large accelerated filers after a further transition period - never in force, and now proposed for rescission.
scope_tests.source_title: Order issuing stay, Securities Act Release No. 11280 / Exchange Act Release No. 99908

adoption.first_reporting_period: Not yet specified; depends on the FCA's Listing Rules outcome and future government decisions
adoption.note: Snapshot updated 18 June 2026. Final UK Sustainability Reporting Standards endorsing IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 were published by the UK government on 25 February 2026 and are available for voluntary use; they do not currently create legal obligations. The FCA consulted on UK Listing Rules amendments from 30 January to 20 March 2026 with final decisions expected in autumn 2026.

adoption.status: Partially incorporating ISSB Standards; target: adopting climate requirements in ISSB Standards
adoption.first_reporting_period: Group 1: periods commencing on or after 1 January 2025; Group 2: on or after 1 July 2026; Group 3: on or after 1 July 2027
adoption.note: Profile updated 12 June 2025. AASB S2 is mandatory and climate-focused (excluding industry-specific requirements); AASB S1 is voluntary and covers all sustainability topics. Applies to Chapter 2M entities meeting thresholds, with the revenue threshold falling from A$500m (Group 1) to A$50m (Group 3).

adoption.status: Adopting ISSB Standards with limited transition; target: fully adopting ISSB Standards
adoption.first_reporting_period: Annual reporting period ending March 2027 for Prime Market entities with market capitalisation of ¥3 trillion or more, phasing to a ¥500 billion threshold through 2029
adoption.note: Profile updated 16 July 2026. SSBJ Standards are designed to deliver outcomes functionally aligned with IFRS S1 and IFRS S2. Japan grants a two-year relief (one year longer than the ISSB transition relief) allowing sustainability disclosures to be reported after the financial statements on initial application.

adoption.status: Partially incorporating ISSB Standards and permitting the use of ISSB Standards; target: fully adopting ISSB Standards by 2028
adoption.first_reporting_period: Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions mandatory for financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2025; LargeCap issuers from 1 January 2026; HKFRS S1/S2 voluntary from 1 August 2025 and expected mandatory from 1 January 2028
adoption.note: Profile updated 12 June 2025. HKEX New Climate Requirements are based on IFRS S2 and apply on a comply-or-explain basis to Main Board issuers from 1 January 2025.

adoption.status: Partially incorporating ISSB Standards; target: full adoption contingent on SGX RegCo regulatory changes
adoption.first_reporting_period: STI constituent listed issuers: FY2025; other listed issuers: FY2028; large non-listed companies: FY2030
adoption.note: Profile updated 26 June 2026. Requirements draw on IFRS S2 and the climate-relevant provisions of IFRS S1. Transitional provisions allow up to five months beyond year-end for reports accompanied by assurance.

adoption.status: Permitting the use of ISSB Standards; target: fully adopting ISSB Standards
adoption.first_reporting_period: CVM-regulated listed entities: mandatory for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2026 (voluntary from 2024 using ISSB Standards, 2025 using CBPS); financial institutions: mandatory 1 January 2026 for segments 1-2 and 1 January 2028 for others
adoption.note: Profile updated 25 June 2026 and noted as under review following CVM Resolution 244 issued 29 May 2026. CBPS 01 and CBPS 02 correspond to IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 and apply to publicly held companies, investment funds and securitisation companies.

adoption.first_reporting_period: 1 January 2025 on a voluntary basis; no date for mandatory reporting established by securities authorities
adoption.note: Snapshot updated 12 June 2025. CSDS 1 and CSDS 2 are voluntary unless mandated by legislation or regulators. The Canadian Securities Administrators paused work on a mandatory climate disclosure rule in April 2025.

adoption.first_reporting_period: Voluntary; implementation scope and mandatory requirements still to be determined, with the full system targeted for 2030
adoption.note: Snapshot updated 18 June 2026. Chinese Sustainability Disclosure Standards for Business Enterprises comprise the Basic Standard (Trial), issued November 2024, and Climate Standard No. 1 (Trial), issued December 2025, led by the Ministry of Finance with nine other ministries, following a convergence approach with ISSB Standards.

adoption.status: Nearly 40 jurisdictions have taken steps to adopt or use ISSB Standards; requirements in 19 jurisdictions have already come into effect (IFRS Foundation, 24 February 2026)
adoption.note: The 'Use of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards by jurisdiction' page states 'Last updated 16 July 2026' and lists published jurisdictional profiles for 22 jurisdictions (Australia, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Ghana, Hong Kong SAR, Japan, Jordan, Kenya, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Philippines, Qatar, Rwanda, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Chinese Taipei, Tanzania, Türkiye, Zambia) with Oman and Zimbabwe marked forthcoming, plus snapshots for 13 jurisdictions (Bolivia, Canada, China, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, Panama, South Korea, Switzerland, Thailand, Uganda, United Kingdom). The page itself states no headline jurisdiction count; the counts here are a tally of the jurisdictions it lists.

glossary.Location-based method: Calculating electricity emissions using the average emissions intensity of the grid you physically draw power from.
glossary.Market-based method: Calculating electricity emissions using the contracts and certificates you have bought, rather than the grid average.
glossary.Hourly matching: Requiring that a clean electricity certificate be generated in the same hour that the electricity was consumed, rather than anywhere in the same year.
glossary.Deliverability: Requiring that the clean electricity you claim could physically have reached you on the grid, rather than coming from an unconnected region.
glossary.Consequential accounting: Estimating how much the world's emissions changed because you took an action, as opposed to measuring the emissions attributed to your own operations.
glossary.Multi-statement reporting: Publishing separate figures for your physical emissions, your contract-based emissions and the wider impact of your climate actions, instead of blending them into one number.
glossary.Physical inventory: The emissions actually released by your operations and value chain, before any certificates or contracts are applied.
glossary.Facilitated emissions: Emissions linked to transactions a financial institution enables for others, such as arranging a bond, rather than ones it finances directly.
glossary.Removals: Carbon dioxide taken out of the atmosphere and stored, whether in land, in products or in geological formations.
glossary.Standard Development Plan: GHG Protocol's published project plan for revising a standard, setting out scope, governance and indicative dates.
glossary.Independent Standards Board: The expert board that oversees GHG Protocol's development process and casts the votes that approve or reject final standards.
glossary.ISO stage code: A two-part number showing how far an ISO document has progressed, from 20.00 working draft through 40.20 enquiry ballot to 60.60 published.
glossary.Committee Draft: An ISO draft circulated for comment within the technical committee, one step before the wider enquiry ballot.
glossary.Draft International Standard: An ISO draft out for formal ballot and public comment across all member countries; the main opportunity for outside input.
glossary.Systematic review: ISO's routine five-year check on whether a published standard should be confirmed, revised or withdrawn.
glossary.ISO 14060 family: The traditional collective name for ISO's greenhouse gas standards (14064, 14065, 14066, 14067) - confusingly, ISO 14060 is now also the number of the new net zero alignment standard.
glossary.Energy attribute certificate: A tradeable document proving a unit of electricity was generated from a specified source, such as a REGO in the UK or a GO in the EU.
glossary.Carbon neutrality: A claim that residual emissions have been counterbalanced by offsetting after reductions, as specified by ISO 14068.
glossary.Category A company: Under Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0, a larger or higher-emitting company that faces the full requirement set, including scope 3 targets, mandatory limited assurance and a published transition plan.
glossary.Category B company: A company below the Category A thresholds, which must set scope 1 and scope 2 targets but for which scope 3 target-setting and third-party assurance are optional.
glossary.Significance-based scope 3 boundary: The V2.0 rule that a scope 3 category needs a target if it represents at least 5% of the company's categories 1-14 emissions, replacing the old fixed coverage percentage.
glossary.Emissions-intensive activity (EIA): A business activity that Category A companies must identify and quantify, and report where it accounts for at least 5% of scope 3 emissions.
glossary.Implementation hierarchy: The V2.0 ordering that requires direct activity-level emissions reductions before actions in shared activity pools or at sector level, which are allowed only where structural constraints exist.
glossary.Ongoing emissions responsibility (OER): The V2.0 framework covering how companies address emissions they are still releasing before their net-zero year, including voluntary contributions and, for Category A companies, mandatory removals from 2035.
glossary.Neutralisation: Counterbalancing residual emissions at and after the net-zero target year using carbon removals that meet SBTi durability and integrity criteria.
glossary.Beyond value chain mitigation (BVCM): Climate action a company funds outside its own value chain, which SBTi recognises but does not allow to substitute for reductions against targets.
glossary.Absolute Contraction Approach (ACA): The target-setting method that applies a linear annual percentage reduction to absolute emissions, revised in April 2026 and retaining a 4.2% minimum annual floor.
glossary.Low-carbon electricity alignment target: A scope 2 target expressed as an increasing share of low-carbon electricity used, contracted or matched, as an alternative to an emissions reduction target.
glossary.Near, new, now: SBTi's shorthand for the three eligibility tests on market instruments used for scope 2 implementation: same synchronous grid, generator generally under 15 years old, and annual temporal matching.
glossary.End-of-cycle assessment: A new V2.0 requirement to evaluate and report target progress at the close of each five-year target cycle, assured by a third party for Category A companies.
glossary.Target base year: Under V2.0, the most recent year for which comprehensive emissions and other applicable data are available, replacing a freely chosen historical base year.
glossary.Mandatory five-year review: The obligation on companies with validated targets to reassess them five years after their most recent validation publication, with six months to file the review form and up to twelve months to resubmit.
glossary.Best efforts basis: V2.0's framing that targets are pursued on a best-efforts basis with disclosed assumptions and dependencies, acknowledging factors outside a company's control.
glossary.Fossil Fuel Policy: The SBTi policy, referenced directly in V2.0's scope section, that restricts commitments and validations from companies directly involved in fossil fuel exploration, extraction, mining or production.
glossary.Global baseline: The IFRS Foundation's term for a common minimum set of investor-focused sustainability disclosures that jurisdictions can build on but should not contradict.
glossary.IFRS Practice Statement: A document developed under the same due process as a Standard but which companies may choose to apply rather than being required to, unless a jurisdiction mandates it.
glossary.Exposure Draft: A formal public consultation document setting out proposed new or amended requirements, open for comment for a fixed period before the board redeliberates.
glossary.Financed emissions: The greenhouse gas emissions attributable to a financial institution's lending and investment activities, a subset of Scope 3 Category 15.
glossary.Scope 3 Category 15: The GHG Protocol category covering emissions associated with an entity's investments, including financed emissions and, before the 2025 amendments, other financial activities such as derivatives.
glossary.Transition relief: A time-limited concession letting an entity omit or simplify a disclosure in the first period or periods it applies a standard.
glossary.Climate-first relief: A transitional concession letting a company report only climate matters in its first year or two, deferring wider sustainability topics.
glossary.Jurisdictional profile: An IFRS Foundation document describing a jurisdiction's approach to using ISSB Standards, prepared once that approach is finalised and no longer subject to consultation.
glossary.Jurisdictional snapshot: A shorter IFRS Foundation overview for a jurisdiction whose approach to ISSB Standards is still being developed or consulted on.
glossary.Global warming potential: A conversion factor used to express emissions of different greenhouse gases as a carbon dioxide equivalent, published in IPCC Assessment Reports.
glossary.Industry-based guidance: Non-mandatory ISSB material, derived from the SASB Standards, that entities must refer to and consider the applicability of when identifying climate-related disclosures under IFRS S2.
glossary.Due process: The IFRS Foundation's mandatory procedural steps — consultation, deliberation in public, effects analysis and balloting — that a proposal must pass before publication.
glossary.CSRD: The EU directive that requires large companies to publish an audited sustainability statement inside their management report.
glossary.ESRS: The detailed EU reporting standards that tell a company exactly what sustainability information to disclose and how.
glossary.Omnibus I: The 2025-2026 EU simplification package that cut the number of companies in sustainability reporting scope and thinned the rules.
glossary.Stop-the-clock: The April 2025 directive that simply pushed back application dates while the substantive rewrite was negotiated.
glossary.Value chain cap: A legal ceiling on how much sustainability data a big reporting company can demand from a smaller supplier for CSRD purposes.
glossary.Protected undertaking: A company in someone's value chain with 1,000 or fewer employees, which can lawfully refuse data requests beyond the cap.
glossary.VSME: A short voluntary sustainability reporting standard designed for smaller companies answering questions from banks and big customers.
glossary.Double materiality: Assessing both how sustainability issues affect the company financially and how the company affects people and the environment.
glossary.Limited assurance: A lower-cost audit-style check where the assurer says nothing came to their attention suggesting the numbers are wrong.
glossary.Reasonable assurance: A full audit-strength check where the assurer gives a positive opinion that the information is fairly stated.
glossary.Wave one: The first group of companies that had to report under CSRD, covering financial year 2024.
glossary.CBAM: A carbon price charged on imports of certain carbon-intensive goods so they face costs comparable to EU producers.
glossary.Authorised CBAM declarant: The registered status an importer needs before it can legally import CBAM goods above the exemption threshold.
glossary.De minimis threshold: The 50-tonne annual import volume below which a company has no CBAM obligations at all.
glossary.EU Taxonomy: A classification system that defines which economic activities count as environmentally sustainable, with mandatory KPI disclosure.
glossary.CSDDD: The EU directive requiring the very largest companies to identify and address human rights and environmental harms in their operations.
glossary.Delegated act: Secondary EU legislation adopted by the Commission that fills in technical detail, subject to a Parliament and Council veto window.
glossary.Scrutiny period: The window in which the European Parliament or Council can object to a delegated act before it can enter into force.
glossary.ESRS-40a: The separate, lighter EU reporting standard being developed for non-EU parent companies with large EU turnover.
glossary.Transposition: The process by which each EU country writes a directive into its own national law by a set deadline.
glossary.SB 253: California's Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act, which makes large companies doing business in California publish their greenhouse gas emissions.
glossary.SB 261: California's climate-related financial risk law, which makes mid-size and larger companies doing business in California publish a report on the climate risks to their business.
glossary.SB 219: The 2024 California law that amended SB 253 and SB 261, including shifting CARB's regulation-making deadline and allowing parent-level consolidated reporting.
glossary.Doing business in California: A tax-law test met if a company is organised or commercially domiciled in California, or its California sales exceed an indexed dollar threshold or 25 per cent of its total sales.
glossary.Gross receipts: The California tax definition of revenue used for the SB 253 and SB 261 thresholds - total amounts taken in before deducting the cost of goods sold.
glossary.Reporting entity: The CARB term for a company caught by SB 253's $1 billion revenue threshold.
glossary.Covered entity: The CARB term for a company caught by SB 261's $500 million revenue threshold.
glossary.Scope 1 emissions: Greenhouse gases released directly by things the company owns or controls, such as its boilers and vehicles.
glossary.Scope 2 emissions: Greenhouse gases released by the power stations that generate the electricity, heat or steam the company buys.
glossary.Scope 3 emissions: Greenhouse gases released across the company's value chain — suppliers, transport, product use and disposal — which it does not own or control.
glossary.Injunction pending appeal: A court order pausing a law's enforcement while an appeal is decided, without deciding whether the law is ultimately valid.
glossary.Held in abeyance: A court putting a case on hold without deciding it, usually to wait for the agency involved to act.
glossary.Office of Administrative Law: The California body that reviews an agency's final regulation for legal sufficiency before it can be filed and take effect.
glossary.Enforcement discretion: A regulator publicly choosing not to penalise non-compliance in specified circumstances, without changing the underlying legal duty.
glossary.Compelled speech: The First Amendment argument that a government cannot force a private party to make statements it does not wish to make.
glossary.UK SRS: The UK's own versions of the ISSB sustainability standards, published in February 2026 and currently voluntary.
glossary.Comply or explain: A rule you must either follow or publicly justify not following, rather than one you must simply obey.
glossary.Intensity ratio: Emissions expressed per unit of something meaningful, such as tonnes of CO2e per million pounds of turnover, so figures can be compared across years and companies.
glossary.Transition plan: A published account of how a company intends to adapt its business towards a low-carbon economy, including targets and the actions behind them.
glossary.Modified liability: A temporary Australian arrangement limiting legal exposure for certain forward-looking climate disclosures during the first years of mandatory reporting.
glossary.Publicly accountable entity: A listed company or a business that holds assets in a fiduciary capacity for outsiders, such as a bank, insurer or pension fund.
glossary.Directors' report: The part of a UK annual report where SECR energy and carbon figures must sit.
glossary.Strategic report: The narrative part of a UK annual report where the mandatory climate-related financial disclosures must sit.
glossary.Group 1, 2 and 3: Australia's three waves of mandatory climate reporters, defined by size and phased in from 2025, 2026 and 2027 respectively.

coverage_notes.ghgp-iso: Checked and verified against official sources only: ghgprotocol.org (standards pages, public consultations page, news index pages 1-2, Consolidated Standard Development Plan v2.0 of 29 July 2026, Scope 3 Phase 1 Progress Update of 31 March 2026, AMI Phase 1 White Paper and explanatory memo, LSR Standard and Guidance pages, Forest Carbon Accounting RFI, ISB and CEO announcements) and iso.org / committee.iso.org (catalogue records for ISO 14064-1:2018, ISO/WD 14064-1.2, ISO 14064-2:2019, ISO/WD 14064-2.2, ISO 14064-3:2019, ISO/TS 14064-4:2025, ISO 14064-5:2026, ISO 14067:2018, ISO 14068-1:2023, ISO 14068, ISO/DIS 14060; the ISO/TC 207/SC 7 projects and under-development listings; ISO news releases of 9 September 2025, 26 February 2026 and 17 June 2026). No third-party tracker, consultancy, law-firm, vendor or news source was used or cited. COULD NOT VERIFY: (1) an exact closing date for the ISO/DIS 14060 enquiry ballot - ISO's news release states only 'early September 2026' for the 12-week window opened on 17 June 2026, so the September 2026 date here is derived from that stated duration; (2) any GHG Protocol revision workstream for the Project Protocol - it appears on ghgprotocol.org/standards as a current publication but no Standard Development Plan, draft or consultation exists for it, so its 'scoping' phase here is inferred from absence rather than from a positive official statement; (3) any published target date, draft or consultation for the joint ISO-GHGP product-level standard beyond the formation of the Joint Working Group; (4) reconciliation between the Q2 2027 consolidated consultation date and the Q3 2027 AMI draft consultation date, both of which appear on official pages without explanation of the gap; (5) the status of ISO 14064-1:2018/DAmd 1 - it is listed on the ISO/TC 207/SC 7 projects page but its catalogue record at iso.org/standard/88065.html returned HTTP 404, so no claim about that amendment is made here. UNREACHABLE PAGES: https://ghgprotocol.org/standards-development returned HTTP 404; https://www.iso.org/committee/546319.html returned HTTP 404; https://www.iso.org/standard/88065.html returned HTTP 404. meta.title: EcoLedger Standards Tracker
meta.sourcing_policy: Every entry is verified against, and links to, the standard-setter or regulator’s own publication. No third-party trackers, consultancy notes or news reports are used as sources of record.
meta.disclaimer: Indicative guide, not legal, accounting or assurance advice. Confirm your obligations against the primary sources linked on every entry before relying on them.

matrix.label: GHGP Scope 3
matrix.note: A prescriptive 95 percent boundary would force you to quantify total scope 3 before you can justify any exclusion, which is a screening exercise most teams have never actually done.
matrix.why: The proposals are set out in an official GHG Protocol progress update, but the document itself states that all revisions remain under development and subject to change, so the 95 percent threshold and Category 16 could both be dropped before consultation.

matrix.label: GHGP Land & Removals
matrix.note: Effective 1 January 2027 and final, it adds land-sector and removals data points that no existing inventory process collects, for anyone with agricultural, forestry or timber inputs.
matrix.why: Both the Standard and the Guidance are published final documents on ghgprotocol.org with a stated effective date of 1 January 2027.

matrix.label: ISO 14060 Net Zero
matrix.note: It turns a transition plan into something independently verifiable, so the work is comment drafting now and, later, evidencing a plan you may currently publish unaudited.
matrix.why: The DIS stage, ballot launch date and 12-week duration are confirmed on ISO's own catalogue record and news release, but ISO's news item gives the closing date only as 'early September 2026' rather than a precise date.

matrix.label: SBTi V2.0
matrix.note: With 42 percent of sections new and no criterion-by-criterion mapping from V1.3.1, a validated company faces a full target rebuild, fresh modelling and board re-approval rather than a renewal.
matrix.why: Read directly from the published V2.0 standard, its Criteria document and the official Main Changes Document dated June 2026 on files.sciencebasedtargets.org.

matrix.label: SBTi Scope 3 test
matrix.note: The 5 percent significance test per category replaces the coverage percentage, so categories you legitimately excluded under V1 may become mandatory and need data sourced from scratch.
matrix.why: Every point is set out in the published V2.0 Main Changes Document and the V2.0 Criteria document.

matrix.label: IFRS S2 GHG amends
matrix.note: The four reliefs, especially the Category 15 relief, cut financial-sector scope, so the work is an early-adoption decision for FY2026 and documenting which reliefs you take.
matrix.why: Final amendments were published by the ISSB on 11 December 2025 with the effective date and each relief set out in the IFRS Foundation's own announcement and completed-project page.

matrix.label: ISSB Nature
matrix.note: A Practice Statement supplementing S1 rather than a new standard, so existing TNFD work gets mapped across instead of a new disclosure programme being built.
matrix.why: The Practice Statement form, 120-day comment period and October 2026 target are formal ISSB decisions recorded in ISSB Updates, but the Exposure Draft itself has not yet been published.

matrix.label: CSRD post-Omnibus
matrix.note: A confirmed FY2027 start with a hard two-limb scope test: in scope means a full double materiality assessment, ESRS datapoints and limited assurance; out of scope means dismantling a programme already part-built.
matrix.why: Published in the Official Journal as Directive (EU) 2026/470 on 26 February 2026 and in force since 18 March 2026; thresholds quoted from the amended Article 19a(1)/29a(1) text on EUR-Lex.

matrix.label: Revised ESRS
matrix.note: Mandatory datapoints fall by over 60 percent, which still means rebuilding the datapoint inventory, remapping every data owner and deciding on early application for FY2026.
matrix.why: Formally adopted by the Commission on 3 July 2026 and published on ec.europa.eu, but not yet in the Official Journal and still capable of objection during Parliament/Council scrutiny, so it is not rated confirmed.

matrix.label: Sector ESRS dropped
matrix.note: The mandate is deleted, so any sector-ESRS readiness project can be closed and its budget released.
matrix.why: The deletion of the Article 29b(1) subparagraphs appears in the adopted text of Directive (EU) 2026/470 published in the Official Journal.

matrix.label: VSME value-chain cap
matrix.note: Supplier questionnaires have to be rewritten to the necessary-information set and a statutory right-to-decline notice added, which touches procurement systems and every live supplier data request.
matrix.why: The Article 29ca empowerment is confirmed in Directive (EU) 2026/470, but the implementing delegated act adopted 3 July 2026 is still in Parliament/Council scrutiny and not yet in the Official Journal.

matrix.label: CBAM definitive
matrix.note: Importers over 50 tonnes need authorised declarant status, embedded-emissions data from suppliers and a certificate purchasing process before the September 2027 surrender deadline.
matrix.why: All figures and dates were read from the Official Journal text of Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 and confirmed on the Commission's taxation and customs pages.

matrix.label: CA SB 253
matrix.note: A first mandatory Scope 1 and 2 submission to CARB with entity-level boundary and consolidation decisions signed off, and Scope 3 following, for companies with no prior US filing obligation.
matrix.why: The statute is in force and the regulation was Board-approved, but the exact 2026 deadline is not yet finally adopted (the OAL package was withdrawn on/after 20 May 2026) and the Ninth Circuit's pending merits decision in Chamber of Commerce v. Sanchez could still strike the law down.

matrix.label: CA SB 261
matrix.note: The report itself is a full TCFD- or IFRS S2-aligned climate risk assessment that must sit publication-ready while the injunction holds and the deadline is reset at short notice.
matrix.why: The statute is in force but a Ninth Circuit injunction pending appeal currently bars enforcement and the merits ruling could either restore or invalidate the obligation, so the outcome is genuinely open.

matrix.label: SEC climate rules
matrix.note: Rescission means stopping work: cancel SEC climate line-item provisioning and keep only materiality-based risk factors you already produce.
matrix.why: The stay and the proposing release are formal Commission actions on the record, but the rescission is only proposed and a final adopting release remains outstanding.

matrix.label: EPA GHGRP repeal
matrix.note: Many US Scope 1 baselines are built on GHGRP facility data; if the programme is repealed that source disappears and facility-level measurement has to be replaced internally.
matrix.why: The deadline extension is a final published rule, while the wider repeal is proposed with a final action still outstanding.

matrix.label: FCA CP26/5
matrix.note: Listed issuers move from TCFD comply-or-explain to mandatory UK SRS S2 for FY2027, which requires scenario analysis and a Scope 3 inventory many issuers have never assured.
matrix.why: CP26/5 is published and closed, but the proposals are not yet rules — the policy statement is still outstanding as at 25 August 2026.

matrix.label: UK transition plans
matrix.note: Both consultation routes end with a published Paris-aligned transition plan, which means capex alignment, sectoral decarbonisation levers and board sign-off rather than a disclosure exercise.
matrix.why: The consultation page still states the government is analysing feedback, so scope, route and timing all remain genuinely open.

matrix_method: Effort scores are EcoLedger's own editorial judgement, not a figure published by any standard-setter, regulator or source we cite. We scored each workstream on the work it would create for a typical mid-sized corporate reporting team - roughly 500 to 5,000 employees, reporting in more than one jurisdiction, with a small sustainability team working alongside finance - asking what new data, systems, contracts or sign-off it actually forces, and deliberately scoring low where a change is voluntary, superseded or simply lets you stop doing something. Plotted against how settled each change is, the scores are a triage aid rather than a budgeting input, and your own score will differ wherever your footprint does.
matrix_x_rule: Horizontal position combines two fields already in the dataset: the confidence rating (confirmed 88, high 68, medium 45, low 22) adjusted by how far through its process the workstream is (in force +7, final +4, adopted but not in force +2, draft −3, consultation −6, drafting −8, scoping −12, in litigation −10). It is a presentation of the ratings, not a separate judgement.

verification.note: Every forward-looking date, scope test and high-significance update in this tracker was re-checked against the regulator's or standard-setter's own page by a second, independent pass. Dates that no official source actually publishes have been removed rather than shown as deadlines. Where two official pages disagreed, the more recent one was taken and the item marked projected.
verification.known_limits: Two statutory sources block automated access and could not be read directly: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (SB 253/261 statutory text) and legislation.gov.uk (SECR regulations). Both rest on the regulator's own restatement instead, which is noted on the affected entries.
